levels.MUST: A release blocker for a new app.
levels.SHOULD: Expected unless the app has a stated reason.
levels.MAY: A pattern worth copying when the app grows into it.

checks.code: Verify by reading or searching the app's source, as the check says.
checks.test: The statement requires a test; confirm the app has it, or its equivalent, and that it runs in the build.
checks.by hand: Needs a person, in the running app or where the check sends them (the repository's pull requests): the source alone can't confirm it, though it can show the rule unmet.

statuses.fail: Not met, and pauta.json records no exception for it. A finding; a failed MUST blocks a release.
statuses.manual: Checked by hand: the source leaves it open, so a person checks it, in the running app or where the Check sends them (the repository's pull requests), and may record a rule found met in pauta.json's `checked` list. Not a finding, recorded or not: the result carries the entry, or its evidence ends "not recorded".
statuses.not-checked: The Check needs something the audit could not read: another repository (the website's), what the repository's host keeps and no file shows (a repository setting, an issue's state), or the rules of the edition the app names, in an audit run against another (ABOUT-07). Not a finding and not a pass; the evidence says what would settle it.
statuses.pending: Not met; pauta.json records it as pending, with an issue.
statuses.deviation: A SHOULD the app does differently on purpose; pauta.json records it, with a decision record.
statuses.not-applicable: The rule reads as applying to every app, but its subject does not exist in this one; pauta.json records it.
statuses.app-only: A template only: the rule needs what each app made from it has of its own; pauta.json records it.
statuses.limited: The rule covers only apps with a feature this one lacks (its text, its page's or section's appliesTo, or the rule it details says so). Needs no exception.

rules.text: Every command, setting and window exists on Windows, macOS and Linux, with the same default. Where the OS can't do what one asks, it stays where it is, disabled, and says why; it is never hidden. The only exceptions are the rows of the table under [Where the OS's way wins](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/same-on-every-os/#where-the-oss-way-wins), on the page Same on every OS: the places where the app hands work to the OS or sits in the OS's own interface, such as the macOS application menu and the macOS form of a keymap's chords.
rules.why: a user who moves to another OS looks for a feature where they left it. A missing row looks like a different app; a disabled one with a reason explains itself.

check.text: no command, menu row or settings row is registered or added inside an OS check, and no default in the settings model depends on the OS, unless a row of the table under [Where the OS's way wins](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/same-on-every-os/#where-the-oss-way-wins) gives that difference: the rows of the macOS application menu, a default chord in its macOS form. An OS check is a test whose answer can differ among Windows, macOS and Linux; a gate that holds on all three alike (a command registered only when the app finds its own launcher, whatever the OS) is not one. A row the OS can't serve calls `setDisable` and carries its reason ([KBD-04](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/keyboard/#kbd-04) for a command).

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/SettingsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsWindow.java) (the extended-window row, disabled on macOS "rather than hidden, so its note still explains why"). Editora doesn't hold the rule everywhere yet: its `file.saveAsAdmin` command ([`ui/WindowCommandRegistrar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowCommandRegistrar.java)) is registered with nothing that disables it on Windows, where it can do nothing. Termina removes its `hideMenuBar` command on macOS ([`ui/TerminalWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalWindow.java)).

rules.text: In an app's code, one class answers which OS the app runs on (this guide calls it `Os`, with `isWindows()`, `isMac()` and `isLinux()`; the names are the app's own), and no other class reads the `os.name` property. A class that only shows the OS's name, in About or a problem report, asks that one class for it.
rules.why: checks scattered through the code are how apps drift apart on one OS without anyone choosing it. In one class, every difference can be found with one search, and a test can run the app as any OS ([OS-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/same-on-every-os/#os-03)).

check.text: `grep -rl '"os.name"' src/main/java` lists one file, the `Os` class, and no other file works out the OS for itself. The Command also lists the files that compare `File.separatorChar` or `File.pathSeparatorChar` with a character (`File.separatorChar == '\\'` for "is this Windows"), the other way Editora does it. A class that only prints the name, in About or a problem report, reads the property too, so it is listed. A grep finds only the spellings it is given: when the Command passes, still read for a test that stands in for the OS some other way, such as a separator compared as a string or an environment variable only one OS sets.
check.command: [ -f pom.xml ] || { echo 'not an app root: no pom.xml here'; exit 1; }; n=$(grep -rl '"os.name"' src/main/java | wc -l); s=$(grep -rlE "eparatorChar *[!=]= *'" src/main/java | wc -l); u=$(grep -rlE "\"os[.]name\"|eparatorChar *[!=]= *'" src/main/java | wc -l); [ "$n" -eq 1 ] && [ "$u" -eq 1 ] || { echo "$n files read os.name (one Os class should):"; grep -rl '"os.name"' src/main/java; echo "$s files compare a file or path separator with a character (only that class may):"; grep -rlE "eparatorChar *[!=]= *'" src/main/java; false; }

rules.reference: the app template's [`Os.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/Os.java), the one class that reads `os.name` (`current`, `isWindows`, `isMac`, `isLinux`, and `description` for About and a problem report); the Command passes on it. Each of the six apps reads `os.name` in several classes, Editora in about fifty, and eleven of Editora's classes tell Windows apart by a separator, eight of them without reading `os.name` ([`lsp/JavaRuntimes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/lsp/JavaRuntimes.java), [`dap/DapManager.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/dap/DapManager.java), [`dap/InstalledAdapter.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/dap/InstalledAdapter.java)). Editora's [`process/DesktopActions.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/process/DesktopActions.java) has the `Os` enum to start from.

rules.text: An app's tests can run as any OS: the one class that answers which OS the app runs on ([OS-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/same-on-every-os/#os-02); this guide calls it `Os`) takes an override, and one test asserts that the command ids, the menu bar's rows and the settings pages are the same for Windows, macOS and Linux.
rules.why: CI runs the FX tests on one or two OSes ([REL-20](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/release/#rel-20)); with the override, the comparison runs on every pull request on Linux alone.

check.text: a test sets each OS in turn through the override and compares the three lists.

rules.reference: the app template's [`Os.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/Os.java) (`override`, and the `exampleapp.os` property) and [`SameOnEveryOsFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/SameOnEveryOsFxTest.java) (`theCommandsTheMenusAndSettingsAreTheSameOnEveryOs`), which starts the app as each OS and compares the command ids, the menu bar's rows and every Settings page's rows. Editora's [`KeymapsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/command/KeymapsTest.java) (`guiKeymapsBindSameCommandSetOnBothPlatforms`) does it for the keymaps.

rules.text: No behavior or layout of an app differs by OS: what a command, a key or a click does, where a control sits and how a window is drawn are the same on Windows, macOS and Linux. The only exceptions are the rows of the table under [Where the OS's way wins](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/same-on-every-os/#where-the-oss-way-wins), on the page Same on every OS: the places where the app hands work to the OS or sits in the OS's own interface, such as the macOS form of a keymap's chords, the system menu bar, the OS's file dialogs, trash, tray and notifications, and the shells a terminal offers. Whether a command, setting or window exists, and its default, is [OS-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/same-on-every-os/#os-01).
rules.why: a feature can be on every OS and still act or sit differently on one: Escape that closes the window on Linux only, a title on the left on Windows only. Each is something to relearn on the next machine, which is what the family exists to spare its users.

check.text: list every place the code tests the OS. They are the callers of the methods of the class [OS-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/same-on-every-os/#os-02) asks for and, in an app that has no such class yet, every file OS-02's Command prints (the files that read `os.name`, and the files that compare `File.separatorChar` or `File.pathSeparatorChar` with a character), together with the callers of whatever those files offer other classes to ask the OS by: a method (Editora's `KeymapManager.isMac()`, which ten files call and eight of them read no `os.name` themselves) or a constant. `grep -rnE 'isMac|isWindows|isLinux' src/main/java` lists the usual names; read the printed files for the app's own. Read each place. It passes when what it changes is what a row of the table under [Where the OS's way wins](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/same-on-every-os/#where-the-oss-way-wins) gives that OS, or is nothing a user can see or do (the path of a binary, a process's arguments, a line ending). It fails when it changes anything else a user can see or do: what a command, a key or a click does, where something sits, how it is drawn or what it says. A place that gives an OS something other than what its row gives is judged by the rule that row links, where that rule covers it: a Windows notification raised as the tray's balloon and not a toast fails [TRAY-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/tray-and-background/#tray-09), not this rule. It fails this rule when the row links no rule, or the rule it links does not cover the difference (a menu bar on one OS and a menu button on the others).

rules.reference: the app template, read through: every place it tests the OS calls its [`Os.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/Os.java), and each is on a row or changes nothing a user sees: the macOS form of the keymap's chords (`Keymap`, `KeyDispatcher`, `AppServices`, and the pickers' keys that `MainWindow` hands `PickerKeys`), the system menu bar and its application menu (`MainWindow`, `Chrome`, `MacAppMenu`), and a program's path, arguments and `PATH` (`Executables`, `Browser`, `ShellPath`). No other app has been read through for it yet. The differences found so far, each on no row or short of its row: Mirada closes its window on Escape on Linux only ([`Command.escapeCloses`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Command.java)), follows the OS's accent color on macOS and Windows only ([`Theme.followsAccent`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Theme.java)), puts its title on the left on Windows only ([`TitleBar.Layout`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/TitleBar.java)) and has a menu bar on macOS only ([`ui/MacMenus.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/MacMenus.java)); Editora deletes a file for good on Windows ([`io/Trash.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/io/Trash.java)), keeps the user's key bindings apart by OS (`keybindings` and `keybindingsMac` in [`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/Settings.java)) and registers its WSL targets on Windows only ([`App`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java)); Termina believes the folder a shell reports for itself on Windows only ([`ProcessCwd.reportedDirectoryWins`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/pty/ProcessCwd.java)), and its Settings Sync keeps the user's key bindings in one file for macOS and another for Windows and Linux ([`sync/KeybindingsFile.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/sync/KeybindingsFile.java)). On a row, and passing: a click that takes `Cmd` on macOS and `Ctrl` elsewhere (Editora's [`editor/EditorBuffer.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/EditorBuffer.java), Termina's [`link/LinkGesture.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/link/LinkGesture.java)), and the profiles Termina lists on Windows only, Command Prompt, PowerShell, Git Bash and the WSL distributions ([`shell/ShellDiscovery.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/shell/ShellDiscovery.java)).

rules.text: Every app implements Pauta: it names one edition (the `pauta.version` of [ABOUT-08](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/about/#about-08)) and states its conformance as [Complete, Core or Partial](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#complete-core-and-partial): Complete meets every MUST and every SHOULD (met, not applicable or a recorded deviation), Core every MUST with SHOULDs still pending, Partial not yet every MUST.
rules.why: an app that is in the family answers to these rules; saying which ones, and how far, is the first of them.

check.text: `pom.xml` defines `pauta.version` and `src/main/resources/com/<app>/pauta.json` exists.
check.command: [ -f pom.xml ] || { echo 'not an app root: no pom.xml here'; exit 1; }; { grep -q '<pauta.version>' pom.xml || { echo 'no pauta.version in pom.xml'; false; }; } && { find src/main/resources -path '*/com/*' -name pauta.json | grep . || { echo 'no pauta.json'; false; }; }

rules.reference: The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/pom.xml) (`pauta.version`) and [`pauta.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/pauta.json).

rules.text: An app's conformance is computed, never stored: one pure helper reads the exceptions and returns Partial when any MUST is pending, Core when any SHOULD is pending, and Complete otherwise. Nothing else enters it: the `checked` list ([PAUTA-18](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#pauta-18)) is a record, and a by-hand rule with no entry there leaves the result as it is. About, the Pauta window and the docs page take it from there; the README's badge and line ([PAUTA-15](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#pauta-15)), which can't call the helper, are held to it by a test.
rules.why: [*One source of truth for each fact*](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/principles/#for-the-people-building-them). A conformance typed in by hand stays "Complete" after a pending exception is added.

check.text: one helper returns the conformance (the template's `PautaConformance.of`): it is handed the exceptions and nothing of the `checked` list, returns Partial for a pending MUST, Core for a pending SHOULD and Complete otherwise, and deviation, not-applicable and app-only entries leave its result alone. About and the Pauta window call it, and nothing in the app's code stores a conformance. A test fails when the README's badge or line names another conformance than the helper returns: the statement requires that one. A unit test of the helper that covers all three results is the surest evidence for the rest. That the docs page shows the same conformance is read with the page itself, in the website's repository ([PAUTA-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#pauta-13)).

rules.reference: The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`PautaConformance.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/PautaConformance.java) (`of`, which takes the exceptions alone, and `conformance`), tested by [`PautaConformanceTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/PautaConformanceTest.java), whose `theReadmeNamesTheEditionAndTheConformanceAndLinksTheDocsPage` holds the README and whose `deviationsAppOnlyAndNotApplicableEntriesAndMaysLeaveTheConformanceAlone` covers the entries that leave it alone.

rules.text: A new app, one that has made no release yet, makes its first release at Core or Complete: the [New app checklist](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/checklist/)'s MUSTs are release blockers, and recording one as pending does not lift that. An app with a release behind it is not covered: it may be at Partial, and says so ([Complete, Core and Partial](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#complete-core-and-partial)). A template repository is never released as an app, so this rule is for the app made from it and the template records no entry for it.

check.text: in an app with no release yet (no numbered section in its `CHANGELOG.md`, no version tag), the About window of the build to be released says Core or Complete. An app that has released, and a template, are outside the rule.

rules.reference: no app yet.

rules.text: Every MUST and SHOULD of the edition that the app does not meet has an exception, and every exception names a rule the app does not meet. An unmet rule with no entry is a failed audit, not an exception; an entry for a rule the app now meets is removed in the same change that meets it. A rule checked by hand counts like any other once a person has checked it in the running app: found unmet, it gets an exception; found met, a `checked` entry ([PAUTA-18](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#pauta-18)). Until then it has neither, and that is not a failed audit: the audit reports it as `manual`, not recorded.
rules.why: [*Never claim what is not true*](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/principles/#for-the-people-using-the-apps). The list is the app's claim; it has to be whole and current.

check.text: the audit of the app against its edition ([Coding agents and LLMs](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/coding-agents/#audit-an-app)) is this check, so the audit judges this rule last, from its other results: no MUST or SHOULD is `fail`, and no result reports an entry for a rule that passes. The evidence names the rules that fail. A `manual` result with no `checked` entry is reported as not recorded (PAUTA-18), and a `not-checked` one as out of the audit's reach: neither is a failure of the app, and neither fails this check. An audit of part of the edition judges it from the rules in its scope and says so.

rules.reference: The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`pauta.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/pauta.json), the only list of exceptions so far, beside the audit report that shows it whole: [`docs/pauta-audit.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/docs/pauta-audit.json) and [`docs/pauta-audit.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/docs/pauta-audit.md), where no MUST or SHOULD fails and its nine `app-only` entries are the only exceptions.

rules.text: A rule limited to apps with a feature needs no entry in an app without that feature. A rule is limited when its own text says so ("An app that stores a secret…"), when its page or section opens with an **Applies to** line (the [Tray and background](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/tray-and-background/) page; `appliesTo` in `rules.json`), or when it details a rule that is limited (WELC-03 onward detail the Welcome page of [WELC-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/welcome/#welc-01)). Nothing else limits a rule: a scope is read from one of the three, never inferred from what the app lacks. `not-applicable` is for a rule that reads as applying to every app.

check.text: no `not-applicable` entry names a rule whose text, page, section or parent rule already limits it.

rules.reference: the [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`pauta.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/pauta.json) has no `not-applicable` entry, so it meets the rule with nothing to hold; the six apps have no `pauta.json`.

rules.text: A `deviation` is a choice, not a gap, and only a SHOULD can have one: a SHOULD is expected unless the app has a stated reason, and the deviation is that reason. It links a decision record in `docs/decisions/` ([DOCS-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/documentation/#docs-13)) that gives the context, what the app does instead, and what it costs. A MUST the app does not meet is `pending`, as is any work it has not done yet.
rules.why: a deviation keeps the conformance; a deviation from a MUST, or missing work called a deviation, would let the app say it is built to an edition it does not meet.

check.text: every `deviation` entry names a SHOULD, and its `link` opens a file under `docs/decisions/` that names the rule's ID.

rules.reference: The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`PautaConformanceTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/PautaConformanceTest.java) (`eachKindHasWhatItNeeds`).

rules.text: A `pending` exception links an open issue in the app's own repository that names the rule's ID and edition, "MENU-14 (Pauta x.y.z)". One issue may hold several rules, one per page for example, if it names each one that way. Closing the issue removes its entries.

check.text: every `pending` entry's `link` is an issue URL in the app's own repository; the source settles that much, and a link that is not one fails the rule. That the issue is open and names the entry's rule ID and edition is read from the issue itself (`gh issue view <number>`), which is on GitHub and not in the checkout. An audit that cannot read the issues reports the rule as `not-checked` and says what would settle it. With no `pending` entry there is nothing to read, and the rule is met.

rules.reference: The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`PautaConformanceTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/PautaConformanceTest.java) (`eachKindHasWhatItNeeds`), which fails a pending link that is not an issue in the app's repository or the template's. The template has no `pending` entry left, so it meets the rule with nothing to read.

rules.text: Each exception's `reason` is one plain sentence for the person using the app, in English like the changelog: what is different and, for a deviation, what they get instead. No rule text, no class names.

check.text: read each reason in the Pauta window as a user would. The source settles two cases: a reason that runs to more than one sentence, or carries rule text or a class name, fails the rule, and with no exception there is no reason to read and the rule is met.

rules.reference: The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`PautaConformanceTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/PautaConformanceTest.java) (`eachKindHasWhatItNeeds`: a reason ends with a period and names no rule ID).

rules.text: A template repository, one that new apps are made from, sets `"template": true` in its `pauta.json` and records as `app-only` the rules that only an app made from it can meet. `app-only` leaves the conformance as it is, like `not-applicable`, and nothing but a template may use it. Making an app from the template sets `template` to `false`. From then on the app's everyday build passes but lists what it inherited: each `app-only` entry and each `pending` link to another repository. Its release build fails until each one is met, or recorded as `pending` with an issue in the app's own repository. An app that was not made from a template inherits nothing, and the rule asks nothing of it.
rules.why: a template can't have the website or screenshots of an app that doesn't exist yet, and an app must not inherit its template's issues as its own. A build that failed the moment the app was made would fail its first step; the release is where it has to be settled ([PAUTA-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#pauta-03)).

check.text: in a template, `pauta.json` has `"template": true` and the script that makes an app from it sets it to `false`. Outside a template, an `app-only` entry or a `pending` link to another repository is what a template left behind: the test of [PAUTA-10](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#pauta-10) lists each one in the everyday build, and the release build runs it with them treated as failures, so no released app keeps an `app-only` entry. An app whose `pauta.json` has no `template` field, no `app-only` entry and no `pending` link to another repository, or that has no `pauta.json`, shows nothing inherited from a template: it is outside the rule, and an audit reports it as `limited`.

rules.reference: the [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template): its [`pauta.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/pauta.json) has `"template": true` and nine `app-only` entries, its [`scripts/rename.sh`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/scripts/rename.sh) sets `"template": false`, and its [`PautaConformanceTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/PautaConformanceTest.java) holds both (`onlyATemplateRecordsWhatOnlyAnAppCanMeet`) and, outside a template, lists the `app-only` entries and the `pending` links to another repository in every build and fails on them when the `dist` profile sets `pauta.release` (`theAppListsWhatItInherited`; [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/pom.xml)). No app has been made from it yet.

rules.text: `pauta.json`'s `checked` list is the record of the rules checked by hand, and this rule governs only the entries an app chooses to record: each one is well formed and not stale. An app that records none, with no `checked` list or an empty one, meets it. An entry is there only because a person checked the rule in the running app and found it met, and it holds the `rule`, the `edition` it was checked against and the `date`, and may hold the app's `version`, for a rule that is checked again with each release (the screen-reader pass of [ACC-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/accessibility/#acc-07)): the audit reports it, and nothing expires by it. It says the rule was met when it was checked, not that the app still meets it. A rule found unmet gets an exception instead ([PAUTA-04](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#pauta-04)), never both. A by-hand rule with no entry has not been recorded as checked: it needs no exception and no issue, it does not change the computed conformance ([PAUTA-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#pauta-02)), and it does not fail this rule. The audit reports it as not recorded, so its report still says which by-hand rules nobody has recorded. An entry is stale when its `edition` is older than the rule's `changed` in the edition's `rules.json`, the edition in which the rule's level, scope or statement last changed, and only then: the app's test fails it ([PAUTA-10](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#pauta-10)) until it is removed and the rule checked again.
rules.why: an audit can only answer `manual` for these rules, and its report is written again each time. Without a record, a rule someone checked last week and a rule nobody ever looked at read the same. The record stays out of the conformance because nothing in the code tells an unchecked rule from a met one: counting it would make an app record as pending what it may well meet.

check.text: every `checked` entry has a `rule`, an `edition` and a `date`; the rule is one of the edition's whose check is by hand (`check.kind` in `rules.json`); the edition is no older than the rule's `changed` (one newer than `pauta.version`, and a rule listed twice, are for the test of [PAUTA-10](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#pauta-10) to fail); and no rule has an exception as well. With no `checked` list, or an empty one, there is no entry to fail and the rule is met: the audit's `manual` results say which by-hand rules are not recorded, and that is no failure of this rule. That a person looked is the entry's own claim, which the code can't show.

rules.reference: no app records a by-hand check yet, so each meets the rule with nothing to hold: the [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`pauta.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/pauta.json) has no `checked` list, though its [`PautaConformanceTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/PautaConformanceTest.java) would hold one (`eachCheckedEntryIsWellFormedAndCurrent`), and the six apps have no `pauta.json`.

rules.text: An app's exceptions and its record of by-hand checks have one source: `pauta.json`, bundled with the app's resources (`src/main/resources/com/<app>/pauta.json`) and laid out as [The file](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#the-file) shows. Its `exceptions` list has `rule`, `level`, `url`, `kind` and `reason` on every entry, `link` on every deviation and pending entry, and one entry per rule. Its `checked` list is the app's to keep or not: an app that records no by-hand check leaves it out or empty, and what an entry of it holds is [PAUTA-18](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#pauta-18)'s. `"template": true` stands beside the two lists only in a template repository (PAUTA-16).

check.text: `pauta.json` is among the app's bundled resources, under `src/main/resources/`; each exception has the fields its kind needs and no rule has two. The entries of the `checked` list are [PAUTA-18](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#pauta-18)'s to judge, and a file with no `checked` list passes.

rules.reference: The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`pauta.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/pauta.json), read by [`PautaConformanceTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/PautaConformanceTest.java) (`parsesEveryField`, `everyEntryNamesARuleOfTheEditionWithItsLevelAndAddress`). The file has no `checked` list, which the rule allows.

rules.text: A test reads `pauta.json` against a copy of the edition's `rules.json` in `src/test/resources/pauta-rules.json` and fails when the copy's `edition` is not `pauta.version`, when an entry names a rule the edition does not have, when its `level` or `url` differs from the edition's, when a rule appears twice, when a deviation names a MUST, when a deviation or pending entry has no `link`, or when a `checked` entry ([PAUTA-18](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#pauta-18)) names a rule that is not checked by hand, a rule listed twice, a rule with an exception, an edition newer than `pauta.version`, or an edition older than the rule's `changed`, which makes the entry stale. Outside a template, it reports each `app-only` entry and each `pending` link that is not an issue in the app's own repository (the one the app's own code names; `AppInfo.GITHUB_REPO` in the template), and fails on them in the release build ([PAUTA-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#pauta-16)).
rules.why: moving to a newer edition changes levels, retires IDs and changes rules a person checked by hand; the test turns each stale entry into a failure.

check.text: `PautaConformanceTest`, or the app's equivalent, runs in the build and has a case for each failure the rule lists.

rules.reference: The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`PautaConformanceTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/PautaConformanceTest.java) and its copy of the edition's rules, [`pauta-rules.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/resources/pauta-rules.json). It has a case for each failure: `theRulesCopyIsTheEditionThePomNames`, `everyEntryNamesARuleOfTheEditionWithItsLevelAndAddress` (an unknown rule, a level or `url` that differs, a rule twice), `eachKindHasWhatItNeeds` (a deviation on a MUST, a missing `link`), `eachCheckedEntryIsWellFormedAndCurrent` (the `checked` list) and `theAppListsWhatItInherited` (what a template left, failed when `pauta.release` is set).

rules.text: Moving to a newer edition is one change: replace `pauta-rules.json` with the new edition's, and the app's copy of the audit skill where it keeps one (the app template's is `.claude/skills/pauta-audit/SKILL.md`); remove the `checked` entries the new `rules.json` makes stale ([PAUTA-18](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#pauta-18)) and check those rules again; run the audit again and update `pauta.json`; then change `pauta.version`, the README and `AGENTS.md` together.
rules.why: each of these names or follows the edition. The test fails a `pauta-rules.json` or a `checked` entry left behind (PAUTA-10); nothing fails a skill copy left behind, which then audits the new rules by the old procedure.

check.text: the change that raises `pauta.version` also replaces `pauta-rules.json` and the skill copy, where the app keeps one, leaves no `checked` entry older than its rule's `changed`, and touches `pauta.json` where the audit found something new.

The Pauta window's link to it is [PWIN-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/pauta-window/#pwin-07).

check.text: the app names a website for its user docs ([DOCS-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/documentation/#docs-01)): an app whose repository and About name none has nowhere to carry the page, and fails the rule from the app's checkout. The rest is in the website's repository (`<app>-website`, [DOCS-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/documentation/#docs-02)): its docs (the files of `src/content/docs/` in editora-website) have the page, and the page gives the edition `pauta.version` names, the conformance the app's exceptions give, and every exception of the app's `pauta.json` under its kind, each with its rule ID linked to the edition's rule, its reason and its link. A page that lists other rules than the file fails. With no `pauta.json`, which is [PAUTA-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#pauta-01)'s and [PAUTA-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#pauta-09)'s failure, there is no list to compare, and the page is judged on being there with the edition. An audit run from the app's checkout alone reports the rule as `not-checked` and says what would settle it.

rules.text: The website's *Pauta conformance* page ([PAUTA-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#pauta-13)) is generated from the app's `pauta.json`, like the Commands page ([DOCS-04](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/documentation/#docs-04)), so it cannot list a different set from the app.

rules.text: The app builds on **JDK 25 or newer**. `maven.compiler.release` 25 is the floor, not the ceiling: a newer JDK builds the app too, so no enforcer rule refuses one, in the main build or in any profile that turns itself on (an `<activation>` by JDK version, OS, property or file, or one that is `activeByDefault`; a profile turned on only by name, with `-P`, is not counted). CI builds every app on JDK 25, the current LTS: every workflow step that sets up a JDK sets up release 25, and the runtime an installer carries ([PLAT-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/platform/#plat-02)) is that JDK's. A leg that builds a native image carries no JDK: it sets up a GraalVM 25 release instead, 25.0 or any later 25.x. The family moves to the next LTS together, in an edition of Pauta.

check.text: `pom.xml` sets `maven.compiler.release` to 25 or later. Every enforcer `requireJavaVersion` rule that counts refuses no JDK from 25 up: its range has no upper bound and starts at 25 or below, as the open-ended `[25,)` does, or a bare `25`, which the enforcer reads as 25 or newer. The rules that count are those of the main build and those inside a profile that turns itself on, one whose `<activation>` holds a `<jdk>`, an `<os>`, a `<property>` or a `<file>`, or an `<activeByDefault>` that is `true`: such a profile is on without being asked for, so its rule is the build's rule wherever it activates. A rule in a profile turned on only by name with `-P` is not counted, and an app with no rule that counts passes. In the workflows, every step that uses a `setup-java` or `setup-graalvm` action (`actions/setup-java`, `graalvm/setup-graalvm`) names 25 or a 25.x release in its `java-version`, and in the `version` a GraalVM step may give beside it or instead. The Command reads the pom as text, with its XML comments left out, and a workflow line by line, not as YAML: a step ends at the next line that opens a list item. A version it cannot read as a number (an expression such as `${{ matrix.java }}`, a `java-version-file`) it prints as not judged and does not fail: read the matrix or the file it names. An enforcer range held in a property (`${…}`) it cannot follow: it prints the property and fails, so read the property's value.

rules.text: Code is formatted by **Spotless** with Palantir Java Format, and CI fails an unformatted change in a Format job of its own: a job that runs `spotless:check` and neither builds nor tests. When CI runs and which of its jobs the default branch requires are [REL-19](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/release/#rel-19).
rules.why: a check bound to a build phase fails in the same job as the tests, so the failed job does not say which of the two is wrong.

check.text: the spotless plugin configures `palantirJavaFormat`, and in a workflow that runs on pull requests, which is where [REL-19](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/release/#rel-19) has CI run and so where an unformatted change is failed, a job runs `spotless:check` and neither builds nor tests: no Maven `compile`, `test-compile`, `test`, `package`, `verify`, `integration-test`, `install` or `deploy` in the same job. The plugin's `check` goal bound to a phase (`./mvnw verify`) does not meet it alone. The Command reads a workflow line by line, not as YAML: a job is what lies between two keys at the indentation of the first key under `jobs:`, and a Maven run counts when its goal is on the line that names `mvn` or `mvnw` (a `name:` line is not a run). A Format job in a workflow of its own that a pull-request workflow calls (`workflow_call`, `uses: ./.github/workflows/<file>`) meets the rule, and the Command follows that call. What it does not see, so read the workflow where one applies: a goal on a continuation line; a build started from a script; a job's `if:`.
check.command: [ -f pom.xml ] || { echo 'not an app root: no pom.xml here'; exit 1; }; grep -q palantirJavaFormat pom.xml || { echo 'pom.xml configures no palantirJavaFormat'; exit 1; }; for f in .github/workflows/*.yml .github/workflows/*.yaml; do grep -qE '^( *-? *|on:.*[^A-Za-z0-9_-])pull_request(_target)?([^A-Za-z0-9_-]|$)' "$f" 2>/dev/null || { grep -qE '^( *-? *|on:.*[^A-Za-z0-9_-])workflow_call([^A-Za-z0-9_-]|$)' "$f" 2>/dev/null && grep -lE "^[^#]*uses:[^#]*\./$f" .github/workflows/* 2>/dev/null | xargs grep -lE '^( *-? *|on:.*[^A-Za-z0-9_-])pull_request(_target)?([^A-Za-z0-9_-]|$)' 2>/dev/null | grep -q .; } || continue; i=$(sed -n '/^jobs:/,$p' < "$f" | grep -E '^ +[A-Za-z0-9_-]+:' | head -n 1 | sed -n 's/^\( *\).*/\1/p'); for s in $(grep -nE '^[^#]*mvnw?(\.cmd)?[[:space:]]([^#]*[[:space:]])?spotless:check' "$f" | grep -vE '^[0-9]+: *-? *name:' | cut -d: -f1); do a=0; b=999999; for h in $(grep -nE "^$i[A-Za-z0-9_-]+:" "$f" | cut -d: -f1); do if [ "$h" -le "$s" ]; then a=$h; elif [ "$b" -eq 999999 ]; then b=$h; fi; done; m=; for t in $(grep -nE '^[^#]*mvnw?(\.cmd)?[[:space:]]([^#]*[[:space:]])?(compile|test-compile|test|package|verify|integration-test|install|deploy)([^A-Za-z0-9:_.=/-]|$)' "$f" | grep -vE '^[0-9]+: *-? *name:' | cut -d: -f1); do [ "$t" -ge "$a" ] && [ "$t" -lt "$b" ] && m="$m $f:$t"; done; [ -z "$m" ] && exit 0; echo "spotless:check at $f:$s shares its job with a build or test run:$m"; done; done; w=$(grep -lE '^[^#]*spotless:check' .github/workflows/* 2>/dev/null); echo "no job of its own runs spotless:check in a workflow that runs on pull requests (named in: ${w:-no workflow})"; exit 1

rules.text: A **JaCoCo** `check` runs at `mvn verify` with build-wide floors of **≥ 0.90 lines and ≥ 0.90 methods**, and no profile that activates by OS or by JDK version lowers a floor or skips the check. The rule is about the pom's profiles, not about where CI runs the gate: a workflow that runs the tests on some of its runners with JaCoCo skipped is the workflow's choice and passes. The branch floor and each package's own floor are [QUAL-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/quality/#qual-03).

check.text: an execution of the JaCoCo plugin's `check` goal, whatever its id (Editora's is `jacoco-check`), is bound to `verify` with `BUNDLE` limits of 0.90 `LINE` and 0.90 `METHOD`. Where a limit is a property (`${coverage.bundle.line}` in Termina), its value is 0.90 or more in the main `<properties>` and in every profile that sets it and activates by OS or by JDK version (an `<activation>` with an `<os>` or a `<jdk>`), and no such profile sets `jacoco.skip` or the check's `<skip>`. rules.text: Every script in `scripts/` is a Java source file the JDK runs as it is (`java scripts/Name.java`, a compact source file or an ordinary class) or an `sh` or bash script.
rules.why: every app already needs the JDK, and a Java script runs the same on Windows, macOS and Linux. A Python or Node script makes every contributor and CI runner install a second toolchain for one step. A script that runs on Windows is easier to keep in Java than in bash.

check.text: no file under `scripts/` is Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Ruby, Perl, Groovy, Lua, PHP, PowerShell or a batch file, and every shebang there names `sh`, `bash` or `java`. Data files beside the scripts (fixtures, lists, templates) are not scripts.
check.command:
[ -f pom.xml ] || { echo 'not an app root: no pom.xml here'; exit 1; }; [ -d scripts ] || exit 0; bad=$(find scripts -type f | while IFS= read -r f; do if printf '%s
' "$f" | grep -qE '\.(py|js|mjs|cjs|ts|rb|pl|ps1|bat|cmd|groovy|kts|lua|php)$'; then echo "$f"; continue; fi; l=$(head -n 1 "$f" | tr -d ''); if printf '%s
' "$l" | grep -q '^#!'; then printf '%s
' "$l" | grep -qE '^#! *(/usr)?/bin/(env +(-S +)?)?((ba|da)?sh|java)( |$)' || echo "$f: $l"; fi; done); [ -z "$bad" ] || { printf '%s
' "$bad"; false; }

rules.reference: Editora [`scripts/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/tree/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/scripts), whose Java scripts have their own tests, run by [`scripts/lib/RunTests.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/scripts/lib/RunTests.java) ([`docs/testing.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/testing.md)).

rules.text: Every app has user documentation: a *Getting started* page (install, first launch, the first thing to do), one page per feature area, the keyboard reference, the Settings, and an FAQ. It is written for the person using the app, in their words, with screenshots from the real window. The README, a landing page of at most 250 lines ([REPO-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/repository/#repo-01)), is not it.

check.text: the app names a website for its user docs: its README or its About links one, or the address `help.documentation` opens ([DOCS-06](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/documentation/#docs-06)) is on one. The repository's own address on GitHub is not one. An app whose repository and About name no website has no user documentation to point at, and fails the rule from the app's checkout. The rest is in the website's repository: its docs (the files of `src/content/docs/` in editora-website) have a getting-started page, a keyboard reference (a keymaps page there), a settings or configuration page, an FAQ and a page per feature area, and the pages carry screenshots of the app's real window. The website is a repository of its own ([DOCS-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/documentation/#docs-02)), which the app's checkout does not hold. An audit run from the app's checkout alone reports the rule as `not-checked` and says what would settle it.

rules.reference: editora-website [`src/content/docs/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/editora-website/tree/1b6390c20c7a8aa3fc6af394b68c11454478d69d/src/content/docs) (43 pages in nine categories, from *Getting started* to *Help*); torrenta-website (19), termina-website (16), mirada-website (11).

rules.text: The user docs live on the app's website, under `/docs/`, in the app's `<app>-website` repository, beside the feature pages, the screenshots, the news posts and the blog. Each docs page is a Markdown file whose frontmatter gives the page's category and its place in it (editora-website's keys are `category` and `order`); the sidebar, the sitemap and the RSS feed follow. The app's repository carries none of them: a page kept in the app's `docs/` fails the rule when any section of it tells the app's user how to install or use something, even if the rest of the page is for contributors, and whether or not the website has it too.

check.text: no page in the app's `docs/` has a section that tells the person using the app how to install or use something: one found there fails the rule from the app's checkout, whoever the rest of the page is written for. So does an app whose repository and About name no website for its user docs ([DOCS-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/documentation/#docs-01)): its user docs live on none. The rest is in the website's repository: every docs page there (the files of `src/content/docs/` in editora-website) gives its category and its order in its frontmatter. An audit run from the app's checkout alone reports the rule as `not-checked` and says what would settle it.

rules.reference: editora-website [`README.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/editora-website/blob/1b6390c20c7a8aa3fc6af394b68c11454478d69d/README.md) (*Content*). Editora doesn't yet, though its [`AGENTS.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/AGENTS.md) says "User-facing feature documentation goes to the separate website repository": [`docs/plugins.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/plugins.md), a page for plugin authors, has a section that tells the user the three ways to install a plugin and one on troubleshooting plugins. Termina doesn't either: [`docs/reference/installing.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/docs/reference/installing.md) tells the person installing it which download to take, how to install each and how to check its signature, and its README sends the reader there. Nor does Torrenta: [`docs/headless.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/docs/headless.md), [`docs/webapi.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/docs/webapi.md) and [`docs/search-providers.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/docs/search-providers.md) are guides for the person using it.

rules.text: Every link from the app into its user docs opens the running version's docs, the address `help.documentation` opens ([DOCS-06](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/documentation/#docs-06)) as much as a link to one page. Pages live under `/docs/v-<version>/…`; bare `/docs` and every unversioned slug redirect to the current version, so a link in a page never carries a version and a bump just regenerates one file (editora-website's `src/lib/version.ts`). The app builds the base from its own version with `-SNAPSHOT` dropped, so a development build points at the release it is working toward instead of a path that would always 404.
rules.why: a release that pointed at another release's docs would claim what is not true ([*Never claim what is not true*](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/principles/#for-the-people-using-the-apps)).

check.text: the address the app opens for its docs is its website's `/docs/v-` plus the app's version without `-SNAPSHOT`: another address, the unversioned `/docs/` among them, fails the rule from the app's checkout. An app that opens no docs address has no link to judge and nothing to fail here: the missing address is [DOCS-06](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/documentation/#docs-06)'s. The rest is in the website's repository: it serves `/docs/v-<version>/` and redirects the unversioned paths (in its `astro.config.mjs`, in editora-website). An audit run from the app's checkout alone reports the rule as `not-checked` and says what would settle it.

rules.reference: Editora [`AppInfo.docsUrl()`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/AppInfo.java), `releaseVersion()`; editora-website [`astro.config.mjs`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/editora-website/blob/1b6390c20c7a8aa3fc6af394b68c11454478d69d/astro.config.mjs), [`README.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/editora-website/blob/1b6390c20c7a8aa3fc6af394b68c11454478d69d/README.md) (*Versioned docs*). The app template builds the same address (`docsUrl()` in its [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/AppInfo.java)). Termina and Mirada don't yet: each opens its site's unversioned `/docs/` (`DOCUMENTATION` in Termina's [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/AppInfo.java), `DOCS_URL` in Mirada's [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/AppInfo.java)). Torrenta, Modula and nux open no docs address. The other three sites carry a comment to port these routes when their app first deep-links.

rules.text: The website's docs are generated where the app is the source. The Commands and Keybindings pages are generated from the app's command registrations, `messages.properties` and keymaps; What's new from `CHANGELOG.md`, and the Roadmap from `TODO.md` where the app keeps one ([REPO-08](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/repository/#repo-08)); the version from `pom.xml`. The output is committed, so the site builds without the app checked out. A check fails the site when a docs page quotes a command id that does not exist or a chord that is bound to a different command.
rules.why: one fact, one source ([*One source of truth for each fact*](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/principles/#for-the-people-building-them)).

check.text: the website's repository holds the generators and their committed output (`scripts/` and `src/lib/` in editora-website) and a check of the ids and chords its docs quote (`npm run check:docs` there), and the site's build or its deploy workflow runs that check. An app that names no website has no docs to generate: the rule fails with [DOCS-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/documentation/#docs-01). All the rest is in the website's repository. An audit run from the app's checkout alone reports the rule as `not-checked` and says what would settle it.

rules.reference: editora-website [`scripts/GenCommands.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/editora-website/blob/1b6390c20c7a8aa3fc6af394b68c11454478d69d/scripts/GenCommands.java) (every `Command.of` in Editora's `com.editora.ui`, [`WindowCommandRegistrar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowCommandRegistrar.java) holding most), [`GenRoadmap.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/editora-website/blob/1b6390c20c7a8aa3fc6af394b68c11454478d69d/scripts/GenRoadmap.java), [`GenFeatures.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/editora-website/blob/1b6390c20c7a8aa3fc6af394b68c11454478d69d/scripts/GenFeatures.java); [`scripts/check-doc-commands.mjs`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/editora-website/blob/1b6390c20c7a8aa3fc6af394b68c11454478d69d/scripts/check-doc-commands.mjs) (`npm run check:docs`), which exits non-zero on a missing id or a chord bound to another command. Nothing runs it yet: neither the `build` script in [`package.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/editora-website/blob/1b6390c20c7a8aa3fc6af394b68c11454478d69d/package.json) nor [`pages.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/editora-website/blob/1b6390c20c7a8aa3fc6af394b68c11454478d69d/.github/workflows/pages.yml) calls it, so it fails the site only when someone runs it by hand.

rules.text: The notes of a GitHub release, the text under its title, are written for the person using the app: they say what changed for them, and are not a list of commits or pull requests. In an app with a Welcome page, the page's *What's New* link opens this build's release, so those notes are what it shows. The bold one-line summary that opens each `CHANGELOG.md` entry is [REPO-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/repository/#repo-02); the website's What's new is [DOCS-04](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/documentation/#docs-04); taking the notes from the version's `CHANGELOG.md` section is [REL-04](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/release/#rel-04).

check.text: the release's notes are not generated from the history: the JReleaser configuration's `changelog` is not a `format` of commit hashes and titles, and no release step sets `generate_release_notes`. They come from text someone wrote, the version's `CHANGELOG.md` section or a notes file. And in an app with a Welcome page, the page's *What's New* link opens the build's own release page (`AppInfo.releaseNotesUrl()` in Editora).

rules.reference: Termina's [`jreleaser.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/jreleaser.yml) takes the notes from a file (`changelog.external`) that [`scripts/release-notes.sh`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/scripts/release-notes.sh) writes from the version's `CHANGELOG.md` section; the app template, Torrenta and Mirada do the same. Editora doesn't yet: its [`jreleaser.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/jreleaser.yml) builds the notes from the commits (`format: '- {{commitShortHash}} {{commitTitle}}'`), and that list is what its *What's New* opens ([`AppInfo.releaseNotesUrl()`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/AppInfo.java), [`WelcomePane`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WelcomePane.java), `welcome.whatsNew`). Modula's [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/.github/workflows/release.yml) and nux's [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/.github/workflows/release.yml) have GitHub generate them (`generate_release_notes: true`).

rules.text: The `help.documentation` command opens the user docs in the browser. It is a command like any other, so it is in the palette and bindable, and where the app has a Help menu (the Help menu of a menu bar, or a Help submenu of the app's main menu, which [WIN-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-14) defines) a **Documentation** row of that menu runs it through the registry like every other row. An app with a Welcome page repeats the command in the page's Help row. The row's place in the Help menu is [DOCS-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/documentation/#docs-07).

check.text: the command `help.documentation` is registered and opens the user docs' address in the browser; where the app has a Help menu, a row of that menu runs the command (the Help `MenuSpec` of Editora's `MenuBarModel` lists it), and a row beside a Help submenu is not in it; and in an app with a Welcome page, the page's Help row runs the same command through the registry (`welcome.documentation` in Editora's `WelcomePane`).

rules.reference: Editora [`WindowCommandRegistrar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowCommandRegistrar.java) (`help.documentation` → [`MainController.openDocumentation()`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java)), [`MenuBarModel`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MenuBarModel.java) (`menubar.help`), [`WelcomePane`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WelcomePane.java) (`welcome.documentation`). Mirada's macOS Help menu has the row ([`MacMenus`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/MacMenus.java)); its main menu doesn't yet: there the Documentation row sits beside the Help submenu, not in it ([`ui/TitleBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/TitleBar.java)).

rules.text: Where the app has a Help menu (the Help menu of a menu bar, or a Help submenu of the app's main menu, which [WIN-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-14) defines), its rows run in this order: Command Palette · Documentation · the keyboard reference ([DOCS-08](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/documentation/#docs-08)) · Welcome Page · Check for Updates · Message Log · Debug Log · Report a Problem · Pauta Conformance · About. In an app with a Simple mode, that mode's Help menu keeps Command Palette, Documentation, Welcome Page and About. An app without a feature drops its row; nothing moves.

check.text: the rows of the Help menu the app has are in that order, in the full menu and in Simple mode's where the app has one (both `menubar.help` menu specs in Editora). An app with a Help menu in a menu bar on one OS and a Help submenu in its main menu is judged on both.

rules.reference: Editora [`MenuBarModel`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MenuBarModel.java), both `MenuSpec("menubar.help", …)`, for the rows its Help menu has. It has no Welcome Page row, since `view.welcome` is still in the View menu ([WELC-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/welcome/#welc-03)), and no keyboard-reference row. Termina's [`MenuBarModel`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/MenuBarModel.java) (`documentation`, `whatsNew`, `keyboardShortcuts`, then `checkForUpdates`) and Mirada's macOS menu bar, [`MacMenus`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/MacMenus.java) (`PALETTE`, `DOCUMENTATION`, `SHORTCUTS`, then `CHECK_FOR_UPDATES`) put the keyboard reference there; Termina's What's New row, between the two, is its own. The Help submenu of Mirada's main menu doesn't follow the order yet: it holds Message Log, Debug Log, Report a Problem, then Check for Updates, and Documentation, the keyboard reference and About are rows of the main menu beside it ([`ui/TitleBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/TitleBar.java)).

rules.text: Where the app has a Help menu (the Help menu of a menu bar, or a Help submenu of the app's main menu, which [WIN-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-14) defines), a row of it opens a keyboard reference: a searchable window of every key, grouped as the menus are, or the keybinding editor.

check.text: open it from Help, search for a command, and find its key.

rules.reference: Termina's [`ShortcutsWindow`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/ShortcutsWindow.java), a row of its Help menu, and Mirada's [`ShortcutsWindow`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/ShortcutsWindow.java), a row of its macOS Help menu; in Mirada's main menu the row sits beside the Help submenu. Editora doesn't yet: its keybinding editor is a page of Settings ([Keyboard first](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/keyboard/)), and no row of its Help menu opens it ([`MenuBarModel`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MenuBarModel.java)).

rules.text: An app with a Search Everywhere picker opens per-command help from it as the Command Palette does: with a command highlighted, the palette's help chord ([PAL-08](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/command-palette/#pal-08)) opens the command's page, `/docs/v-<version>/commands/<id>`. The two pickers share the chord and the URL builder, so they can never disagree.

check.text: Search Everywhere takes its help chord the way the palette does and builds the page's address with the palette's own method (Editora's `CommandPalette.docsUrl`).

rules.reference: Editora [`SearchEverywhereHost`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SearchEverywhereHost.java) (`CommandPalette.docsUrl`) and [`SearchEverywherePopup`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SearchEverywherePopup.java) (`docsChord`, from [`PickerKeys.freeChord`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/PickerKeys.java) as the palette's); [`CommandPalette.docsUrl`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java).

rules.text: Each page of the Settings window has a link to its docs page, *Help for* and the page's name, from one map of page to slug.

check.text: one map from Settings page to docs slug feeds every page's help link.

rules.reference: Editora [`SettingsWindow`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsWindow.java), [`SettingsFrameBits.helpUrl`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsFrameBits.java), `settings.help`.

rules.text: `docs/` has an index. `docs/README.md` says who the folder is for (contributors; user docs live on the website) and lists every guide with one line; that the code wins is [DOCS-17](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/documentation/#docs-17).
