rules.text: Never block the JavaFX application thread. No file or network I/O, no process start or wait, no parsing, searching, hashing or JSON of any size on it, and no `Thread.sleep`, `Future.get()`, `join()` or `Process.waitFor()` there. Two exceptions. At start-up, before the first window is shown, `start()` may wait once for the config read that [PERF-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/performance/#perf-16) began before the toolkit, and may read the bundled resources that window is built from: its fonts, registered there or by a thread `start()` waits for once ([ICON-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/icons-and-color/#icon-02) requires them before any CSS is applied), the message catalog, the keymap and its icons. Nothing else at start-up is excepted: a log file opened, a file or a store of the user's read (presets, profiles, schedules, themes the user added), a ledger read, a socket bound or a lock taken blocks the thread as it would anywhere, and so does a font registered on it after the first frame. And as the app quits, when no frame is left to block, the quit method ([WIN-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-13)) or `Application.stop()` may make the last save on it: write the settings, the window state and the session, or wait for a write already under way. An app whose `start()` loads its settings itself, whether or not `main` read the file earlier, or waits for a read begun after the toolkit, has PERF-16's gap and none here.

check.text: `grep -rnE 'Files\.[a-z]|File(Input|Output)Stream|File(Reader|Writer)|RandomAccessFile|getResourceAsStream|loadFont|HttpClient|openConnection|openStream|new Socket|SocketChannel\.open|ProcessBuilder|getRuntime\(\)\.exec|\.waitFor\(|Thread\.sleep|\.join\(\)|uture[A-Za-z]*\.get\(|\.get\([^)]*TimeUnit|invokeAndWait|\.await\(' src/main/java` lists the candidates: the lines that read or write a file or a bundled resource, open a connection, start or wait for a process, sleep, or wait for another thread. Each line is judged by reading what calls it. It is fine when only an executor's task or a thread's body reaches it; when `start()` reaches it before the first window is shown and it is one of the things the statement allows there, the one `join()` or `get()` on the config read begun before the toolkit, or the reading of a resource bundled with the app that the first window is built from: the registering of the fonts it draws with (Editora's `Fonts.loadForFirstPaint`) or the one wait for the thread that registers them, the message catalog (Editora's `Messages.init`), the keymap (Editora's `KeymapManager.loadNamed`) or the window's icons; or when it is the last save, made by the quit method or `Application.stop()`, which may do nothing else that blocks. It is a violation when an event handler, a listener, a `Platform.runLater` body, a timer's or an animation's callback, or `start()` reaches it on the FX thread, itself or through a method it calls: a handler that calls a settings store's `save()` writes the file on the FX thread. In `start()` everything else is a violation, before the first window is shown or after: a second wait for the config, a log file opened, a file or a store of the user's read (presets, profiles, schedules, a folder of themes the user added), a ledger read, a socket bound, a lock taken. Only the settings are left to [PERF-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/performance/#perf-16): a load of them made in `start()` itself, whether or not `main` read the file earlier, and a wait for a read of them begun after the toolkit. A font registered on the FX thread after the first frame is a violation too. A grep finds only the spellings it is given: read the handlers and listeners too for parsing, searching, hashing or JSON done in place, and for a wait under another name.

rules.reference: Editora [`docs/performance.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/performance.md) §1; its one start-up wait is `takeBootstrap` in [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java), which joins the `config-prefetch` read, and `Fonts.loadForFirstPaint`, called next, registers its first fonts ([`ui/Fonts.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Fonts.java)); the `config-prefetch` thread reads the catalog too, and `start()` reads it only when that thread picked another language (`Messages.init`). Mirada's `start()` makes the two waits the first exception allows: `settings()` joins the settings read, which also reads its catalog (in its jlink image that read begins after the toolkit, which is [PERF-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/performance/#perf-16)'s gap and none here), and `Fonts.ready`, before the window is shown, joins the thread that registers its fonts ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/App.java), [`ui/Fonts.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Fonts.java)). For the last save, the app template's [`MainWindow.quit`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MainWindow.java) waits for the settings write on a background thread and exits from there, which needs no exception, and its `Application.stop()` then waits for the writer once more on the FX thread (`Running.close` in [`ui/Startup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Startup.java)), which the second exception allows; Termina's [`WindowManager.closeAll`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/WindowManager.java), run from `Application.stop()`, flushes its settings on the FX thread, which the second exception allows. The app template does its start's file work off the FX thread: `prepare` in [`ui/Startup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Startup.java), which refuses the FX thread and runs on a thread of its own while the toolkit starts, opens the Debug Log's session file, reads the settings, the catalog and `pauta.json` and binds the single-instance socket; `start()` then registers its first fonts, which the first exception allows (`Fonts.load`), and the remaining font is registered off the FX thread after the first frame (`Fonts.loadDeferred`). No app has been read through for the rule yet, and none holds it everywhere. Found so far: Editora's `start()`, in that `App.java`, does on the FX thread, before its first window is shown, what no exception covers: its calls to `DebugLog.attachFile` (the Debug Log's session file), `SharedConfig.claimInstance` (the lock on a file in the config folder), `ProcessRegistry.reapOrphans` (the ledger of the servers it started), `McpServer.reapStaleEndpoint` (a stale `mcp-endpoint.json`) and `Themes.loadUserThemes` (the user themes' folders). Some of its handlers still touch the disk too, for example `renameFileTo` (`Files.exists`, `Files.move`) and `openPersonalDictionary` (`Files.writeString`) in [`ui/MainController.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java) and the new-folder prompt in [`ui/ProjectPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ProjectPanel.java) (`Files.createDirectories`). Torrenta's `start()` reads its catalog, which the exception allows, and opens that file the same way (`DebugLog.attachFile` in its [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/App.java)); its main window's constructor, before the window is shown, reads six stores of the user's (the profiles, the labels, the watch folders, the search providers, their definitions and the RSS feeds, in [`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java)), and `start()` reads `profiles.json` again once the window is shown (`Startup.profile`). Termina reads its settings, its first fonts, its catalog and its imported themes in `Application.init()`, off the FX thread (`prepare` in its [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/App.java)); building its first window then reads the bundled keymap ([`ui/Keymap.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/Keymap.java), on the first `Keymap.defaultFor`) and decodes the window's icons ([`ui/Icons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/Icons.java), `Icons.applyTo`) on the FX thread, which the exception allows, and once the window is shown `start()` deletes a stale socket file and binds the socket for later launches there, which it does not (`serve` in [`instance/SingleInstance.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/instance/SingleInstance.java)). It also registers its remaining font families on the FX thread after the first frame, which no exception covers ([`Fonts.loadRest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/Fonts.java), called from that `App.java`). Mirada, on macOS, compares two paths on the FX thread when it was started with a file and the OS hands it its first one (`Files.isSameFile` in [`os/MacOpenFiles.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/os/MacOpenFiles.java)). nux waits up to two seconds for the tray icon's removal in the handler of Settings' Save ([`AwtTray.dispose`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/tray/AwtTray.java), reached from [`TrayController.settingsSaved`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/app/TrayController.java)) and writes its `--screenshot` file from an animation's callback ([`ui/Screenshot.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/Screenshot.java)). Torrenta writes its settings from the listeners of its Settings rows (`saveQuietly` in [`ui/SettingsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/SettingsWindow.java)) and asks the file store for the free space on each keystroke in a save-folder field (`updateFreeSpace` in [`ui/LocationDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/LocationDialog.java)). Modula reads its presets and its schedules in its pane's constructor, before the window is shown (`config.loadPresets` and `config.loadSchedules` in [`ui/RadioPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/RadioPane.java)), writes its presets and settings from handlers (`config.savePresets` and `config.saveSettings` in that file) and, building its Settings window, starts `ffmpeg -version` and waits up to five seconds for it ([`Encoders.isAvailable`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/audio/Encoders.java)).

rules.text: Touch the scene graph only on the FX thread. Background work hands its result back with `Platform.runLater`; nothing else creates, changes or reads live nodes.

check.text: `grep -rnE 'new Thread\(|Thread\.(ofVirtual|ofPlatform|startVirtualThread)|\.(submit|execute|schedule|scheduleAtFixedRate|scheduleWithFixedDelay)\(|(supply|run)Async\(|\.(thenAccept|thenRun|thenApply|thenCompose|whenComplete|handle|exceptionally)(Async)?\(' src/main/java` lists the candidates: the lines that start a thread, hand a task to an executor, or add a step to a future that completes off the FX thread. Each line is judged by reading the task's body. It is fine when the body touches nothing a scene shows, or touches it only inside `Platform.runLater`. It is a violation when the body, or a method it calls, sets a control's value, changes an observable list a view shows, or reads a live node's state outside a `runLater`. A callback that a library runs on a thread of its own (a file watcher, a process's reader, a logging handler) is a task body too, and the grep does not list those: read the listeners the app gives its services as well.

rules.reference: Editora [`git/GitService.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/git/GitService.java): every task it gives its workers hands the result to its caller inside `Platform.runLater`. No app has been read through for the rule yet.

rules.text: A background result is applied under a generation guard, so an answer to an old request never overwrites a newer one.

check.text: `grep -rn 'runLater' src/main/java` lists the candidates: the lines where another thread hands something to the FX thread. Each line is judged by reading it. It needs the guard when what it applies answers a request that can be made again before the answer comes: a search, a load, a status or completion query that typing, a selection or a refresh starts. There each request takes a mark that the next request replaces (a counter, as Editora's `AtomicLong.incrementAndGet`, or a helper that keeps the latest request only, as Editora's `LatestOnly`), and the answer is applied only while its mark is still the newest, compared inside the `runLater`. It is a violation when such an answer is applied with no comparison, or with one made only before the `runLater`. A line needs no guard when nothing newer can replace what it hands over: an event, a batch of a stream, a result asked for once at start-up.

rules.reference: Editora [`git/GitService.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/git/GitService.java) (`refresh`, with its `refreshGen` counter), [`search/SearchService.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/search/SearchService.java) and [`ui/LatestOnly.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/LatestOnly.java) ([`LatestOnlyTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/LatestOnlyTest.java)); Termina ([`work/LatestOnly.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/work/LatestOnly.java)) and Mirada ([`ui/LatestOnly.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/LatestOnly.java)) carry the same helper. No app has been read through for the rule yet. Found so far: nux applies each Refresh of its Events window, and each load of the Energy and Outages tabs of its History window, with no mark ([`ui/EventsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/EventsWindow.java), `offFx` in [`ui/HistoryWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/HistoryWindow.java)), beside a Charts tab that numbers its loads and applies only the newest.

rules.text: Every thread is named and is a daemon.
rules.why: a thread dump then says what is running, and a stray worker never keeps the app alive after its last window closes.

check.text: every `Executors.new…` and `new Thread` gets a name and `setDaemon(true)`, through a thread factory such as `daemon("my-feature")`; virtual threads are daemons already.

rules.reference: Editora [`terminal/TerminalExecutors.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/terminal/TerminalExecutors.java) (its `daemon(name)` thread factory); the canonical shape is in [The UI thread](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/performance/#the-ui-thread).

rules.text: Blocking work stays off the common `ForkJoinPool`: no `supplyAsync` or `runAsync` without an executor runs a blocking call, and a `Process` subclass overrides `onExit()`, whose inherited version is a `waitFor()` on that pool.
rules.why: the common pool has one worker fewer than the machine has cores, so a few blocked waits (`CompletableFuture.supplyAsync` of a `waitFor`) starve every other user of it.

check.text: no `supplyAsync` or `runAsync` without an executor wraps a blocking call (a wait, a read or write of a file, a socket or a process), and every class that extends `Process` overrides `onExit()`. An app with no `Process` subclass has only the first half to show.

rules.reference: Editora [`process/ExitWatch.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/process/ExitWatch.java), [`docs/gotchas.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/gotchas.md). Editora's [`DapManager.reportJavaExit`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/dap/DapManager.java) still waits up to 3 s for an exit code in a `supplyAsync` on the common pool, and Termina's `handOff` in [`instance/SingleInstance.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/instance/SingleInstance.java) connects to a socket, writes and reads in one.

rules.text: Redraws are coalesced to at most one per pulse, with a flag that one request is already queued. A redraw is the painting of what the app draws itself, a canvas, a chart or a grid of cells; in an app that paints nothing itself, it is the refresh of its list or view.

check.text: a redraw request sets a flag (Editora's are named `…Pending`) and schedules one pass, and a request that finds the flag set schedules nothing. A handler that paints, or in an app that paints nothing refreshes its list or view, straight from its event has no such flag and fails: a chart drawn from its width listener and again from its height listener draws twice for one resize. Setting a control's own property in a handler (a label's text, a progress bar's value) is not a redraw: JavaFX draws the control once on the next pulse.

rules.reference: Editora [`docs/performance.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/performance.md) §2 (the `redrawPending` shape) and [`ui/WindowToolbar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowToolbar.java) (`scheduleEditStateRefresh`, with its `editStateRefreshPending` flag). [`ui/FxThrottle.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/FxThrottle.java) is another tool: a leading-edge throttle with a maximum wait and no such flag, which runs the first request of a burst at once and then at most one per interval.

rules.text: Work driven by text the user types waits for typing to pause (a debounce) when it leaves the FX thread or cannot finish within a frame: a search of files, a request to a server, a re-highlight. Filtering a list already in memory, as a command palette does, is exempt and runs on every keystroke.

check.text: a listener on a text input's text that starts background work, or work too long for one frame, restarts a timer (a `PauseTransition`'s `playFromStart`, or the app's debounce helper) and the work runs when the timer fires; a listener that only filters or ranks an in-memory list needs none.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/SearchInFilesPopup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SearchInFilesPopup.java) (150 ms before `runSearch`), [`ui/SearchEverywherePopup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SearchEverywherePopup.java) (120 ms), [`ui/WorkspaceSymbolPopup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WorkspaceSymbolPopup.java) (150 ms before the language server is asked) and, for the editor's text, [`editor/SettledEditDispatcher.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/SettledEditDispatcher.java), one timer that runs the re-highlight 150 ms after the last edit. Its [`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java) and [`ui/QuickOpen.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpen.java) filter their in-memory lists on every keystroke: the exempt case. Editora doesn't hold the rule everywhere yet: the debugger's completion ([`ui/DebugCompletion.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/DebugCompletion.java)) asks the debug adapter again on every change of the field's text while its list is open, with no timer, and [`ui/FileFinder.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/FileFinder.java) starts reading a folder as soon as the typed path names another one.

rules.text: An app that shows a stream as it arrives (the output of a process, log records, progress or readings from another thread) hands it to the FX thread in batches at least 16 ms apart, never one `runLater` per line or record.

check.text: in an app that shows a stream, the thread that receives it appends to a buffer that the FX thread drains, with a minimum interval of 16 ms or more between drains, or once a pulse (pulses come a frame apart); no reader calls `Platform.runLater` once for each line or record. A stream is what arrives at its source's pace, however many items that is: a process's output, log records, the results of a scan handed over as each is found. A poll the app paces itself, one hand-over for each tick of a timer of 16 ms or more (a reading fetched every few seconds), already hands over that far apart and needs no buffer. An app whose FX thread is sent no stream, as one whose log window reads its store only when it opens or is refreshed, is not covered.

rules.reference: Editora [`process/OutputPump.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/process/OutputPump.java) (`MIN_DRAIN_INTERVAL_MILLIS`), [`ui/ConsoleAppender.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ConsoleAppender.java). Torrenta doesn't yet for its event log: the bridge in [`ui/EventLog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/EventLog.java) (`logBridge`) hands each warning it catches to the FX thread in a `runLater` of its own. nux doesn't yet for its network scan: `scan` in [`service/DiscoveryService.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/service/DiscoveryService.java) hands each server it finds to the FX thread in a `runLater` of its own; its poll hands over one reading every five seconds ([`service/PollService.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/service/PollService.java)), which is paced already. Mirada's Debug Log window ([`ui/DebugLogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/DebugLogWindow.java)) reads the log when it opens and on Refresh, so no log stream reaches its FX thread.

rules.text: Work only on what is visible and only on what changed: no O(document) or O(list) work per keystroke, scroll or tick, and a list the user or the data can grow without a limit the app sets is shown in a virtualized control (`ListView`, `TableView`, a fixed cell size), which builds nodes for the visible rows only. Filtering a list already in memory, as a command palette does, is exempt and runs on every keystroke.

check.text: `grep -rnE 'textProperty\(\)|KEY_(TYPED|PRESSED)|setOnKey|setOnScroll|vvalueProperty|AnimationTimer|Timeline|PauseTransition|scheduleAtFixedRate' src/main/java` lists the first candidates: the listeners on text, keys and scrolling, and the timers. Each line is judged by reading what it runs on every keystroke, scroll or tick. It is fine when that handles the edited range or the visible rows, or filters or ranks a list already in memory. It is a violation when it reads, measures, styles or rebuilds the whole document or every item of a list. An editor's own stream of changes is a text listener too (Editora's `plainTextChanges`), which the grep does not list. `grep -rnE 'getChildren\(\)\.(add|addAll|setAll)\(' src/main/java` lists the second: the lines that put nodes into a pane. It is a violation where a loop makes one node for each item of a list the user or the data can grow without a limit the app sets (results, log records, files, transfers), which belongs in a `ListView` or `TableView`; it is fine where the pane holds a set of controls the code fixes, or a list the app caps at a number it names (a bar of at most five preset chips).

rules.reference: Editora [`editor/highlight/HighlightPass.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/highlight/HighlightPass.java), which restyles only as far as an edit reaches. No app has been read through for the rule yet. Found so far, each a loop that makes a node for every item of a list nothing caps: Modula's preset bar (a chip for each preset, `rebuild` in [`ui/PresetBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/PresetBar.java)); nux's dashboard (a card for each saved profile it watches and for each UPS, rebuilt as readings arrive, `setFleet` and `setOverview` in [`ui/Dashboard.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/Dashboard.java)); Torrenta's rule and tags dialogs (a check box for each feed and each tag, [`ui/RuleDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/RuleDialog.java), [`ui/TagsDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/TagsDialog.java)); and Editora's crontab preview and pull-request checks card (a node for each job and each check run, [`editor/structured/CrontabPreview.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/structured/CrontabPreview.java), [`ui/ChecksListCard.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ChecksListCard.java)).

rules.text: A hot path allocates little: it reuses buffers and arrays, and caches data a repaint only reads.

check.text: the per-frame and per-keystroke code allocates no new arrays or images when the size has not changed.

rules.reference: Editora [`editor/minimap/Minimap.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/minimap/Minimap.java) (the snapshot image reused at the same size), [`MinimapRows.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/minimap/MinimapRows.java). The app template's palette cells keep their text runs, chord chip and tooltip and relabel them as the query changes, making a new run only when a title needs more than the cell had ([`ui/Picker.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Picker.java)).

rules.text: CSS stays cheap: no `applyCss()` on a large subtree, stable style classes, and spans of the same style merged before they are applied.

check.text: `applyCss()` is called only on small nodes; style classes are not toggled per keystroke.

rules.reference: Editora `SpanMerger` in [`editor/highlight/TextMateHighlighter.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/highlight/TextMateHighlighter.java), [`docs/gotchas.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/gotchas.md). The app template's palette draws a title as one text run per change of style, not a node per letter ([`ui/Picker.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Picker.java)).

rules.text: Everything that grows is bounded: logs, histories, consoles, caches, undo. The newest is kept.

check.text: each store that grows while the app runs (a log, a history, a console's text, a cache, an undo stack) has a named cap, and the code that adds to it drops the oldest entry once the cap is passed. A test that fills a store past its cap and finds the oldest dropped is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/MessageLog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLog.java) (200 entries, the oldest dropped; [`MessageLogTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLogTest.java)), [`ui/DebugLog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/DebugLog.java) (2,000 records, the oldest dropped; [`DebugLogTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/DebugLogTest.java)), and [`test/OutputCap.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/test/OutputCap.java), which keeps the head and the tail of one test's output (200,000 characters) with a note between them of how much was cut. The note is Editora's choice, not part of the rule.

rules.text: In an app that opens files or data the user picks, a large input is guarded before it loads: its size is checked before its content is read, or the read is capped, and what will not fit is never read in. The app refuses it with a message or opens only the part that fits. Where an input can open with less, without features the app runs over its content, as a file in an editor can open without highlighting or a minimap, the app steps down as the input grows: those features turn off past one threshold, and past another it opens read-only or capped. An input the app can only read in or refuse (an imported theme, a `.torrent` file) has nothing to step down to.

check.text: the code that loads a picked file or import compares its size against a named limit before reading the content, or reads through a cap, and refuses or cuts what passes the limit. Where the app runs features over an input's content that the input can open without (an editor's highlighting, its minimap), a lower named threshold turns them off and a higher one opens the input read-only or capped. Where it runs none, the size check or the cap is the whole of the rule.

rules.reference: Editora, whose tiers are the example: [`EditorBuffer.LARGE_FILE_BYTES`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/EditorBuffer.java) (5 MB: no highlighting, no minimap) and `HUGE_FILE_BYTES` (50 MB: read-only and cut to 50 MB), and [`ui/LoadHeapGuard.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/LoadHeapGuard.java), which caps a load at what the free heap affords ([`LoadHeapGuardTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/LoadHeapGuardTest.java)). Termina's theme import has nothing to step down to: `importFile` in [`ui/Themes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/Themes.java) reads at most 8 MB and [`theme/ThemeImport.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/theme/ThemeImport.java) refuses a file over 4 MB. Torrenta doesn't yet for a `.torrent` file the user picks: `resolve` in [`session/Session.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/session/Session.java) reads it whole (`Files.readAllBytes`) without looking at its size.

rules.text: A closed window releases what it held: listeners, timers, executors, file watchers, native resources.

check.text: the code that runs when a window closes (its close or hide handler, or the dispose method that handler calls) stops every timer and animation the window started, shuts down every executor, thread and file watcher it owns, frees its native resources (a process, a socket, a file handle), and removes each listener it added to something that outlives it: the shared settings, a service, another window. A test that opens and closes windows and finds nothing left running is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora's [`MainController.disposeWindow`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java), which shuts down each owner of a window's workers in turn, one failure never skipping the rest ([`ui/WindowDisposal.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowDisposal.java)). Its tests: [`FxWindowFixtureLifecycleFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/FxWindowFixtureLifecycleFxTest.java), which finds a disposed window's workers shut down, and [`ClosedLspManagers`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/lsp/ClosedLspManagers.java). The app template ([`WindowLifecycleFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/WindowLifecycleFxTest.java)), Termina ([`WindowLifecycleTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/ui/WindowLifecycleTest.java)) and Mirada ([`ClosedWindowTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/ui/ClosedWindowTest.java)) have such a test too.

rules.text: The first frame comes first: only what the first window shows is built before it. Everything else builds on first open: a closed panel's content, the Settings pages, the dialogs and the other windows.

check.text: the code that builds the first window (`start()`, and the main window's constructor and what it calls) makes only what that window shows: no Settings window or page, no dialog, no other window and, in an app with tool panels, no closed panel's content. Each of those is made by the code that first opens it, through a supplier or a field filled on first use. A test that opens the first window and finds none of them built is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora's lazy [`ToolWindow`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindow.java) suppliers, and its Settings pages, built on the first `show` ([`ui/SettingsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsWindow.java)). [`LazyToolWindowsFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/LazyToolWindowsFxTest.java) asserts the tool-panel part: no closed tool window has built its panel. Editora doesn't hold the rule in one place yet: it builds the shared Output console (`buildOutput`), an empty tab pane, with the window, because every build writes to it while it is closed, and the test leaves that panel out. The template's [`StartupDeferralFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/StartupDeferralFxTest.java) and Mirada's [`StartupDeferralTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/ui/StartupDeferralTest.java) assert it for their first windows. Torrenta doesn't yet: the constructor of its main window makes the Log, the Statistics and the Settings windows (`new LogWindow`, `new StatisticsWindow`, `new SettingsWindow` in [`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java)).

rules.text: What nobody waits for starts after the first frame has painted: the update check, extra fonts, indexes and caches.

check.text: the update check, the loading of fonts the first window does not draw with, and the building of indexes and caches start from a callback that runs once the first frame has painted (a pulse after the window is shown, as Editora's `loadRemainingAfterNextPaint` waits for), never from `main`, `init()` or the body of `start()`. A test that finds the deferred work not started before the first paint is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/UpdateCheckScheduler.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/UpdateCheckScheduler.java), [`Fonts.loadRemainingAfterNextPaint`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Fonts.java) ([`UpdateCheckSchedulerTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/UpdateCheckSchedulerTest.java), [`FontsDeferredLoadFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/FontsDeferredLoadFxTest.java), [`StartupDeferralFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/StartupDeferralFxTest.java)). The template (`FirstPaint.then` in [`ui/Startup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Startup.java)), Termina (`FirstFrame.after` in its [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/App.java)) and Mirada (`afterFirstPaint` in [`ui/ViewerWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/ViewerWindow.java)) defer theirs the same way. Modula and nux don't yet: each starts its update check in the body of `start()` (`checkForUpdates` in [`ModulaApp.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ModulaApp.java), `maybeCheckForUpdates` in nux's [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java)).

rules.text: The config read starts on a thread of its own before the toolkit does, so the two overlap and the wait for it that [PERF-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/performance/#perf-01) allows at start-up, `start()` taking the result, is short. An app whose `start()` loads its settings itself does not meet this, whether or not `main` read the file earlier.

check.text: `main` starts the config read on its own thread before `launch`, from an entry point that is not the `Application` subclass (the launcher starts the toolkit for one before its `main` runs), and `start()` takes that read's result instead of reading the files itself. A load `start()` makes only when the earlier read failed is a fallback and passes.

rules.reference: Editora's `config-prefetch` thread in [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java) (`prefetchConfig`, joined once by `takeBootstrap`), entered through [`Launcher.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/Launcher.java). Mirada's `settings-read` thread in its [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/App.java) (`readSettings`, joined by `settings()`) does the same in the native image, which enters through `Launcher`; its jlink image's main class is `App` itself, so there the toolkit is up before the read starts. Termina reads its settings in `Application.init()` (`prepare` in its [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/App.java)): off the FX thread, so `start()` waits for nothing, but after the toolkit has started. The app template meets it: its [`Main.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/Main.java), not the `Application` subclass, starts `Startup.readAhead` on a thread of its own before `launch`, and `App.init` takes the result (`takePrepared` in [`ui/Startup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Startup.java)), so `start()` reads no settings file. Torrenta ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/App.java)), Modula ([`ModulaApp.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ModulaApp.java)) and nux ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java), which also reads the file once in `main` for the language) load their settings inside `start()`. Torrenta's `main` reads the file once as well, on the main thread, for its tray and badge settings.

rules.text: The app ships precompiled stylesheets (`.bss`). The AOT cache, the other half of a fast start, is [REL-10](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/release/#rel-10).

check.text: the build converts the app's `.css` files to `.bss`, and the packaged app carries them.

rules.reference: Editora [`scripts/css2bss.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/scripts/css2bss.java), run by the `css-to-bss` execution in [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/pom.xml). The app template's `dist` profile runs its [`ui/StyleCompiler.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/StyleCompiler.java) over the built stylesheets, which writes a `.bss` beside each `.css`, and [`ui/Themes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Themes.java) loads the `.bss` where there is one ([`StyleCompilerTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/StyleCompilerTest.java)). No other app converts its own stylesheets yet.

rules.text: Every change on a hot path says what it costs in its pull request: added FX-thread work, allocation per keystroke or scroll, extra layout passes, memory. "Negligible" is an answer; no answer is not.

check.text: read the app's recent pull requests that touch a hot path.

rules.reference: Editora [`docs/performance.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/docs/performance.md) (its opening paragraph).

rules.text: Start-up is measured by a script that takes the median of several cold launches, and by phase marks in the app.

check.text: the repository has the script, and `main` and the first paint record phase marks.

rules.reference: `scripts/measure-startup.sh` in Editora, Termina, Mirada and the app template, whose marks are recorded by [`StartupMarks.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/StartupMarks.java) from `main` and the first paint; Editora [`perf/Startup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/perf/Startup.java).

check.text: an environment variable or property turns on a sampler of the FX thread's stack.

check.text: the fix for a hot-path regression adds a headless test that fails on the old code.

rules.text: Every user-facing action is a command (an id, a title and a runnable) registered in one command registry (Editora's `Command` and `CommandRegistry`).

check.text: what a menu item, a toolbar button, a palette row or a key binding does is a registered command: the control runs the command's id through the registry, or calls what the command's runnable calls. No button, menu row or key handler does work no command can reach.

rules.reference: Editora [`command/Command.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/command/Command.java), [`command/CommandRegistry.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/command/CommandRegistry.java). Editora doesn't hold the rule everywhere yet: the Clear button of its Message Log ([`ui/MessageLogPopup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLogPopup.java)) empties the log in its own handler, and the Previous Run and Save Output buttons of its build console ([`ui/BuildToolPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/BuildToolPanel.java)) work the same way, with no command behind any of the three. Termina doesn't either. These buttons, among others, do their work in handlers of their own with no command behind them: Clear in its Message Log ([`ui/MessageLogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/MessageLogWindow.java)), Refresh, Copy, Export and Clear in its Debug Log ([`ui/DebugLogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/DebugLogWindow.java)), and Import theme in Settings ([`ui/SettingsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/SettingsWindow.java)).

rules.text: Command ids are dotted and grouped by area, as in `file.open`, `view.toggleStatusBar` and `help.reportProblem`. A rule that names a command's id requires that id; these three are examples.

check.text: every registered id is two or more names joined by dots, and the first is the area the command belongs to: `file.open`, and with a sub-area `git.log.checkout`.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/MenuBarModel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MenuBarModel.java).

rules.text: A command's title comes from `command.<id>` and its one-line palette description from `command.<id>.desc` in the message catalogs.
rules.why: a registered command is then localized and discoverable without extra work.

check.text: every registered command has a `command.<id>` and a `command.<id>.desc` key in the message catalogs, and the registry reads its title and description from them. A catalog parity test that walks the registered commands and fails on a missing key is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: the app template's [`CommandSweepFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/CommandSweepFxTest.java) (`everyCommandIsLocalizedAndRuns`) and Mirada's [`CommandCatalogTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/ui/CommandCatalogTest.java) (`everyCommandHasItsTitleAndDescriptionInTheCatalog`) walk the registered commands. rules.text: A command that cannot run in the current context is shown grayed, with a tooltip that says why, not hidden.

check.text: the palette and menus list a disabled command with a reason, rather than filtering it out.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/Chrome.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Chrome.java) (`paletteEnabled`, `disabledReason`). The app template's menu rows of a command that can't run stay, grayed, with the reason as their tooltip ([`ui/AppMenus.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AppMenus.java), `showAvailability`; [`RightClickMenusFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/RightClickMenusFxTest.java), `anUnavailableRowStaysAndSaysWhy`), and its palette lists such a command with the reason.

rules.text: The Command Palette opens with `M-x` in the Emacs keymap and `Ctrl+Shift+P` (`Cmd+Shift+P` on macOS) in the others; the IntelliJ keymap may use IntelliJ's own Find Action chord, `Ctrl+Shift+A` (`Cmd+Shift+A`), instead. An app with one key table and no Emacs keymap, which is a terminal app's own keymap ([KBD-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/keyboard/#kbd-09)) or the built-in table of an app that ships no keymap files, counts as one of the others: it binds `Ctrl+Shift+P` (`Cmd+Shift+P` on macOS). An app that ships no keymap files owes this chord and fails KBD-09 all the same: KBD-09 requires the files of every app.

check.text: each bundled keymap binds that chord to the palette command, and so does the one key table of an app that has no keymap files. An app whose chord opens the palette from a handler, with no palette command registered, passes this rule and fails [PAL-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/command-palette/#pal-01) for the missing command.

rules.text: The palette matches fuzzily over the command's title and over the words of its id or its keywords; the description is shown, not matched. A query that names a command's title outranks a fuzzy hit. Each row shows the command's binding in the active keymap. See the [Command Palette template](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/command-palette/).

check.text: the palette's matcher matches the query fuzzily against each command's title and finds a command by a word of its id or a keyword that its title doesn't carry; a query that spells a command's title ranks that command above the fuzzy hits; the description is drawn and never matched, and each row draws the binding the active keymap gives the command. A ranking test that asserts the order is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java) (`orderedMatches`), [`search/FuzzyMatch.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/search/FuzzyMatch.java). It scores the title first; when the title doesn't match, the id's namespace word as a keyword ([`Command.keywords`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/command/Command.java)); then the names IntelliJ and VS Code give the command ([`command/OtherIdeNames.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/command/OtherIdeNames.java)). It doesn't match the rest of the id or the description, which is shown under the list. [`CommandPaletteRankTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPaletteRankTest.java) holds the order (`aCommandIsFoundByItsNamespaceWhenItsTitleDoesNotCarryIt`, `aKeywordMatchRanksBelowEveryTitleMatch`, and for a typed title `anExactTitleLeadsAnotherCommandsAlias` and `aWholeOneWordTitleLeads`). The app template's [`ui/Picker.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Picker.java) (`rank`, with `idWords`) matches the title fuzzily and the id's words, never the description, and puts a title that holds the query first ([`PickerFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/PickerFxTest.java), `ranksTitlesFirstAndSkipsUnavailableRows`).

rules.text: The palette and every picker (a card that lists choices to filter and pick one from: [QOPEN-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/quick-open/#qopen-01)) are in-scene overlays in the window's root `StackPane`, never a `javafx.stage.Popup`.
rules.why: on Windows a Popup does not reliably take OS keyboard focus, and the whole app can stop receiving keystrokes.

check.text: the palette and every picker add their node to the root `StackPane`; none creates a `Popup`.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/OverlayHost.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/OverlayHost.java), the one host installed in the scene's root `StackPane`, which shows the palette ([`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java)), the picker ([`ui/QuickOpen.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpen.java)) and the picker's relatives ([QOPEN-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/quick-open/#qopen-12)).

rules.text: Except in a terminal app, Emacs and CUA keymaps ship as JSON resources, `emacs.json` and `cua.json`, CUA with a `cua.mac.json` variant where Cmd replaces Ctrl. A terminal's keys belong to the program it runs (`C-a`, `M-x` reach the shell), so a terminal app ships one keymap of its own instead, `keymap.json` and `keymap.mac.json`, binding its commands to chords programs don't use. Neither file binds a plain `Ctrl` or `Alt` (`Option` on macOS) with a letter: off macOS that leaves `Ctrl+Shift+T`, not `Ctrl+T`, and on macOS `Cmd+T`, since no program in the terminal receives `Cmd`.
rules.why: an Emacs keymap in a terminal would take the shell's own keys away from it: `Ctrl+W` deletes a word, `Ctrl+C` interrupts, `Alt+F` and `Alt+B` move by word. The shell reads the same keys on macOS, where `Option` with a letter also types a character.

check.text: `emacs.json`, `cua.json` and `cua.mac.json` are in the app's resources. In a terminal app, `keymap.json` and `keymap.mac.json` are there instead, and no default binding in either file is `Ctrl` alone or `Alt` alone with a letter. Read each chord as the OS reads it: a modifier that stands for the OS's own shortcut key (JavaFX's `Shortcut`, as Termina writes it) is `Ctrl` in `keymap.json` and `Cmd` in `keymap.mac.json`.

rules.reference: Editora [`src/main/resources/com/editora/keymaps/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/tree/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/keymaps); Termina's [`keymaps/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/tree/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/resources/com/termina/keymaps), whose [`KeymapTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/ui/KeymapTest.java) (`offMacOsAnApplicationChordNeverTakesPlainCtrlAndALetter`) holds the `Ctrl` half off macOS; no test holds the `Alt` half or reads `keymap.mac.json`, where every chord carries `Cmd` today.

rules.text: Except in a terminal app ([KBD-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/keyboard/#kbd-09)), an app also ships IntelliJ, VS Code and Sublime keymaps as JSON resources beside its Emacs and CUA keymaps: `intellij.json`, `vscode.json` and `sublime.json`, each with its `.mac.json` variant.

check.text: `intellij`, `vscode` and `sublime` `.json` and `.mac.json` files are in the resources. An app that ships a terminal's keymap, `keymap.json` and `keymap.mac.json` with no `emacs.json` and no `cua.json` ([KBD-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/keyboard/#kbd-09)), needs none of them.
check.command: [ -f pom.xml ] || { echo 'not an app root: no pom.xml here'; exit 1; }; has() { find src/main/resources -name "$1" | grep -q .; }; if has keymap.json && has keymap.mac.json && ! has emacs.json && ! has cua.json; then exit 0; fi; ! for k in intellij vscode sublime; do for f in "$k.json" "$k.mac.json"; do has "$f" || echo "missing $f"; done; done | grep .

rules.reference: Editora [`src/main/resources/com/editora/keymaps/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/tree/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/keymaps). Termina ships the terminal's two files only ([`keymaps/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/tree/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/resources/com/termina/keymaps)). The app template ships all five, each IDE keymap with its `.mac.json` (`PRESETS` in [`command/Keymap.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/command/Keymap.java)). Mirada ships Emacs and CUA and none of these three yet; Torrenta, Modula and nux ship no keymap file.

rules.text: A keymap's `.mac.json` variant binds the same commands as the keymap it varies. A chord may differ, to put `Cmd` where the other has `Ctrl`, to follow the macOS keymap of the editor it copies, or where macOS keeps the chord for itself (`Cmd+Space`, `Cmd+Tab`). See [Same on every OS](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/same-on-every-os/).
rules.why: a command with no chord on one OS is a command that user never finds from the keyboard.

check.text: each keymap file and its `.mac.json` variant bind the same set of command ids: no command is bound in one and missing from the other. An app that ships no keymap files has no pair to compare and fails with [KBD-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/keyboard/#kbd-09). A test that loads both and compares the commands they bind is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`KeymapsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/command/KeymapsTest.java) (`guiKeymapsBindSameCommandSetOnBothPlatforms`), Termina's [`KeymapTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/ui/KeymapTest.java) (`bothPlatformsBindTheSameCommands`) and the app template's [`KeybindingsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/command/KeybindingsTest.java) (`cuaHasAMacVariantWhereCmdReplacesCtrl`). Mirada's [`cua.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/resources/com/mirada/keymaps/cua.json) and [`cua.mac.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/resources/com/mirada/keymaps/cua.mac.json) bind the same commands, with no test that compares the two.

rules.text: Keymaps are applied in layers: base keymap → user overrides → plugin keymaps → the user's own bindings again. An app without plugins has the first two.
rules.why: the user always has the last word, and a plugin can still use a chord the user freed.

check.text: one place applies the layers in that order.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/KeymapLayers.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/KeymapLayers.java).

rules.text: A keymap editor in Settings lists every command with its chord, is searchable, and warns of conflicts.

check.text: open Settings → Keymap, search, and bind a chord that is taken.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/SettingsKeymapsPage.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsKeymapsPage.java); conflicts from [`KeybindingEdits.conflicts`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/command/KeybindingEdits.java), and the defaults a chord would take from [`EditorSettingsCoordinator.takenDefaults`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/EditorSettingsCoordinator.java).

rules.text: No command's chord is written into translated text. Every other label that shows a chord (a hint, the palette, the status bar) shows the binding from the active keymap; tooltips are [TBAR-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/toolbars-and-tooltips/#tbar-03) and menu rows [MENU-15](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/menus/#menu-15). Fixed keys of a control (Enter, Tab, Esc, arrows) and keys meant for another program may be written.

check.text: no message catalog value names a command's chord (`Ctrl+`, `Cmd+`, `C-x`, `M-x`); chords are rendered by one formatter.

rules.reference: Editora [`command/ChordFormat.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/command/ChordFormat.java), the one place a binding is rendered. Editora's `command.edit.universalArgument` title still carries `C-u`.

rules.text: A multi-key prefix (`C-x …`) shows a which-key style hint listing the possible next keys.

check.text: press `C-x` in the Emacs keymap and wait.

rules.reference: no app lists the next keys yet. Editora echoes only the pending prefix (`C-x -`) in the status bar ([`command/KeyDispatcher.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/command/KeyDispatcher.java)).

rules.text: Every interactive control is reachable with Tab and operable with Space or Enter. A control is the exception when the keyboard does what it does another way: the buttons of a toolbar stay out of the Tab order ([TBAR-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/toolbars-and-tooltips/#tbar-02), which says what a toolbar is: a bar of labeled buttons is not one, and its buttons are held to this rule), and the find-bar and filter controls that [FIND-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/find-bar/#find-16) names may leave it. See [Accessibility](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/accessibility/).
rules.why: a control that Tab can't reach is one a keyboard-only or screen-reader user can't use at all.

check.text: first in the source, find every control the keyboard cannot focus: one the app takes out of the Tab order (`setFocusTraversable(false)` in the code, `-fx-focus-traversable: false` in a stylesheet), and a label or a pane that acts on a click. The keyboard does all that each one does another way: it is a button of a toolbar as [The toolbar](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/toolbars-and-tooltips/#the-toolbar) defines one ([TBAR-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/toolbars-and-tooltips/#tbar-02); a bar of labeled buttons, such as nux's, is not one), a find-bar or filter control that [FIND-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/find-bar/#find-16) lets leave the Tab order (one that fails FIND-16, such as an option's toggle that no command toggles, fails here too), a list whose text field moves its selection with the arrow keys, or a control whose every action, the rows of its right-click menu included, a registered command also runs. A control only the mouse can work fails the rule, and the source alone shows it. Then in the running app, Tab reaches every other control of each window and dialog, and Space or Enter works it.

rules.reference: the app template, where each control the keyboard cannot focus has its other way: the status bar's echo area, error count and update notice run commands (`view.messageLog`, `help.openNewRelease`: [`ui/StatusBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/StatusBar.java)), its toolbar's buttons are [TBAR-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/toolbars-and-tooltips/#tbar-02)'s (`Icons.toolbarButton` in [`ui/Icons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Icons.java)), a tool window's header buttons run commands ([`ui/ToolWindowManager.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/ToolWindowManager.java)), the find bars' buttons are [FIND-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/find-bar/#find-16)'s ([`ui/FindBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/FindBar.java)), and the picker's list is moved from its field ([`ui/Picker.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Picker.java)). Editora doesn't hold the rule everywhere yet: the Clear button of its Message Log ([`ui/MessageLogPopup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLogPopup.java)) and the Previous Run and Save Output buttons of its build console ([`ui/BuildToolPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/BuildToolPanel.java)) are out of the Tab order with no command and no key behind them. Modula doesn't either: it takes every control of its window out of the Tab order ([`RadioPane.keepOutOfFocus`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/RadioPane.java)) and gives most of what they do a key or a palette row, but a preset's Rename and Remove are rows of its chip's right-click menu alone ([`ui/PresetBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/PresetBar.java)). Termina doesn't either: the regular-expression toggle of its find bar is out of the Tab order, and no command and no key toggles it ([`ui/SearchBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/SearchBar.java); [FIND-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/find-bar/#find-16) fails for it too).

rules.text: Every button, toggle, menu button, link, combo box, check box, radio button and text field shows the focus ring when the keyboard focuses it. The ring is one layer of `:focus-visible` rules in the app stylesheet, after every rule that sets a border or background on the same controls, since rules of equal specificity are decided by order. Its color and contrast are [ICON-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/icons-and-color/#icon-12).
rules.why: a keyboard user who can't see where focus is can't use the window; the ring's color is a MUST, and so is drawing it.

check.text: the app stylesheet holds the ring as one block of `:focus-visible` rules that covers each of these kinds of control the app uses (buttons, toggles, menu buttons, links, combo boxes, check boxes, radio buttons, text fields), and no rule after the block, of the same or higher specificity, sets again what the block sets on those controls (the border; on a text field, the background insets). A test that tabs to each control family and asserts the ring is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css) (*Keyboard focus*, one layer for every control), held by [`FocusRingFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/FocusRingFxTest.java), which tabs to each control family. Termina's [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/resources/com/termina/styles/app.css) and Mirada's [`mirada.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/resources/com/mirada/styles/mirada.css) end with a layer of the same kind; neither app has a test that tabs to a control.

rules.text: The focus ring is 2 px wide at the default zoom and sits just outside the control with a 1 px gap: a border with negative insets, which adds nothing to the control's own, so focusing a control never moves the layout. Two kinds of control draw it inside instead, at the same 2 px and still without moving anything: a text field, whose own focus border is widened, and a control flush with the window's edge, where a ring outside would be cut off.
rules.why: a ring drawn on the control's own border is lost on a flat or filled button, and one that takes room makes the row jump as Tab moves along it. A text field already draws an accent border on focus, so a second ring around it would be one too many.

check.text: in the `:focus-visible` rules of [KBD-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/keyboard/#kbd-16), the one for the controls that take the outside ring (buttons, toggles, menu buttons, links, combo boxes, the boxes of check boxes and radio buttons, as many of them as the app has) sets `-fx-border-width: 2` and `-fx-border-insets: -3`; the one for text fields widens the field's focus border to 2 px instead (`-fx-background-insets: 0, 2px`); and a rule that draws the ring inside a control at the window's edge keeps the 2 px width and takes the room back out of the control's padding.

rules.reference: Editora [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css) (*Keyboard focus*), Termina's [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/resources/com/termina/styles/app.css) and Mirada's [`mirada.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/resources/com/mirada/styles/mirada.css): the same outside ring, and the same text-field rule (Mirada's covers text areas too). Editora alone has the second exception: `.tool-stripe-button:focus-visible` draws the ring at `-fx-border-insets: 1` and gives 3 px of padding back, since the stripes sit against the window's edge. The app template's [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/styles/app.css) has the same outside ring and text-field rule; its check boxes and radio buttons take the ring around the whole control, label included, not around the box alone.

rules.text: A row that turns a setting on or off (in Settings, a panel or a dialog) uses a switch the keyboard operates: it takes focus, Space toggles it, and its accessible role is `TOGGLE_BUTTON`.
rules.why: a bare AtlantaFX `ToggleSwitch` is mouse-only.

check.text: every row that turns a setting on or off uses a switch that takes focus, toggles on Space and sets `AccessibleRole.TOGGLE_BUTTON` (Editora has one class for it, `SettingSwitch`); a row that uses AtlantaFX's `ToggleSwitch` as it comes fails.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/SettingSwitch.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingSwitch.java).

rules.text: Every control a person can reach with Tab or the mouse has an accessible name: its own text, a `Label` whose `labelFor` is the control, or `setAccessibleText`. A row drawn from a graphic (a `CustomMenuItem`, a list cell that lays out its own nodes) carries its text too. A test holds it.
rules.why: a screen reader announces an unnamed control as "button", or says nothing.

check.text: an FX test opens each window and dialog and fails on a control (a button, a toggle, a field, a combo box or any other `Control` a person can focus or click, in the Tab order or out of it) that has no text, no accessible text and no label pointing at it, and on a list cell or menu row that reads as nothing. JavaFX names a `CustomMenuItem` row from its content's accessible text, and a cell from its text or its graphic's, so a row that lays out its own nodes sets `setAccessibleText` on them.

rules.reference: Editora names its controls area by area ([`NamedControlsFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/NamedControlsFxTest.java)), and sets each row's text on the macOS system menu bar. Its in-window command rows, each a `CustomMenuItem` that draws an icon, a title and a chord ([`ui/MainMenuBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainMenuBar.java)), carry no text and no accessible text yet; its submenus keep their own. The app template has the test that sweeps every window for every control: [`NamedControlsFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/NamedControlsFxTest.java) (`everyControlInEveryWindowHasAName`, and `everyMenuRowReadsAsItsTitleAndWearsAGlyph` for the menu rows, which [`AppMenus.inWindowRow`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AppMenus.java) names from their title and chord) opens the main window and its panels, the find bars, the Message Log, Settings, About, the Pauta window, the Debug Log and Report a Problem, the palette, the switcher, a question and a prompt. Termina's [`IconOnlyButtonsFxTest.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/ui/IconOnlyButtonsFxTest.java) comes nearest: it opens the main window, the menus, Settings and About and fails an icon-only button with no name, and no other kind of control. Torrenta's one call to `setAccessibleText` is in a helper ([`ui/Icons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/Icons.java), `name`) that names every button of its main toolbar and the Search view's Clear button, and no other control; Modula never calls it.

rules.text: A control the app builds from panes or draws itself says what it is and does what its role offers: `setAccessibleRole` with the role it acts as (`BUTTON`, `TOGGLE_BUTTON`, `LIST_VIEW`, `TREE_ITEM`), its state answered from `queryAccessibleAttribute` (selected, expanded, checked), `notifyAccessibleAttributeChanged` when the state changes, and the role's actions (`FIRE`, `EXPAND`, `COLLAPSE`) handled in `executeAccessibleAction`.
rules.why: without a role, a screen reader can't tell a status-bar segment that opens a picker from a label; and it presses a control through its action, not a mouse click, so a `BUTTON` that ignores `FIRE` can be found but not used.

check.text: every `Pane`, `Region`, `Label` or `Canvas` that handles a click or a key sets an accessible role and overrides `executeAccessibleAction` for that role's actions.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/SettingSwitch.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingSwitch.java) (the `TOGGLE_BUTTON` role; it handles `FIRE` only) and [`ui/MapAccessibleRows.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MapAccessibleRows.java) (`FIRE`, `EXPAND` and `COLLAPSE` on each row). Its status-bar segments ([`ui/StatusBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/StatusBar.java)) take the `BUTTON` role but don't handle `FIRE` yet.

rules.text: An app that paints content on a `Canvas` (a map, a strip of images, a terminal grid) gives it to the screen reader: an accessible text that sums it up and, where a person moves through items in it, one accessible node for each item on screen.

check.text: the canvas, or the node that stands for it, sets an accessible text, and where a person moves through items it exposes a node with a role and a name for each item on screen. A test that reads the accessible text, or the roles and names of those nodes, is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/MapAccessibleRows.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MapAccessibleRows.java) (the Project Map's rows on screen, as `TREE_ITEM` nodes under a `TREE_VIEW`), read by [`MapAccessibleRowsFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/MapAccessibleRowsFxTest.java).

rules.text: Motion follows the OS: while `Platform.getPreferences().isReducedMotion()` is true, an animation jumps to its end, and a change to the setting applies at once.
rules.why: sliding and fading can make a person dizzy or sick, and they turned motion off in the OS for that reason.
