check.text: every `Transition`, `Timeline` or `AnimationTimer` that moves, fades or flashes part of the UI starts through one helper that reads `reducedMotionProperty()`.

rules.reference: no app reads the setting yet. The app template animates nothing, so it has nothing to judge: its timelines and pauses are timers that move, fade or flash no part of the UI (the Output sample's lines in [`ui/SamplePanels.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/SamplePanels.java), the debounce of [`ui/Debounce.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Debounce.java), the sync interval and the update check's delay). Mirada fades its on-screen controls in and out ([`ui/OnScreenControls.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/OnScreenControls.java), a `FadeTransition`), and Editora's Project Map flashes a revealed row for 900 ms ([`ui/MapSurface.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MapSurface.java), an `AnimationTimer`); neither reads a motion setting.

rules.text: Color is never the only signal: a state shown in color (an error, a changed line, a status) also shows a word, a glyph or a shape.
rules.why: about one man in twelve can't tell red from green.

check.text: look at a grayscale screenshot of each window and find every state still told apart.

rules.reference: Editora's echo area colors an error and also says what failed ([`ui/StatusBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/StatusBar.java); [WIN-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-01)). The app template gives a file's Git status its letter beside the color, on a tab ([`ui/TabHeaders.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/TabHeaders.java); [`TabsAndPanelsFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/TabsAndPanelsFxTest.java), `aTabShowsItsGitStatusAsALetter`) and on the file's row in its Documents window ([`ui/SamplePanels.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/SamplePanels.java)).

rules.text: In an app whose window has more than one region (the content and at least one panel beside it), a command moves focus to the next region, another moves it to the previous one, and every keymap binds both.
rules.why: Tab walks through every control inside a region; with several panels open, a keyboard user needs a way to jump between them.

check.text: the two commands are registered and bound in each bundled keymap.

rules.reference: the app template's `window.focusNextRegion` and `window.focusPreviousRegion` ([`ui/Commands.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Commands.java), `focusRegion` in [`ui/ToolWindowManager.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/ToolWindowManager.java)), on `F6` and `Shift+F6` in its CUA keymaps and `C-x o` and `C-x S-o` in Emacs, bound in every keymap it ships ([`TabsAndPanelsFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/TabsAndPanelsFxTest.java), `theRegionCommandsWalkTheDocumentsAndTheOpenToolWindows`). Editora's `window.other` ("Cycle focus between the editor and tool windows", [`ui/WindowCommandRegistrar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowCommandRegistrar.java)), one command that cycles, bound only in the Emacs keymap (`C-x o`, [`keymaps/emacs.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/keymaps/emacs.json)). `F6`, the Windows convention, is taken in every other Editora keymap: CUA and VS Code bind it to `debug.pause`, IntelliJ to `lsp.move` and Sublime to `view.toggleSpellCheck`.

rules.text: Before a release, a person makes a pass with the screen reader on Windows and on macOS: with Narrator and with VoiceOver, open the Command Palette, run a command, and move through Settings, hearing each control's name and role. It is a step of its own in `docs/release.md` ([REPO-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/repository/#repo-07)): the smoke test of [REL-29](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/release/#rel-29) is a CI step, with nobody there to listen.

check.text: `docs/release.md` has the step, naming Narrator and VoiceOver, and someone made the pass for this release. The file settles the first half: with no such step the rule is unmet, whoever listened. The pass itself is a person's to record, as a `checked` entry that carries the app's `version` ([PAUTA-18](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#pauta-18)).

rules.reference: no app yet. No app's `docs/release.md` names either screen reader, and Modula and nux have no `docs/release.md`.

rules.text: In an overlay list that keeps focus in its text field (the Command Palette, a picker: [QOPEN-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/quick-open/#qopen-01)), the row the arrow keys select is announced, with its state: the list tells the screen reader its focused item moved (`notifyAccessibleAttributeChanged(FOCUS_ITEM)`), and a row that can't run says so in its accessible text.
rules.why: the arrows move the highlight, not the focus, so a screen reader stays on the text field and reads nothing as the user moves through the list.

check.text: the code that moves the selection calls `notifyAccessibleAttributeChanged(AccessibleAttribute.FOCUS_ITEM)` on the list, the list answers `FOCUS_ITEM` with the selected row, and a row that can't run says so in its accessible text.

rules.reference: the app template's [`ui/Picker.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Picker.java), behind its palette and pickers: `select` moves the list's focus model and calls `notifyAccessibleAttributeChanged(FOCUS_ITEM)`, and a row's accessible text is its title, its keys and, for a row that can't run, the reason. Editora's palette rows are graphics with no text ([`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java)).

rules.text: In Windows' high-contrast mode the app switches to a high-contrast theme, and back when the mode ends: it follows `Platform.getPreferences()`'s `Windows.SPI.HighContrast`.
rules.why: JavaFX applies its own high-contrast stylesheet only over its built-in Modena theme, which AtlantaFX replaces, so without this the app ignores a setting the person turned on to read the screen at all.

check.text: a listener on the preference switches the theme, and the theme list has a high-contrast theme.

rules.reference: the app template's [`ui/Themes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Themes.java) (`WINDOWS_HIGH_CONTRAST`, a listener on `Platform.getPreferences()` that applies its `HIGH_CONTRAST` theme while the mode is on and the chosen one when it ends), held by [`StyleContrastTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/StyleContrastTest.java) (`theOsHighContrastModeWinsWhileItIsOn`, `theHighContrastThemeReadsAtSevenToOne`). No app does it yet.

rules.text: The main window has a status bar, shown by default; the user may hide it. Its left side is the *echo area*: one line of feedback for the last action, errors in red and warnings in amber. Clicking it opens the Message Log ([DIAG-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/diagnostics/#diag-01)).

check.text: the main window builds a status bar that is visible unless the user hid it; the echo label switches between an error and a warning style class, and its click handler runs the Message Log command.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/StatusBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/StatusBar.java) (`status-echo-error`, `status-echo-warn`; a click runs `view.messageLog`) and the [Message Log template](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/message-log/). Editora hides and shows the bar with `view.toggleStatusBar` and a setting, and Zen mode hides it ([`ui/Chrome.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Chrome.java), `statusBar`). Termina doesn't meet the rule yet: its status bar is a setting that starts off ([`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/config/Settings.java), `showStatusBar`).

rules.text: In an app with a menu bar, the menu bar sits in the title bar by default on Windows and Linux: JavaFX 27's `HeaderBar` with `StageStyle.EXTENDED` carries the menu, and a setting that starts on lets the user fall back to a decorated window. On macOS the menus are in the system menu bar (`useSystemMenuBar`), and the window is decorated, or extended with a header that holds no menus.
rules.why: the family looks the same on every OS only if every app starts with the same title bar; an app that ships it off looks like another family.

check.text: on Windows and Linux the main stage is created `StageStyle.EXTENDED` with a `HeaderBar` that holds the menu bar, and the setting that falls back to a decorated window defaults to on (in the title bar); on macOS the menu bar sets `useSystemMenuBar`, and a header, where the window has one, holds no menus.

rules.reference: the app template ([`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/Settings.java), `titleBarMenus = true`, read by [`Chrome.usesHeaderBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Chrome.java)). Editora ([`ui/ExtendedWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ExtendedWindow.java), [`ui/MainMenuBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainMenuBar.java)), Torrenta and Termina have the setting but start it off. Mirada has no setting: its [`ui/TitleBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/TitleBar.java) is a `HeaderBar` on a `StageStyle.EXTENDED` stage wherever JavaFX supports one, on macOS too. Its header holds the file name and buttons, the main menu's among them, and no menu bar; on macOS [`ui/MacMenus.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/MacMenus.java) puts the menus in the system menu bar. Modula and nux have no menu bar.

rules.text: Native dialogs go through one helper that attaches the app stylesheet. The UI font reaches every scene, a dialog's included, by [ICON-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/icons-and-color/#icon-01).
rules.why: a dialog is its own scene and does not inherit the window's stylesheet.

check.text: every `Alert` and `Dialog` the app builds passes through the helper.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/Dialogs.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Dialogs.java) ([`Dialogs.styled`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Dialogs.java)), which attaches `app.css` only. The UI font reaches an Editora dialog another way: [`App.installUiFont`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java) adds `ui-font.css` to every window's scene ([ICON-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/icons-and-color/#icon-01)).

rules.text: A dialog's buttons are in the same order on every OS, with Cancel to the left of every action, as the [Confirm dialog](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/confirm-dialog/) draws them (Cancel, Save and Discard where there are three: [CONF-05](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-05)): the dialog's `ButtonBar` gets one fixed order, never JavaFX's default for the OS. See [Same on every OS](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/same-on-every-os/).
rules.why: JavaFX orders a `ButtonBar` by the OS it runs on (`BUTTON_ORDER_WINDOWS`, `_MAC_OS`, `_LINUX`), so the same confirmation puts its action on the left on Windows and on the right on macOS and Linux.

check.text: the dialog helper ([WIN-04](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-04)), or each dialog, calls `setButtonOrder` on the dialog pane's `ButtonBar` with one order string, the same on every OS, in which `C` (`CANCEL_CLOSE`) comes before the letter of every action button the dialogs use (`O` for `OK_DONE`, `Y`, `N`, `A`, `U` for `OTHER`). `BUTTON_ORDER_WINDOWS` on every OS fails: it puts `Y`, `N` and `O` before `C`.

rules.reference: the app template's [`ui/Dialogs.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Dialogs.java) (`BUTTON_ORDER`, `L_HE+CUYNBXIAO_R`, set by `styled`, which every dialog of the template goes through), held by [`DialogsFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/DialogsFxTest.java) (`everyDialogHasOneButtonOrderAndCatalogWords`). Editora's Git confirmations give their buttons the `OK_DONE` and `CANCEL_CLOSE` roles and leave the order to JavaFX.

rules.text: The main window's size, position and maximized state are restored on the next launch, and in an app that opens documents or sessions, so are the items that were open. `--no-session` skipping the restore is [CLI-04](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/command-line/#cli-04).

check.text: closing the window saves its size, position and maximized flag, and the open items in an app that has them, and the next launch reads them back and applies them. A test that saves the state and reads it back is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`config/WorkspaceState.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/WorkspaceState.java) (`windowX` … `windowMaximized`), [`ui/WindowSessionCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowSessionCoordinator.java), [`App.noSessionFlag`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java); tests [`AppArgsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/AppArgsTest.java), [`NoSessionStartupFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/NoSessionStartupFxTest.java) and, for the window's geometry, [`WindowManagerLaunchFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/WindowManagerLaunchFxTest.java) (`aWindowComesBackAtTheSizeAndPlaceItsSessionRecorded`, `aWindowThatWasMaximizedComesBackMaximized`), which restore a window from a saved `workspace-state.json`. No Editora test saves the geometry and reads it back. The app template does both: `saveWindowState` in [`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MainWindow.java) writes the size, place, maximized state and the open documents to `session.json`, and the next launch restores them ([`ui/DocumentTabs.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/DocumentTabs.java); [`SessionAndWelcomeFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/SessionAndWelcomeFxTest.java), `theOpenDocumentsComeBackFromTheSessionFile`).

rules.text: In an app with content to zoom (text, an image, a terminal), it zooms from the keyboard (`Ctrl+=`, `Ctrl+-` and `Ctrl+0`, with `Cmd` on macOS; `=` is the key that carries `+`), kept across launches. The UI zoom is [WIN-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-12).

check.text: the content's zoom in, out and reset are commands bound in every keymap, and the zoom level is a saved setting.

rules.reference: Editora `view.textZoomIn`, `view.textZoomOut` and `view.textZoomReset`, kept in [`Settings.fontZoom`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/Settings.java) and bound to `C-=`, `C--` and `C-0` ([`keymaps/cua.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/keymaps/cua.json)); Termina's `zoomIn`, `zoomOut` and `actualSize`, on `Shortcut+Equals`, `Shortcut+Minus` and `Shortcut+0` ([`keymaps/keymap.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/resources/com/termina/keymaps/keymap.json)), kept in `font.zoom` ([`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/config/Settings.java)); the app template's `view.zoomIn`, `view.zoomOut` and `view.zoomReset` for its documents' text, bound to `Ctrl+=`, `Ctrl+-` and `Ctrl+0` (`Cmd` on macOS) in every keymap it ships and kept in `textZoom` ([`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/Settings.java); [`SessionAndWelcomeFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/SessionAndWelcomeFxTest.java), `theDocumentsTextZoomsOnItsOwn`).

rules.text: The app has a UI zoom: one setting scales the whole chrome, the menus ([MENU-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/menus/#menu-16)), toolbar, tabs and status bar included. It applies at once, is kept across launches, and three commands zoom it in, out and back to the default. In an app with content of its own to zoom (an editor's text, a terminal's grid, an image) `Ctrl+=`, `Ctrl+-` and `Ctrl+0` (`Cmd` on macOS) stay with the content zoom ([WIN-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-09)) and this rule fixes no chord for the UI zoom's commands; in an app without, those chords are the UI zoom's.
rules.why: a person who needs larger text gets it everywhere, and the menus can only follow a zoom that exists.

check.text: the chrome's font sizes come from one root size the setting changes, and its fixed sizes are multiplied by the zoom, not written as absolute pixels. A change to the setting restyles every open window with no restart, and the value is saved with the settings and read back at start-up. Three registered commands zoom it in, out and back to the default. The rule names no ids for them: they are the app's own. In an app with a content zoom they are three more commands, with ids that are not the content zoom's (Mirada's `view.zoomIn` and Termina's `zoomIn` zoom the content), and the keymaps bind `=`, `-` and `0` with `Ctrl` (`Cmd` on macOS) to the content zoom's commands; in an app without, to the UI zoom's.

rules.reference: the app template's [`ui/UiZoom.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/UiZoom.java) and [`ui/Themes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Themes.java) (`zoom`): one setting, `uiZoom` in [`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/Settings.java), scales every pixel size of the stylesheets, the root font size among them, and the sizes the code fixes are bound to the zoom; a change restyles every open window at once. Its commands are `view.uiZoomIn`, `view.uiZoomOut` and `view.uiZoomReset` ([`ui/Commands.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Commands.java)), on `Ctrl+Alt+=`, `Ctrl+Alt+-` and `Ctrl+Alt+0` (`Cmd+Alt` on macOS) in its CUA keymaps, which leave `Ctrl+=`, `Ctrl+-` and `Ctrl+0` to its documents' text zoom ([WIN-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-09)); [`UiZoomTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/UiZoomTest.java) holds the scaling. Editora, Termina and Mirada zoom their content only (`view.textZoomIn`, `zoomIn`, `view.zoomIn`), and Editora writes its menu font as absolute pixels ([`MainMenuBar.UI_FONT_SIZE`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainMenuBar.java), `.context-menu` in [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css)). Torrenta, Modula and nux have no zoom command.

rules.text: Every quit entry point an app has runs one quit method: the Quit row and the `app.quit` command ([WIN-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-14) says which of them an app must have), and the system's own Quit, which on macOS is the application menu's and the Dock's. That method asks what the [Confirm dialog](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/confirm-dialog/) rules require ([CONF-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-01)), closes open dialogs and runs the save the app runs when its window closes, so quitting loses nothing a close would have kept; what an app keeps across launches is [WIN-08](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-08). A tray's Quit is [TRAY-04](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/tray-and-background/#tray-04).
rules.why: a second way out skips what the first one does: the question about unsaved work, the saved window, or, in a tray app, the quit itself. Quitting from inside a dialog's nested event loop has aborted the JVM.

check.text: one quit method. The Quit row and the quit command run it, where the app has them (an app with neither fails [WIN-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-14), not this rule), and on macOS the system's Quit reaches it. JavaFX turns the application menu's and the Dock's Quit into a close request on every window (`GlassStage.requestClosingAllWindows`) unless the app catches Glass's quit action (`handleQuitAction`), so the quit handler calls the quit method, or, in an app with one main window, that window's close request does. In an app with one main window and no quit command, what the close request runs is the quit method, and it is judged as one; an app with several main windows whose close requests each ask for themselves has no quit method. The method itself asks before it discards anything [CONF-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-01) covers (unsaved work; an app with nothing to lose asks nothing), closes its open dialogs before it exits, and runs the same save a close of the window runs (the window state of [WIN-08](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-08), in an app that keeps it).

rules.reference: the app template's [`MainWindow.quit`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MainWindow.java): the `app.quit` command, which File → Quit runs, and the window's close request both call it, so macOS's Quit reaches it as a close request; it hides the other windows and dialogs, saves the window state and waits for the last settings write before it exits, and has nothing unsaved to ask about. That wait is the last save [PERF-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/performance/#perf-01) allows as the app quits; the template makes it on a background thread all the same. Editora's File → Quit and `app.quit` run [`MainController.onQuit`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java), which asks about the quit once and then about each window's unsaved files; macOS's Quit doesn't reach it yet: [`MacOpenFiles`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/MacOpenFiles.java) wraps Glass's handler and passes `handleQuitAction` on to JavaFX's own, so each window gets a close request and asks for itself. Torrenta ([`MainWindow.quit`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java)), Modula ([`ModulaApp.quit`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ModulaApp.java)) and nux (`Platform.exit`, from `app.quit` and from the tray, in [`App`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java)) don't catch macOS's Quit either. Termina and Mirada have no quit command ([WIN-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-14)). Mirada has one main window, and what its close request runs is its quit method: it asks about an unsaved edit, closes its tool windows and saves the window's place ([`ui/ViewerWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/ViewerWindow.java), `mayClose`, `release`, `rememberPlace`), and macOS's Quit arrives there as a close request. Termina doesn't meet the rule yet: it has several windows and no quit method, so macOS's Quit arrives at each window as a close request and each asks for itself ([`TerminalWindow.close`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalWindow.java)).

rules.text: Every app has a Quit, on every OS: the `app.quit` command, in the Command Palette, and, where the app has a File menu or a main menu, a Quit row in that menu that runs the command. A main menu is a menu button in the window that holds the app's commands as a menu bar would (Mirada's ☰, which it shows on every OS). A menu button that lists one kind of thing is not a main menu (nux's Profiles and Commands), and neither is a right-click menu (the only menu Modula has): an app with no File menu and no main menu meets the rule with the command alone. What Quit does is [WIN-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-13). Closing the last window may end the app as well, but it is never the only way out.
rules.why: someone who quits one app of the family from the palette or the File menu looks for the same in the next. An app that ends only with its last window has no answer once it has a tray or a second window.

check.text: `app.quit` is registered and the palette lists it. Where the app builds a File menu, a row of it runs `app.quit`; where it has no menu bar and a main menu instead, a row of that menu does. An app with neither menu passes on the command.

rules.reference: the app template's [`Commands.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Commands.java) (`app.quit`) and [`AppMenus.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AppMenus.java) (Quit, the File menu's last row); Editora's `app.quit`, the last row of its File menu ([`ui/MenuBarModel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MenuBarModel.java)). Torrenta's File menu ends with Quit, and it registers the command as `quit`. Termina and Mirada have no Quit. Termina's File menu has Close Window and ends with Settings, Sync Now and Configure Profiles ([`ui/MenuBarModel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/MenuBarModel.java)); Mirada's ☰ menu, on every OS ([`ui/TitleBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/TitleBar.java)), and, on macOS, its File menu ([`ui/MacMenus.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/MacMenus.java)) end with Close (`window.close`). nux has neither menu and meets the rule with `app.quit` ([`App`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java)). Modula has neither menu and no quit command: it quits from its tray and its window's close button ([`ModulaApp.quit`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ModulaApp.java)).

rules.text: On macOS, Settings is in the application menu, the one macOS names after the app, and runs the same command as the Settings row on Windows and Linux. Its row shows the chord the active keymap binds to that command (`Cmd+,` in the CUA keymap: [SET-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/settings/#set-01)), appended to the title as [MENU-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/menus/#menu-02) has the system menu bar's rows show theirs, and the item is given no key equivalent of its own. About, in the same menu, is [ABOUT-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/about/#about-01), and the Quit JavaFX puts there is [WIN-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-13).
rules.why: it is where every Mac app has Settings, one of the places [the OS's way wins](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/same-on-every-os/#where-the-oss-way-wins). A key equivalent set on the item is an accelerator under another name: macOS runs the item before the app's key dispatcher sees the key, and the menu goes on showing `⌘,` in a keymap that binds another chord, or none.

check.text: on macOS the app inserts a Settings item into the application menu that runs the settings command. The item's title carries the chord the active keymap binds to that command and is written again when the keymap changes; the item is created without a key equivalent.

rules.reference: Mirada [`MacAppMenu.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/os/MacAppMenu.java) adds the item, and it runs `app.settings`. It doesn't show the keymap's chord yet: it creates the item with the native key equivalent `Cmd+,` (`createMenuItem(…, ',', COMMAND)`), which stays whatever the keymap binds, and Mirada's Emacs keymap binds `C-,` ([`keymaps/emacs.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/resources/com/mirada/keymaps/emacs.json)). The app template's [`ui/MacAppMenu.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MacAppMenu.java) meets it: it inserts a Settings item that runs `app.settings`, created with no key equivalent, whose title carries the keymap's chord and is written again on a keymap change (`refresh`, from [`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MainWindow.java)). Termina's [`MacAppMenu.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/MacAppMenu.java) adds About only. Editora, Torrenta, Modula and nux add nothing to that menu.

rules.text: The window has modes that change how much chrome it shows: Zen shows none, Expert keeps only the status bar, and Simple shows fewer menus, for new users.

check.text: each mode is a command, and one truth table decides which chrome each mode shows.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/WindowChromeCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowChromeCoordinator.java) (`toggleZen`, `toggleExpert`, `applySimpleMode`) over the truth table in [`ui/Chrome.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Chrome.java), where Expert hides the menu bar, the toolbar, the tabs, the breadcrumb and the tool stripes (`menuBar` keys on both focus modes; in an extended window the title and the window buttons stay).

rules.text: Inter is attached by a *scene* stylesheet on every window's scene, dialogs, popups and tooltips included, not by a rule in the app stylesheet.
rules.why: dialogs, the Settings window, the palette, context menus and tooltips each live in a scene of their own that does not share `app.css`, and a scene sheet is re-applied cleanly when the theme switches at run time (`setUserAgentStylesheet`). AtlantaFX neither bundles nor names Inter, and JavaFX does not fall through a font-family list, so without the sheet the whole interface renders in the platform's "System" face.

check.text: every window's scene gets the font sheet (Editora's `ui-font.css`): a listener on `Window.getWindows()` adds it to each window's scene, and to a new scene when the window's scene changes, or every window and dialog the app builds adds it itself, none left out. A popup or a tooltip needs no call of its own: when JavaFX shows one, it gives it the scene stylesheets of the window it is shown from (`PopupWindow.applyStylesheetFromOwner`). No `.root` rule in the app stylesheet (Editora's `app.css`) sets `-fx-font-family`.

rules.reference: Editora [`App.installUiFont`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java), a listener on `Window.getWindows()`, and [`styles/ui-font.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/ui-font.css); the app template's [`ui/Themes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Themes.java) (`installUiFont`, `hookUiFont`) and Mirada's [`ui/Fonts.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Fonts.java) (`installSheet`) do the same. Termina and Torrenta carry the same sheet with no listener: each window and dialog adds it by calling `Fonts.installUiFont`, about forty times in Torrenta. Termina doesn't meet the rule yet: its helper is called for seven windows and [`ui/Confirm.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/Confirm.java) adds the sheet to its questions, but four dialogs get none: the two alerts and the rename-tab `TextInputDialog` built in [`ui/TerminalWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalWindow.java), and the `TextInputDialog` in [`ui/SettingsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/SettingsWindow.java). Modula doesn't yet: the `.root` rule of its [`modula.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/resources/com/modula/modula.css) sets IBM Plex Mono for the whole window.

rules.text: The app bundles Inter's four faces and registers them before any CSS is applied; it never maps the platform's own UI font.
rules.why: an earlier macOS-only sheet used San Francisco, which JavaFX faux-bolds; Inter has a real bold on every platform.

check.text: `Inter-Regular`, `Inter-Bold`, `Inter-Italic` and `Inter-BoldItalic` `.ttf` are under the app's `fonts/inter/` with their `OFL.txt`, and `Font.loadFont` runs on them before the first window is shown.

rules.reference: Editora [`src/main/resources/com/editora/fonts/inter/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/tree/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/fonts/inter), [`ui/Fonts.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Fonts.java) (`loadForFirstPaint`, called from [`App`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java)). Termina and Torrenta bundle the same four faces. Modula doesn't yet: its [`fonts/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/tree/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/resources/com/modula/fonts) holds IBM Plex Mono only.

rules.text: A theme file follows the vendored AtlantaFX community themes: a `.root` block of `-color-*` tokens, then component rules that reference only those tokens.

check.text: the file's first rule is `.root`, and no rule after it holds a `#` hex.

rules.reference: Editora [`styles/atlantafx-themes/editora-light.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/atlantafx-themes/editora-light.css), `editora-dark.css`.

rules.text: A new app ships the Caret & Ink pair as its default theme, with `editora-light.css` and `editora-dark.css` copied unchanged into its own `styles/`.
rules.why: the palette is the family's, not the editor's.

check.text: the app's two files are identical to Editora's.

rules.reference: Termina [`styles/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/tree/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/resources/com/termina/styles) and the app template's [`styles/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/tree/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/styles), whose two files match Editora's. Torrenta's `editora-dark.css` matches too; its [`editora-light.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/resources/com/torrenta/styles/editora-light.css) still has the earlier `-color-accent-fg`, `-color-warning-fg` and `-color-success-fg`, which Editora has since darkened.

rules.text: Brace, the palette's periwinkle for the keyboard (chord chips, the menus' chord column), is one token on `.root` (Editora's `-state-key`): a `ladder()` over `-color-bg-default` that picks a deep ink on a light ground and a lighter periwinkle the darker the ground gets, and reads at 4.5:1 or more on every bundled theme's default and subtle surfaces.
rules.why: Brace has no AtlantaFX role, so it has to be a literal.

check.text: the token is a `ladder()` of `-color-bg-default`, and the color it resolves to on each bundled theme's default and subtle grounds is 4.5:1 or more against that ground. A contrast test that resolves the ladder against every bundled theme's grounds is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css) (`.root`), [`StyleContrastTest.theKeyboardPeriwinkleReadsOnEveryBundledAppTheme`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/StyleContrastTest.java).

rules.text: Each state color is named once, as a token on `.root` (Editora's `-state-*`) that chains to one of the theme's roles (or a `ladder()` of its ground), and component rules use the token.

check.text: each state color has one token (Editora's `-state-*`), declared once, in a `.root` block of the app stylesheet, as a `-color-*` role or a `ladder()` of the ground. A component rule that colors one of those states uses the token: none names the role behind it (`-color-danger-fg` for an error) or writes the ladder out again.

rules.reference: the app template's [`styles/app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/styles/app.css) (`.root`), held by [`StyleContrastTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/StyleContrastTest.java) (`theStateTokensAreDeclaredOnceAtTheTopAndChainToARole`, and `severityColorsComeFromTheStateTokens`, which fails a component rule that names a danger, warning or success role). Termina meets it too: its [`styles/app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/resources/com/termina/styles/app.css) declares `-state-red`, `-state-amber` and `-state-green` on `.root`, and no component rule of its stylesheets names the role behind one. The other five apps don't yet. Editora's [`styles/app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css) declares its tokens the same way (`.root`), but Editora doesn't hold the last clause: 79 declarations in that file's component rules name `-color-danger-fg`, `-color-warning-fg` or `-color-success-fg` directly, errors among them (`.crontab-error`, `.md-math-error`). Torrenta's tokens are on `.root` too (`-torrenta-*`), and two of its component rules write out the ladder of `-torrenta-up` again ([`styles/app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/resources/com/torrenta/styles/app.css), `.speed-graph-up`, `.speed-graph-legend-up`). Torrenta doesn't hold the last clause either: 24 declarations in that file's component rules and five in `add-dialog.css` name `-color-danger-fg`, `-color-warning-fg` or `-color-success-fg` directly (`.port-dot.port-down`, `.add-fetch-failed`), not the `-torrenta-error`, `-torrenta-stall` and `-torrenta-done` tokens that chain to them. Mirada and nux have no token for a state (Mirada's one `-state-*` token is `-state-key`, the keyboard's): Mirada's [`styles/mirada.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/resources/com/mirada/styles/mirada.css) redefines the roles themselves on `.root`, as ladders, and four of its component rules name `-color-danger-fg` or `-color-warning-fg` (`.status-echo-error`, `.status-echo-warn` and the Message Log's two); nux's [`nux.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/resources/com/nux/nux.css) has no `.root` block, and three of its rules name `-color-warning-fg` or `-color-danger-fg` (`.on-battery-note`, `.settings-problem`, `.detail-warn`). Modula's [`modula.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/resources/com/modula/modula.css) has tokens its rules use (`-lock`, `-fault`), set as fixed hexes on `.root` and again on `.root.daylight`, chained to no role.

rules.text: App stylesheets take their colors from AtlantaFX `-color-*` tokens, or from tokens the app builds on them; no component rule carries a fixed color, whatever its spelling: a hex, an `rgb()`, `rgba()` or `hsb()` value, or a named color such as `white`. A fixed color may stand only in a token's definition, on `.root` or in a scoped block that sets `-color-*` tokens, and only where the theme has no role to build on: a scrim's or a shadow's color, a color drawn over an image or a canvas and not on the theme's ground, or a color inside a `ladder()` of the ground ([ICON-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/icons-and-color/#icon-13)). The ground, ink or accent of the app's own windows given there as a fixed color, in place of the theme's role, fails this rule; a state color given so is [ICON-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/icons-and-color/#icon-07)'s failure and is not counted here again. `transparent` is not a color.
rules.why: a fixed color suits one theme; the roles track every theme for free.

check.text: every color in a component rule of the app's stylesheets is an AtlantaFX `-color-*` role or a token, and a fixed color stands only where a token is defined, in a `.root` block or in a scoped block that sets `-color-*` tokens: as the plain value of a token for a scrim, a shadow or what is drawn over an image or a canvas (an `rgba()` of black, say), or inside a `ladder()` of the ground. A token for the ground, ink or accent of the app's own windows whose value is a fixed color and no role fails; a state color's token with no role behind it is [ICON-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/icons-and-color/#icon-07)'s to judge, not this rule's. A fixed color is a hex (`grep -nE '#[0-9a-fA-F]{3,8}\b'` over those stylesheets lists them), an `rgb()`, `rgba()`, `hsb()` or `hsba()` value, or a named color such as `white`; `transparent` is not one. No component rule holds one, whichever property it sets (a `-fx-*-color`, a `-fx-fill`, an effect's color), inside a `ladder()` or not. A test that fails a fixed color outside the token block is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Termina's [`AppCssColorsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/ui/AppCssColorsTest.java) (`componentRulesUseTokensNotLiteralColours`) and Mirada's [`StyleContrastTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/ui/StyleContrastTest.java) (`noRuleAfterTheTokenBlockHoldsAFixedColour`) fail a fixed color outside the `.root` block: a hex, an `rgb()` or an `hsb()` value, a shadow's color included, and in Mirada's a named color too. Both apps keep the scrim behind an overlay and their shadows' colors as tokens on `.root`, and so does the app template: `-scrim` and `-shadow` on `.root` in its [`styles/app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/styles/app.css), used by `.overlay-backdrop` and the cards' shadows, with no test that holds it. Editora's [`StyleContrastTest.severityAndDebugColoursComeFromTheStateTokens`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/StyleContrastTest.java) holds six selectors it names, and Editora doesn't yet pass the whole check: `.breakpoint-marker`, `.debug-menu-logpoint`, `.exec-arrow`, `.view-mode-bar`, `.recent-remove`, `.personal-note-tooltip-content`, the fold-gutter markers and the default editor and Markdown preview palettes in [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css) still carry fixed hexes, other rules an `rgba()` (the scrim of `.overlay-backdrop`, the diff and merge tints and shadows among them), and `.breakpoint-condition-mark` a fixed `white`. Torrenta doesn't either: `.speed-graph-up` and `.speed-graph-legend-up` in its [`styles/app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/resources/com/torrenta/styles/app.css) hold a ladder of two hexes, and `.palette-backdrop` and two shadows an `rgba()`. Modula and nux write the palette's scrim as an `rgba()` background in a component rule, and a shadow's color the same way (`.palette-backdrop` and `.palette-card` in [`modula.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/resources/com/modula/modula.css) and [`nux.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/resources/com/nux/nux.css)), so neither meets the rule yet; nux also sets `-fx-text-fill: white` on `.status-pill` and `.update-badge`.

rules.text: Readable text uses `-color-fg-muted` or stronger, which is 4.5:1 on the default, subtle and overlay grounds in both flagship themes, Editora Light and Editora Dark: a line of UI text is `-color-fg-default` and secondary text `-color-fg-muted`. `-color-fg-subtle` (2.7:1 to 3.9:1, under 3:1 on Editora Light's subtle and inset grounds) is for disabled or decorative text only. An app whose default light and dark themes are another pair is held to the same on that pair. A test holds it.

check.text: a contrast test computes muted ink on the default, subtle and overlay grounds of both flagship themes (Editora Light and Editora Dark), or of the app's own default light and dark themes where it ships another pair, and finds 4.5:1 or more; and it walks every rule of the app's stylesheets: it fails a rule that sets a text fill (`-fx-text-fill`, or `-fx-fill` on text) to `-color-fg-subtle` unless its selector is on a list the test names, of disabled and decorative selectors only. A test that checks a list of readable selectors instead passes every selector it doesn't name.

rules.reference: only the app template's test walks every rule. Editora's [`StyleContrastTest.textThatMustBeReadUsesTheMutedRoleNotSubtle`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/StyleContrastTest.java) computes the ratios and checks six selectors it names (the palette's and the switcher's hints, an unbound shortcut, the line numbers of the notes and structure trees, the blame date), so it passes while `.encryption-locked-hint` and `.pom-version-unknown` in [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css) set text a person reads in `-color-fg-subtle`. The app template's test of the same name ([`StyleContrastTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/StyleContrastTest.java)) walks every rule of its `app.css` and both themes and fails a text fill in `-color-fg-subtle` on any selector but the disabled and decorative ones it lists (`SUBTLE_TEXT`), and computes the muted role's ratio on the grounds of both themes. Mirada's [`StyleContrastTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/ui/StyleContrastTest.java) has no test for this rule, and Termina, Torrenta, Modula and nux have no contrast test of their stylesheets.

rules.text: Text in a role's tint (the theme's `-color-<role>-fg`, for the accent, success, warning and danger roles) reaches 4.5:1 on that role's subtle fill (`-color-<role>-subtle`) and on the default and subtle grounds (`-color-bg-default`, `-color-bg-subtle`), in both flagship themes, Editora Light and Editora Dark, or, in an app whose default light and dark themes are another pair, in that pair. A test holds it.

check.text: a contrast test computes each role's `-fg` on its `-subtle`, on `-color-bg-subtle` and on `-color-bg-default`, in both flagship themes (Editora Light and Editora Dark), or in the app's own default light and dark themes where it ships another pair, and finds 4.5:1 or more.

rules.reference: Editora [`StyleContrastTest.lightTintedTextReachesAaOnItsOwnGroundAndOnTheSubtleSurface`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/StyleContrastTest.java), `darkTintedTextStaysAa`. Mirada's [`StyleContrastTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/ui/StyleContrastTest.java) (`tintedTextReachesAaOnItsOwnFillAndOnBothGrounds`) holds it on Cupertino Light and Cupertino Dark, the pair it ships.

rules.text: Ink on an emphasis fill is `-color-fg-emphasis`, never a fixed white: the token is white in the light themes and a dark ink in the dark ones, 4.5:1 or more on the emphasis fill of the accent, success, warning and danger roles in the two themes [ICON-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/icons-and-color/#icon-09) names. A test holds it.
rules.why: white on the dark accent is 1.68:1.

check.text: a contrast test computes `-color-fg-emphasis` on the `-emphasis` fill of the accent, success, warning and danger roles, in both flagship themes (Editora Light and Editora Dark) or in the app's own default light and dark themes where it ships another pair, and finds 4.5:1 or more; and the rules that paint on an emphasis fill use it.

rules.reference: Editora [`StyleContrastTest.inkOnAnEmphasisFillIsTheThemesOnEmphasisColour`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/StyleContrastTest.java), and Mirada's test of the same name ([`StyleContrastTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/ui/StyleContrastTest.java)), on Cupertino Light and Cupertino Dark: each holds 4.5:1.

rules.text: One focus ring color, the theme's `-color-accent-emphasis`, named once on `.root` (Editora's `-focus-ring`) and drawn by the `:focus-visible` block in the app stylesheet ([KBD-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/keyboard/#kbd-16)), at 3:1 or better on every surface: the default, subtle, inset and overlay grounds of the two themes [ICON-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/icons-and-color/#icon-09) names (see [Keyboard first](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/keyboard/)). A test holds it.

check.text: a test reads the ring's token from `.root` (Editora's `-focus-ring`) and computes it on the default, subtle, inset and overlay grounds of both flagship themes (Editora Light and Editora Dark), or of the app's own default light and dark themes where it ships another pair, and finds 3:1 or more.

rules.reference: Editora [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css) (*Keyboard focus*), [`StyleContrastTest.theFocusRingIsAtLeastThreeToOneOnEverySurface`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/StyleContrastTest.java).

rules.text: A state color the AtlantaFX theme has no role for (Editora's Git olive and violet) is a `ladder()` of `-color-bg-default`, never one fixed hex for light themes and another for dark. Brace, the periwinkle, is [ICON-06](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/icons-and-color/#icon-06).
rules.why: the old fixed light hexes read at 3.2:1 on Editora Dark.

check.text: each such token is declared as a `ladder()` of `-color-bg-default`; none is a fixed hex, or a pair of hexes switched by theme. A contrast test that resolves each ladder on every bundled theme's ground is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css) (`-state-olive`, `-state-violet`, `-state-key`), [`StyleContrastTest.theGitOliveAndVioletFollowTheAppThemesGround`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/StyleContrastTest.java).

rules.text: The contrast tests are pure: they read the stylesheets and do the WCAG arithmetic without starting the toolkit, so they run with the unit tests on every OS.
rules.why: a test that starts the toolkit is an FX test, tagged and run apart from the unit tests ([QUAL-06](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/quality/#qual-06)); a pure one fails the plain unit run on every OS, the first time a color changes.

check.text: every test class that computes a contrast ratio reads the app's `.css` resources as text and starts no toolkit: none is an FX test.

rules.reference: the app template's [`StyleContrastTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/StyleContrastTest.java) and Mirada's [`StyleContrastTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/ui/StyleContrastTest.java): each reads the stylesheets as text and uses `javafx.scene.paint.Color` for the arithmetic alone. The template's key color is held there too (`theKeyColorReadsOnBothThemesGrounds`), and no FX test of its computes a contrast. Mirada's [`AccentTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/ui/AccentTest.java) is pure too, over the accent it derives from the system's, and so is Termina's [`ThemeTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/ui/ThemeTest.java), which holds the colors of its terminal schemes and not the chrome's stylesheet. Editora's [`StyleContrastTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/StyleContrastTest.java) is pure as well, but Editora doesn't meet the rule yet: FX tests compute contrast ratios on rendered nodes too, [`ChordChipThemeFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/ChordChipThemeFxTest.java), [`DebugValuePopupThemeFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/DebugValuePopupThemeFxTest.java) and [`SettingsFrameFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsFrameFxTest.java) among them.

rules.text: The app has light and dark themes and switches between them at run time, without a restart.

check.text: the app has a light theme and a dark one, and picking a theme calls `Application.setUserAgentStylesheet` in the running app.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/Themes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Themes.java) (`applyAppTheme`).

rules.text: The theme setting offers "follow the system": a choice that applies the light or dark theme to match the system's color scheme, and changes with it.

check.text: the theme setting has a system value, the place where the user picks a theme lists it, and while it is chosen a listener on `Platform.getPreferences().colorSchemeProperty()` re-applies the theme.

rules.reference: Mirada [`settings/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/settings/Settings.java) (`ThemeChoice.SYSTEM`), [`ui/Theme.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Theme.java); nux [`config/Advanced.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/config/Advanced.java) (`THEME_SYSTEM`), [`ui/Theme.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/Theme.java); Termina [`ui/Themes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/Themes.java) (`SYSTEM_ID`, `followSystem`), with the listener in [`ui/WindowManager.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/WindowManager.java); the app template's [`ui/Themes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Themes.java) (`ThemeChoice.SYSTEM`). Each lists the choice in its Settings. Editora, Torrenta and Modula don't offer it yet: Editora's and Torrenta's pickers list named themes only ([`ui/Themes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Themes.java), Torrenta's [`ui/Theme.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/Theme.java)), and Modula's theme is one on/off setting, `daylight` ([`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/config/Settings.java)).

rules.text: A theme name the app does not know falls back to the first-run default theme.

check.text: the lookup from a saved name to a theme ends in the default, not an exception.

rules.reference: Editora [`Themes.themeFor`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Themes.java), falling back to [`Themes.DEFAULT`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Themes.java) (Editora Light).

rules.text: The state colors never decorate: in every theme amber means "not durable yet", a warning ([WIN-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-01) requires a warning in the echo area in amber) or an update available in About ([ABOUT-10](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/about/#about-10) asks for it there), red "broken" and green "verified", and nothing is colored amber, red or green for any other reason. A theme may change the accent, the ground and the ink, never these meanings.

check.text: every rule that uses the amber, red or green state token (Editora's `-state-amber`, `-state-red` and `-state-green`) marks one of the meanings in the table under [State colors](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/icons-and-color/#state-colors).

rules.reference: Editora [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css).

rules.text: In an app whose icons come in two families, one colored by its stroke and one by its fill, a glyph node carries the style class of one family, never both (Editora's two are `icon-line` and `toolbar-icon`). An app with one icon family, or with no icons in its window, has nothing to mix.
rules.why: a line glyph is colored by its stroke, and any `X .toolbar-icon` fill rule (there are dozens) would paint its outline solid. A glyph that moves family moves its CSS with it.

check.text: the method that builds a line glyph adds the line family's class alone, the one that builds a filled glyph adds the filled family's alone (Editora's `Icons.line` and `Icons.of`), and no other code adds the second class to a glyph node. A test that builds every glyph and fails when one carries both classes is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/Icons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Icons.java) (`line`, `of`) and [`editor/MenuIcons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/MenuIcons.java), whose glyphs [`MenuIconFamilyFxTest.aLineGlyphIsNeverAlsoTaggedAsAFilledOne`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/MenuIconFamilyFxTest.java) holds. Torrenta's [`IconsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/test/java/com/torrenta/ui/IconsTest.java) (`everyGlyphIsAStyledScaledPath`) builds every glyph and fails one that carries both classes or neither. Termina, Mirada and Modula draw one family each.

rules.text: The same action wears the same glyph wherever it is reached: Save is one floppy on the toolbar, in the File menu and in a tab's menu.

check.text: wherever an action is drawn (a toolbar button, a menu row, a tab's menu), its glyph comes from one icon class or one lookup keyed by the command. Where a second icon class holds a copy of its own, the copy has the same path data and style class. A test that compares the path data and style class of each action's glyph across the icon classes is the surest evidence. An app that draws no glyph anywhere has nothing to compare and passes; its missing icons are [MENU-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/menus/#menu-14)'s.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/MenuBarIcons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MenuBarIcons.java) reuses [`Icons`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Icons.java); [`editor/MenuIcons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/MenuIcons.java) (the editor package may not depend on `ui`) copies each twin's family and path data verbatim, held by [`MenuIconFamilyFxTest.everySharedActionUsesTheSameGlyphInBothIconSets`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/MenuIconFamilyFxTest.java). Mirada gives a command's menu row and its button one glyph from one lookup ([`ui/Icons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Icons.java), `forCommand`).

rules.text: In an app that shows files with an icon each (a project tree, file tabs, a list of files), a file's icon comes from a pure function from file name to icon key, unit-tested without the toolkit, and any type it does not know gets the generic document glyph, so a new type never regresses the look.

check.text: a unit test resolves names to keys, an unknown one to the generic key.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/FileIcons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/FileIcons.java): `iconKeyFor(name)` resolves the key, `forFileName` turns it into a node; brand logos from Simple Icons, category glyphs (image, archive, PDF, table, lock, JSON, settings) from Material. [`FileIconsTest.unknownAndNullFallBackToGeneric`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/FileIconsTest.java).

rules.text: Every glyph set and font the app ships is credited in `NOTICE` with its license.

check.text: each icon source named in the icon classes and each family under `fonts/` has an entry in `NOTICE`. An app that ships no glyph set and no font has nothing to credit here.

rules.reference: Editora [`NOTICE`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/NOTICE): Material Design Icons (Apache-2.0), Simple Icons (CC0; the logos stay their owners' trademarks), Inter and the monospace faces (OFL), and the glyph sets inside the bundled Symbols Nerd Font, Octicons and Seti UI (MIT) among them.

rules.text: Every icon-only button, one that shows a glyph or a symbol such as "?" or "···" and no word, has a name: one helper sets its tooltip and its accessible text from the same string, the chord included where the tooltip carries one ([TBAR-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/toolbars-and-tooltips/#tbar-03)), so a screen reader says what a sighted user reads.
rules.why: a hand-rolled button gets the tooltip and forgets the name, which is how Editora once had seven copies of the helper drifting apart, and how a screen reader comes to announce "button".

check.text: every icon-only button gets its tooltip and its accessible text in one call that sets both from one string (Editora's `Icons.button`, `Icons.toolbarButton` and `Icons.name`). A button with a `setTooltip` and no `setAccessibleText` fails, and so does one whose tooltip is written again later, to add a chord, while its accessible text keeps the first string.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/Icons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Icons.java) (`button`, `toolbarButton`, `name`), used by its panel toolbars. Torrenta's copy of all three ([`ui/Icons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/Icons.java)): its `name` is the one place Torrenta sets an accessible text, and it names every button of the main toolbar ([`MainWindow.toolButton`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java)) and names them again when the keys change. Termina's [`ui/IconNames.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/IconNames.java) (`name`), which binds both to one string. Five apps don't meet it yet. Editora sets the tooltip only on its main toolbar ([`WindowToolbar.setupButton`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowToolbar.java) and [`ToolbarCoordinator.buildExtraButton`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolbarCoordinator.java)) and on the floating buttons that leave Zen and Expert mode and bring the toolbar back ([`WindowChromeCoordinator.installZenOverlay`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowChromeCoordinator.java)), and its stripe buttons' accessible text is the tool window's title without the chord the tooltip carries ([`ToolWindowManager.register`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindowManager.java)). Torrenta's detail pane gives its "···" button a tooltip and no accessible text ([`ui/DetailPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/DetailPane.java)). Mirada's [`ui/Icons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Icons.java) (`button`, `name`) makes the accessible text the command's title and puts the chord in the tooltip only. nux's [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java) sets the tooltip and the accessible text of its "?" button from one string, then its `shortcut` helper writes the tooltip again as "About Nux  (F1)" and leaves the accessible text. Modula's transport, Settings and Record buttons have a tooltip and no accessible text ([`ui/RadioPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/RadioPane.java)), and so has the "+" button of its preset row ([`ui/PresetBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/PresetBar.java)).

rules.text: The tooltip of a button that runs a command names the command and its chord, read from the active keymap and never typed into a string: "Save (C-x C-s)". The name is the command's title ([KBD-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/keyboard/#kbd-03)), which a tooltip may show without its category prefix, as a menu row may ([MENU-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/menus/#menu-01)): "Save" for "File: Save". An unbound command shows its title alone.

check.text: the tooltip shows the command's title, whole or without its category prefix, and the keymap's display chord for its id, and is rebuilt when the keymap changes. The chord is the one of the command the button runs, and no chord is typed into the string. A fixed key of the control itself (Enter in a find field) is no command's chord and may be written, as [KBD-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/keyboard/#kbd-13) allows.

rules.reference: Editora [`ToolbarCoordinator.buildExtraButton`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolbarCoordinator.java) (the `command.<id>` title, prefix and all) and [`ToolWindowManager.tooltipFor`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindowManager.java). Its main toolbar ([`WindowToolbar.setupButton`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowToolbar.java), `refreshToolbarTooltips`) takes the chord from the keymap and the name from a `tooltip.*` catalog key of its own: for most buttons that is the title without its prefix (`tooltip.save=Save` beside `command.file.save=File: Save`), for six another name, which doesn't meet the rule: "Find / Replace" for `find.show`, whose title is "Find: Incremental Search"; "Open" for `file.find` ("File: Find File…"); "Close Tab" for `buffer.close` ("Buffer: Close"); "Open Folder as Project…" for `project.open` ("Project: Open Folder…"); "New From Template" for `template.new` ("Template: New File From Template…"); and "Simple UI mode" for `view.toggleSimpleMode` ("View: Toggle Simple UI Mode"). Two more buttons miss it another way: `file.clearRecent` ("File: Clear Recent Files") reads "Clear recent files", and the pinned tail's Stop button, which stops the run as `run.stop` ("Run: Stop Program") does, is set up with no command id, so it reads "Stop the running program" and shows no chord. Torrenta's `toolbar.withChord`. Mirada's [`Icons.tooltip`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Icons.java) builds the same "label (key)" form with the chord from the keymap in use ([`Command.chord`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Command.java)), and [`TitleBar.relabel`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/TitleBar.java) names the header buttons again when the keys change; Termina's [`IconNames.withChord`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/IconNames.java) takes the chord from its keymap too, but its find bar's arrows don't meet the rule yet: [`ui/SearchBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/SearchBar.java) names them from `search.older` and `search.newer`, "Previous match, up (Enter)" and "Next match, down (Shift+Enter)", not from a command's title, and gives each arrow the chord of the command that steps the other way. The up arrow steps to an older match, as `findNext` does ([`ui/TerminalWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalWindow.java)), and shows the chord of `findPrevious`; the down arrow steps to a newer one, as `findPrevious` does, and shows the chord of `findNext`. The Enter and Shift+Enter in the two strings are the field's own keys. Modula's and nux's tooltips are written in the code, not read from a command: Modula's carry no chord ([`ui/RadioPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/RadioPane.java)), and nux's add the display text of a `KeyCombination` to the button's label ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java), `shortcut`).

rules.text: Every tooltip shows after the same delay, 400 ms, set where the app makes its tooltips and not tooltip by tooltip.
rules.why: JavaFX waits a full second, which reads as no tooltip at all on a row of icons, and a delay set here and there makes some buttons answer faster than their neighbors.

check.text: every `Tooltip` the app creates gets a 400 ms show delay from one place: each is made by one factory that calls `setShowDelay`, or the stylesheet's `.tooltip` rule sets `-fx-show-delay: 400ms`. A tooltip made with `new Tooltip` outside the factory and given no delay fails, as does any other delay.

rules.reference: the app template: its [`styles/app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/styles/app.css) sets `-fx-show-delay: 400ms` on `.tooltip`, and the tooltips its code makes get the same from one constant, `TOOLTIP_DELAY` in [`ui/Icons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Icons.java) (`bindName`, and [`ui/TabHeaders.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/TabHeaders.java) for a tab's). Termina is nearest among the apps: [`ui/IconNames.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/IconNames.java) (`name`, `SHOW_DELAY`) sets 400 ms on every tooltip it makes, and [`ui/TerminalWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalWindow.java) sets the same inline on a tab's folder tooltip, but the tooltip on a disabled row of its [`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/CommandPalette.java) sets none. Editora sets 300, 350 or 400 ms on some ([`editor/LazyTooltip.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/LazyTooltip.java)'s callers, [`ui/StructurePanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/StructurePanel.java), [`ui/MapSurface.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MapSurface.java), [`ui/DiffViewerPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/DiffViewerPane.java)) and leaves the rest at JavaFX's second; Mirada sets 250 ms on one ([`ui/MarksBadge.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/MarksBadge.java)) and none on the others; Torrenta, Modula and nux set none.
