No app's stylesheet sets `-fx-show-delay`.

rules.text: The bars an app stacks at the top of its main window are one chrome band: whichever of the menu bar, the toolbar and the tab strip it has share `-color-bg-subtle` and draw no hairline between them. The bars it stacks at the bottom, whichever of a breadcrumb, a bottom stripe and the status bar it has, do the same. An app with one bar at an edge has nothing to join there.
rules.why: three rules within forty pixels read as clutter, not structure.

check.text: look at the top and the bottom of the main window in a light and a dark theme for a line between two bars, or a change of ground from one to the next.

rules.reference: Editora [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css) (`.menu-bar, .tool-bar`).

rules.appliesTo: an app with a toolbar: a bar of icon-only buttons in a window's chrome (its title bar, a band of its own under the title bar or the menu bar, or the header of a panel), each a shortcut to a command. Editora's and Torrenta's `ToolBar`, the toolbars of Editora's panels and Mirada's header buttons are toolbars. So is a [tool window stripe](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/toolbars-and-tooltips/#tool-window-stripes), on every side: the label its bottom buttons add to the glyph does not change what they are. These are not toolbars: a bar of labeled buttons (nux's `ToolBar`, whose one icon-only button, "?", only [TBAR-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/toolbars-and-tooltips/#tbar-01) covers); controls that belong to the window's content, icon-only or not (Modula's transport and footer controls, Mirada's controls over the image); the buttons at the end of a tab strip (Termina's "+" and its chevron); and a find bar's buttons ([FIND-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/find-bar/#find-16) is theirs). Controls that belong to the window's content include a row of preset chips with its add button (Modula's) and the buttons inside a panel's rows (Mirada's info panel), and an image, PDF or Diff viewer's own bar in the content area (Editora's) is content too.
rules.text: Toolbar buttons stay out of the Tab order: the command, the palette and the menus reach the action, and Tab is for the content. The [keyboard page](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/keyboard/#focus-and-accessibility) has the general focus rules.

check.text: every button on a toolbar is taken out of the Tab order with `setFocusTraversable(false)`, where it is built or by the helper that builds it (Editora's `Icons.toolbarButton`).

rules.reference: Editora [`Icons.toolbarButton`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Icons.java), used by the toolbars of its Git and Markdown lint tool windows; Torrenta's copy of it, which builds every button of its main toolbar ([`MainWindow.toolButton`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java)); Mirada's header buttons: its [`Icons.button`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Icons.java) takes Rotate out of the Tab order, and [`ui/TitleBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/TitleBar.java) takes Info and ☰ out where it builds them. Editora doesn't yet, on these toolbars among others: the buttons of its main toolbar, built by [`WindowToolbar.setupButton`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowToolbar.java) and [`ToolbarCoordinator.buildExtraButton`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolbarCoordinator.java), the stripe buttons, the buttons of the Test Results panel's toolbar, built by `Icons.button` ([`ui/TestRunnerPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TestRunnerPanel.java)), and the float, maximize and close buttons in the header of every tool window ([`ui/ToolWindowPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindowPanel.java)) take focus.

rules.appliesTo: an app with a toolbar: a bar of icon-only buttons in a window's chrome (its title bar, a band of its own under the title bar or the menu bar, or the header of a panel), each a shortcut to a command. Editora's and Torrenta's `ToolBar`, the toolbars of Editora's panels and Mirada's header buttons are toolbars. So is a [tool window stripe](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/toolbars-and-tooltips/#tool-window-stripes), on every side: the label its bottom buttons add to the glyph does not change what they are. These are not toolbars: a bar of labeled buttons (nux's `ToolBar`, whose one icon-only button, "?", only [TBAR-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/toolbars-and-tooltips/#tbar-01) covers); controls that belong to the window's content, icon-only or not (Modula's transport and footer controls, Mirada's controls over the image); the buttons at the end of a tab strip (Termina's "+" and its chevron); and a find bar's buttons ([FIND-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/find-bar/#find-16) is theirs). rules.text: A toolbar's groups of buttons are separated by spacing, not rules: where a toolbar holds `Separator` nodes, keep them (their padding is the gap) and make the line transparent.

rules.appliesTo: an app whose main window holds documents or sessions in tabs the user opens and closes, as Editora's files and Termina's terminals are. The pages of a Settings window (nux's `TabPane`), the fixed sections of a detail pane (Torrenta's) and a strip that switches the window between views (Torrenta's Transfers, Search and RSS) are not such tabs: the user neither opens nor closes them. The Tabs rules cover every tab of the main window's strip, whatever it shows (Editora's image, hex and PDF viewer tabs as much as its editor tabs), not tabs inside a tool window (those of Editora's Terminal and Build Output panels).
rules.text: Every tab operation is a command, so it can be bound to a chord, is in the palette and has a menu row: close, close others, close all, close unmodified, close to the left and right, pin, reopen closed, next and previous. The tab's [right-click menu](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/menus/) lists the ones that act on a tab. A terminal app's tabs are never saved or unsaved, so a terminal app has no close unmodified, and closing its window closes all its tabs, so it needs no close all; the other operations are its commands too.

check.text: the registry holds a command for each operation, each has a row in the menu bar or in the tab's right-click menu, and that menu (Editora's `TabContextMenu`), on every tab of the strip, lists the ones that act on a tab; in a terminal app, each operation but close unmodified and close all.

rules.appliesTo: an app whose main window holds documents or sessions in tabs the user opens and closes, as Editora's files and Termina's terminals are. The pages of a Settings window (nux's `TabPane`), the fixed sections of a detail pane (Torrenta's) and a strip that switches the window between views (Torrenta's Transfers, Search and RSS) are not such tabs: the user neither opens nor closes them. The Tabs rules cover every tab of the main window's strip, whatever it shows (Editora's image, hex and PDF viewer tabs as much as its editor tabs), not tabs inside a tool window (those of Editora's Terminal and Build Output panels).
rules.text: The header is the title: the Tab's own text stays empty, and a graphic header carries the file-type glyph, the markers and the title in a label of its own (Editora's style class for it is `tab-title`). The tooltip is the full path, in which `~` may stand for the home folder. A terminal app's tab shows no file: its header has no file-type glyph, its title names the tab (the user's own name for it, the title the shell set, the running program or the working folder), and its tooltip is the working folder's full path.
rules.why: the graphic is what makes the header a drag handle and lets each state set its own color.

check.text: every tab that shows a file, an editor's or a viewer's, gets `setText("")` and a graphic that holds the file-type glyph and the title in a label of its own (Editora's `.tab-title`); its tooltip is the file's path. In a terminal app: every tab's own text is empty, its graphic holds the title label and no file-type glyph, and the tooltip is the working folder of the tab's active pane. A path that writes the home folder as `~` is a full path.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/TabHeaders.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TabHeaders.java), for its editor tabs (`bufferHeader`, `tooltip`). Its image, hex and PDF viewer tabs don't yet: `contentHeader`, which builds their header, sets no tooltip. Termina [`TerminalWindow.addTab`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalWindow.java) (a `tab-title` label as the tab's graphic, and `installDirectoryTooltip`) over [`ui/TerminalTitle.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalTitle.java) (`tab`, and `tooltip`, which writes the home folder as `~`).

rules.text: A tab's header, the one graphic header of [TABS-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/tabs-and-panels/#tabs-02), carries the tab's states: a `• ` prefix in amber italic for unsaved, a pin and bold for pinned, muted italic for read-only. A terminal app's tab is never unsaved or read-only, and its header says in their place what the tab is doing: the title is the running program's name while one runs, unless the user or the shell named the tab, and a mark beside the title says what happened while the tab was not selected (a notification, a bell, or output after a quiet spell), cleared when the tab is selected. A pinned terminal tab is drawn as any other pinned tab, with a pin and a bold title.

check.text: the code that builds a tab's header marks it unsaved, pinned or read-only (Editora's style classes `dirty`, `pinned` and `read-only` on `.tab-header`) and adds the `• ` prefix and the pin, and the stylesheet gives each mark the look the rule names. In a terminal app: the stylesheet styles the pinned title, the code that names the tab puts the running program before the folder, and the header shows the mark and clears it when the tab is selected.

rules.text: Bulk close skips pinned tabs: close others, close all, close unmodified and close to the left or right never close a pinned tab. A terminal app has three of them ([TABS-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/tabs-and-panels/#tabs-01)), and each skips its pinned tabs too.

check.text: every bulk close the app has (close others, close all, close unmodified, close to the left and to the right) builds the list of tabs it will close without the pinned ones: it tests each tab for pinned before taking it (Editora's `closeOtherTabs`, `closeAllTabs`, `closeUnmodifiedTabs`, `eligibleToLeft` and `eligibleToRight`). A test that asserts it is the surest evidence.

rules.text: Reopen Closed Tab brings back the files whose tabs this window closed, newest first, bounded to twenty, a file listed once, with the caret where it was. In a terminal app the *tab* comes back (its shells, their directories, the pane arrangement, the names the user gave them, its place in the strip) and not the scrollback.
rules.why: the process is gone, and pretending otherwise would be worse than saying so.

check.text: each window keeps a list of the tabs it closed, newest first and no longer than twenty; the command takes the newest entry and opens it. In an app whose tabs hold files, an entry is the file, whether an editor's tab or a viewer's showed it, with the caret where the tab has one; closing a file again replaces its earlier entry, and reopening puts the caret back. In a terminal app, an entry holds the tab's panes with each one's shell and directory, their arrangement, the names the user gave them and the tab's place in the strip, and no scrollback. A test over the list is the surest evidence.

rules.text: In an app whose tabs hold files, a tab shows its file's Git status in the Project tree's colors: modified accent, added green, untracked olive, renamed violet, deleted muted, conflict red. A read-only tab still shows it; an unsaved one shows amber. The tab's tooltip names the file's Git status too, so color is not the status's only sign ([ACC-05](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/accessibility/#acc-05)). A terminal app's tabs hold no files, so the rule passes it by.

check.text: the code that styles a tab gives it, for its file's Git status, the style class the Project tree gives that file's row, read-only or not, and the stylesheet lets the unsaved tab's amber win over it; and the code that sets the tab's tooltip adds the status in words (modified, added, untracked and the rest) when the file has one. A test that finds the tree's class on a changed file's tab, and the status in its tooltip, is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: for the colors, Editora [`ui/TabGitStatus.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TabGitStatus.java), [`TabGitStatusTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/TabGitStatusTest.java). For the tooltip, no app yet: Editora's tab tooltip is the file's full path (`tooltip` in [`ui/TabHeaders.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TabHeaders.java)), so the tint is the tab's only sign of the status. Its Project tree adds a letter to the color; its tabs add no word, glyph or shape. The app template meets both halves for its sample files: [`ui/TabGitStatus.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/TabGitStatus.java) gives a tab the class its Documents window gives the file's row ([`TabsAndPanelsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/TabsAndPanelsTest.java), `aChangedFileWearsTheDocumentsWindowsClass`), and [`ui/TabHeaders.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/TabHeaders.java) adds the status in words to the tab's tooltip, after the path.

rules.text: An app whose tabs hold files has a switcher that lists the open files in tab order. A command opens it; the arrows or the active keymap's line chords move, Enter or releasing Ctrl (the Control key, on macOS too) activates, Esc or the keymap's cancel chord cancels, and Backspace, Delete or the keymap's delete-character chord closes the highlighted file. The switcher's width is fixed to the longest path on each open, so it never resizes while you move. A terminal app's tabs hold no files, so the rule passes it by.

check.text: open it with several tabs; move with the arrows and with the active keymap's line chords, close a file from it, cancel it, and open it again to activate another file; the list keeps its width.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/Switcher.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/Switcher.java), which reads its keys through [`ui/PickerKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/PickerKeys.java) and the keymap, and [`SwitcherFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/SwitcherFxTest.java). In Editora's Emacs keymap `C-x C-b` opens it (`switcher.show`), `C-n` and `C-p` move, `C-g` cancels and `C-d` closes the file ([`keymaps/emacs.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/keymaps/emacs.json)); no other Editora keymap binds `switcher.show`.

rules.text: A command hides the tab bar.

check.text: a registered command hides the tab header, with any number of tabs open. One that hides it only while the window has a single tab does not meet the rule.

rules.reference: Editora `view.toggleTabBar`, `.tab-pane.no-tab-header` in [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css). Termina doesn't yet: the nearest it has is a setting, with a palette command that toggles it, that hides the strip only while the window has one tab (`settings.hideTabBar` in [`ui/SettingCommands.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/SettingCommands.java)).

rules.appliesTo: an app with tool panels: a tool panel is a panel docked at an edge of the main window, beside or under the content, that the user shows and hides as a whole, the content taking its room while it is hidden. A sidebar, a detail pane, an info panel and a thumbnail strip are tool panels, on a stripe or not. A section that folds in place and leaves its heading showing is content (nux's All variables table, a `TitledPane` under its dashboard), and so are a terminal's split panes: neither is a tool panel. Nor is a bar of the window's chrome that a command hides (a toolbar, a status bar, a tab strip).
rules.text: Every tool panel has a command that shows and hides it, with the id `tool.<id>`, as Editora's `tool.project` is, and where the app has a stripe, the panel's stripe button runs that command. In the Emacs keymap, `M-1` through `M-9` and then `M-0` run those commands, one chord to a panel: an app with fewer than ten panels uses the first of the chords, and one with more chooses the ten panels that get them. An app with one key table and no Emacs keymap ([KBD-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/keyboard/#kbd-09)) owes none of these chords.

check.text: every tool panel has a registered command whose id is `tool.` and the panel's own id, which shows the panel when it is hidden and hides it when it shows; a stripe button, where the app has stripes, runs that command, and one that toggles the panel directly and skips what the command does first fails; and `emacs.json`, in an app that ships one, binds `M-1`, `M-2` and on through `M-0` to those commands, one for each panel up to ten.

rules.reference: Editora registers a `tool.<id>` command for each of its tool windows ([`ui/WindowCommandRegistrar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowCommandRegistrar.java)) and binds ten of them to `M-1` … `M-0` ([`keymaps/emacs.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/keymaps/emacs.json)). It doesn't meet the stripe clause yet: [`ToolWindowManager.register`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindowManager.java) gives each stripe button the manager's own `toggle`, not the command, so the button skips what some commands do first (`tool.remote` refreshes its panel; `tool.project` and `tool.notes` test that the feature is on). Nor does every one of its commands hide a panel that shows: `tool.gitLog`, for one, only opens its panel (`openGitLog` in [`ui/GitWindowCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/GitWindowCoordinator.java)), and so do the `tool.<id>` commands of its build tools (`registerCommands` in [`ui/BuildCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/BuildCoordinator.java)). Torrenta and Mirada don't meet the rule yet. Torrenta has no `tool.<id>` command: its two panels' commands are `toggle-sidebar` and `toggle-detail` ([`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java)), and it ships no keymap file, so it owes no chord. Mirada's two are `view.properties` and `view.thumbnails` ([`ui/Command.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Command.java)), and its [`keymaps/emacs.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/resources/com/mirada/keymaps/emacs.json) binds them to `i` and `t`, where the rule requires `M-1` and `M-2`.

rules.text: Closing the panel that holds keyboard focus returns focus to where it was in the content (in Editora, the editor).

check.text: the code that closes a panel keeps the content's last focus owner and refocuses it on close.

rules.reference: Editora [`ToolWindowManager.focusEditor`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindowManager.java), a weak reference to the last editor focus owner.

rules.appliesTo: an app with tool window stripes.
rules.text: Tool windows dock on three sides, left, right and bottom, and a side holds at most two windows stacked (Project over Structure, two consoles along the bottom).
rules.why: past that a side stops being a dock and becomes a list of slivers.

check.text: the sides are an enum of three and the per-side limit is two.

rules.reference: Editora [`ToolWindow.Side`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindow.java), [`ToolWindowManager.MAX_PER_SIDE`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindowManager.java).

rules.appliesTo: an app with tool window stripes.
rules.text: A tool window re-docks by dragging its stripe button to another stripe, with the same dim-and-accent-line feedback as a tab; an empty stripe appears as a dashed accent drop zone for the duration of the drag.

check.text: drag a stripe button to the opposite side.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/ToolWindowDock.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindowDock.java), [`ToolWindowVisibilityTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindowVisibilityTest.java) (an empty stripe shows while dragging).

rules.appliesTo: an app with tool window stripes.
rules.text: Tool windows float, maximize, resize and close from the keyboard, and at most one window is maximized at a time.

check.text: floating, maximizing, resizing and closing a tool window are each a registered command, so the palette runs them without the mouse; and maximizing one first restores the one that was maximized.

rules.reference: Editora `view.floatToolWindow` (palette only), `view.maximizeToolWindow` (`C-x f`), `view.closeFocusedToolWindow` (`C-x 0`), the resize commands (`C-x S-.`, `C-x S-,`, `C-x S-6`); [`ui/ToolWindowManager.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindowManager.java) keeps one `maximized` panel and restores it before it maximizes another.

rules.appliesTo: an app with tool window stripes.
rules.text: Hidden is not unavailable: the user's show/hide choice for a stripe button is kept apart from a context-driven hide (the Commit window outside a Git repository), so the second never clobbers the first.

check.text: the stripe keeps two values for a tool window, the user's saved show/hide choice and whether the context offers the window now, shows the button only when both hold, and never writes the first when the second changes. A test that asserts it is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/ToolWindowVisibility.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindowVisibility.java), [`ToolWindowVisibilityTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindowVisibilityTest.java).

rules.appliesTo: an app with tool window stripes.
rules.text: A tool window whose content needs more room than the default share of its side can ask for more on its first open (Editora's Debug window asks for 42 %); the user's own size wins afterwards.

check.text: a tool window can ask for a larger share of the side on its first open (Editora's `setFirstOpenShare`), the docking code grants it only while the user has set no size for that window, and the other windows keep the side's size. A test that asserts it is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`ToolWindow.setFirstOpenShare`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindow.java), [`ToolWindowFirstOpenShareTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindowFirstOpenShareTest.java).

rules.appliesTo: an app with tool window stripes.
rules.text: A stripe button badges a spinner while its window has something under way.

check.text: a tool window has a busy state, and its stripe button shows a spinner badge while the state holds and hides it when it ends. A test that asserts it is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`ToolWindow.busy`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindow.java), [`ToolWindowManagerFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/ToolWindowManagerFxTest.java).

rules.appliesTo: an app with tool window stripes.
rules.text: Tool windows follow the active document where they should: the Git UI follows the active tab's repository, the status bar's environment segment the active `.http` file, Local History the file whose tab menu opened it.

check.text: switch between tabs from two repositories with the Git window open.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/GitPathScope.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/GitPathScope.java).

rules.text: Every row of every menu the app draws carries an icon that depicts it. A command row wears its command's glyph; a row that names a thing rather than an action (a recent file, a branch, a project) wears that thing's icon; a submenu wears its family's. Only a check or radio row goes without, because its mark fills the icon column. Where the icon set has no glyph that depicts a command, the app adds one (a Material 24 dp path, or a line glyph in the kit's style) instead of leaving the row blank or borrowing another command's.
rules.why: a menu is scanned before it is read, and the glyph is what the eye finds first; the same glyph on the toolbar, in the palette and in the menu ([ICON-20](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/icons-and-color/#icon-20)) is learned once. A blank cell breaks the column, and a borrowed glyph says something else.

check.text: every row the app adds to a menu it draws is given a glyph where the row is built, and only check and radio rows are built without one. On a plain `MenuItem` the glyph is its graphic. A menu-bar row ([MENU-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/menus/#menu-02)) is a `CustomMenuItem` whose `getGraphic()` is null: its glyph is the node inside the icon column of its content (Editora's `menu-item-icon`), and an empty column fails. A submenu's graphic is the same row layout, read the same way. Where the glyphs come from a table keyed by command id, the table has an entry for every command a menu lists, and none is another command's glyph. A test that opens the menu bar's menus and the right-click menus of a tab, an editor, a list row and the toolbar, and fails on a visible row with no glyph, is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/MenuBarIcons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MenuBarIcons.java), [`editor/MenuIcons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/MenuIcons.java), [`ui/TabContextMenu.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TabContextMenu.java); Termina's tab menu has an icon on every row. The app template builds every row of its menus with the command's glyph (`inWindowRow` in [`ui/AppMenus.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AppMenus.java), from `BY_COMMAND` in [`ui/Icons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Icons.java)), and its [`NamedControlsFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/NamedControlsFxTest.java) (`everyMenuRowReadsAsItsTitleAndWearsAGlyph`) fails on a row without one. Mirada's [`MenusFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/ui/MenusFxTest.java) (`everyRowOfEveryMenuHasAGlyph`) opens its header menu, its zoom menu and the image's right-click menu and fails on a row with no glyph. Editora doesn't yet pass: about half its menu-bar rows have no glyph, and [`MenuBarIconsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/MenuBarIconsTest.java) holds that a command without a fitting glyph gets none, which this rule reverses; many right-click and drop-down rows have none either (Run All Requests in a `.http` file, the CSV grid's menu, the Markdown preview's).

rules.text: In every menu the app draws itself, a row whose command has a chord in the active keymap shows that chord, in right-click menus, drop-downs and the toolbar's overflow as in the in-window menu bar: right-aligned in the menu's chord column, in the keyboard color, the one color the app keeps for chords and key chips (Editora's token for it is `-state-key`; [ICON-06](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/icons-and-color/#icon-06) says how the color is made), at the size [MENU-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/menus/#menu-16) gives. An unbound command leaves the cell empty, never a wrong chord, and a keymap switch rewrites every cell. The menus a platform draws are outside this rule: the macOS system menu bar, whose rows append the chord to the title ([MENU-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/menus/#menu-02)), and a tray icon's menu, which shows none.
rules.why: the menu is where a user learns the keys. A right-click menu that hides them teaches the mouse, while the palette and the toolbar's tooltips already show the same chord.

check.text: in the in-window menu bar, in every right-click menu and in every drop-down, a row that runs a command has a chord cell, right-aligned in one column of the menu, that the code fills with the active keymap's display chord for the command's id and leaves empty for an unbound command: a label of the row's own (Editora's `menu-item-chord`) or, outside the menu bar, the item's accelerator text, never a chord typed into a string. The cell is filled again on each showing or when the keymap changes, and the stylesheet draws it in the app's keyboard color at [MENU-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/menus/#menu-16)'s size. An app whose menu rows run only commands that have no chord (nux's drop-downs: its one key table binds none of their commands) has nothing to show, and passes. A row of the macOS system menu bar is not judged here, since [MENU-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/menus/#menu-02) has its chord appended to its title, and neither is a tray icon's menu. A test that binds a command, opens a right-click menu that lists it, finds its chord, and finds the new chord after a keymap switch is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`MainMenuBar.rowContent`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainMenuBar.java) and `alignChordColumns`, `.menu-item-chord` in [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css), for the menu bar. Its editor, editor tab, preview and output-console right-click menus show them too: a row tagged with the command it does ([`editor/MenuChords.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/MenuChords.java), `tag`) carries that command's chord as an accelerator that only displays, re-read from the active keymap each time a right-click menu opens (`refresh`), and `.accelerator-text` in its `app.css` draws it in `-state-key` at 11 px ([`MenuChordsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/editor/MenuChordsTest.java), [`ContextMenuFontFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/ContextMenuFontFxTest.java)). Editora doesn't meet the rule yet: its other right-click menus and its drop-downs tag no row, so the Copy, Select All, Add Bookmark and Add Note of a Project Map card's menu show no chord ([`ui/ProjectMapPreview.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ProjectMapPreview.java)). The app template's right-click menus show them: [`ui/CommandMenu.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/CommandMenu.java) draws each row as the menu bar's ([`AppMenus.inWindowRow`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AppMenus.java)) and re-reads its chord on every showing (`refresh`), in `-state-key` at 11 px (`.menu-item-chord` in its [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/styles/app.css)); its [`MenuLookFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/MenuLookFxTest.java) (`aRightClickMenuShowsEachChordInTheKeyColorAndFollowsTheKeymap`) opens a right-click menu, reads the chord and reads the new one after a keymap switch. Termina's menu bar colors its chords `-color-fg-muted`, not a keyboard color ([`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/resources/com/termina/styles/app.css)).

rules.text: Every menu the app draws itself (the in-window menu bar, right-click menus, the drop-down of a menu button or a split button, the toolbar's overflow) draws its titles in Inter 14 px regular and its chords in Inter 11 px at the default zoom, scaled by the UI zoom ([WIN-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-12)), whatever node it was opened from: the size is set on `.context-menu` and its rows' labels from one value the zoom sets, never inherited from the node. The macOS system menu bar and a tray icon's menu are the platform's, drawn in the platform's font, and outside this rule.
rules.why: a popup inherits the font of the node it was shown from, and `em` resolves against it: Editora's toolbar menu once rendered at the bar's 18 px, a third larger than every other menu, and a file tree's or a monospace editor's font leaks the same way.

check.text: the stylesheet sets the font family and the size on `.context-menu` and on its rows' title and chord labels from one value, in pixels and never in `em`, so the font of the node a menu was opened from cannot reach it; and the code that applies the UI zoom rewrites that value, so the 14 px and the 11 px scale with the zoom. A test that opens a menu from the toolbar, an editor and a tree row and reads Inter 14 px from each row's title, and 14 px times the zoom after the UI zoom changes, is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora `.context-menu` and `.menu-item-chord` in [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css), [`MainMenuBar.UI_FONT_SIZE`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainMenuBar.java), [`ToolbarMenuFontFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/ToolbarMenuFontFxTest.java) and [`ContextMenuFontFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/ContextMenuFontFxTest.java). Editora writes 14 px and 11 px as absolute pixels and has no UI zoom yet ([WIN-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-12)), so its menus keep their size whatever opens them but don't scale. The app template meets it: `.context-menu` and its rows' labels in its [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/styles/app.css) are pinned to Inter 14 px and the chord to 11 px, in pixels, which its UI zoom multiplies ([`ui/UiZoom.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/UiZoom.java)), and its [`MenuLookFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/MenuLookFxTest.java) (`everyMenuDrawsInInterFourteenWhateverOpenedIt`, `theUiZoomScalesEveryMenu`) holds both.

rules.text: At the default zoom a menu row is 34 px high (padding 8 × 12), its icon column is 22 px wide with 8 px to the title, and its chord starts at least 18 px after the title column. The popup's card has a radius of 8 and a shadow of radius 16 at offset Y 16: the offset is at least the radius.
rules.why: one row in every app is what makes the menus one family's. And a menu is a native window sized to its root with the effect included, so a shadow that reaches above the menu is invisible window over the bar the menu hangs from, and the pointer lands on it instead of the next menu button.

check.text: the stylesheet sets the row's padding and the popup's radius and shadow, with the shadow's offset no smaller than its radius; the row's layout sets the icon column's width and the chord's margin.

rules.reference: Editora `.menu-item` and `.context-menu` in [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css), and [`MainMenuBar.ICON_COLUMN`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainMenuBar.java) and `rowContent`; [`MenuPopupBoundsFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/MenuPopupBoundsFxTest.java) holds the shadow below the popup. The app template draws the same card and row: `.context-menu` in its [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/styles/app.css) (radius 8, a shadow of radius 16 at offset Y 16, rows padded 8 × 12) and `inWindowRow` in its [`ui/AppMenus.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AppMenus.java) (a 22 px icon column, `ICON_SLOT`, 8 px to the title and an 18 px chord margin). Termina and Torrenta get the row's padding from the Editora themes they ship, and keep those themes' popup: a radius of 4 and a shadow of radius 6 (8 in the dark theme) at offset Y 2 (`.menu-item` and `.context-menu` in each one's `editora-light.css` and `editora-dark.css`). Termina's [`ui/MenuRows.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/MenuRows.java) has the same 22 px column and 18 px chord margin. Mirada and nux write no radius or shadow for `.context-menu` and take their AtlantaFX theme's popup (Cupertino, Primer). Modula's [`modula.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/resources/com/modula/modula.css) gives `.context-menu` a radius of 8 and a shadow of radius 20 at offset Y 6, and its rows a padding of 4 × 8.

rules.appliesTo: an app with a menu bar.
rules.text: Every menu-bar item is a command from the registry, with the command's title ([KBD-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/keyboard/#kbd-03)), its chord from the active keymap and its enabled state from the command's gate. A row may show the title without its category prefix ("Save As…" for "File: Save As…"); it never carries a title of its own. The bar assembles and refreshes; it holds no behavior of its own.

check.text: the bar's model lists command ids only, beside the separators and the submenus that group them, and every row runs its id through the registry. A row that is no command id fails: one built by hand, with a title and a handler of its own.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/MenuBarModel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MenuBarModel.java) over [`command/CommandRegistry.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/command/CommandRegistry.java), [`ui/MainMenuBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainMenuBar.java): the model's entries are command ids, separators and the titles of its submenus. Torrenta and Termina don't meet the rule yet. Rows of Torrenta's View menu, the Command Palette, Toolbar, Sidebar and Simple Mode rows among them, are built by hand with `menu.*` titles and handlers of their own ([`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java)). Termina's model ([`ui/MenuBarModel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/MenuBarModel.java)) holds rows that are no command id: the New Tab With Profile submenu, whose rows carry each profile's name and open the tab from a handler of their own (`profileBarRows` in [`ui/TerminalWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalWindow.java)), and, off macOS, the zoom row, one row of buttons for its four zoom commands.

rules.appliesTo: an app with a menu bar.
rules.text: Menu-bar rows use no `KeyCombination` accelerators. In the in-window bar each row is a `CustomMenuItem` laying out icon, title, spacer and chord. On the macOS system menu bar (`useSystemMenuBar`) the chord is appended to the title and rows carry no icon.
rules.why: Emacs chords are multi-key, which a `KeyCombination` cannot express, and on macOS an accelerator would bypass the key dispatcher. The native macOS menu draws text only and no graphics, which is also the platform's convention.

check.text: no menu-bar row calls `setAccelerator`; each row of the in-window bar is a `CustomMenuItem` whose content lays out the icon, the title, a spacer and the chord; and where the bar is the macOS system menu bar, a row's text is the title with the chord appended and the row has no graphic.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/MainMenuBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainMenuBar.java) (`rowContent`, `refresh`).

rules.appliesTo: an app with a menu bar.
rules.text: Enablement is re-read every time a menu opens, and titles and chords on a keymap or locale change.
rules.why: a menu built before Git finished detecting a repository must not stay grayed out.

check.text: each menu's on-showing handler reads every row's enabled state from its command again, and the code that switches the keymap or the locale rewrites every row's title and chord. A test that changes a command's state after the window is built (a repository detected late) and finds the row enabled is the surest evidence.
