rules.appliesTo: an app with a menu bar.
rules.text: The in-window menu bar, the one an app shows on Windows and Linux ([WIN-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-03)), is reachable from the keyboard in every keymap. JavaFX opens the bar's first menu on `F10` and on a lone `Alt`; a keymap that binds `F10` to something else binds a command that focuses the menu bar instead. So does a terminal app, where a plain `F10` goes to the program it runs. The macOS system menu bar is reached with the OS's own keys and asks nothing of the app.
rules.why: the menus are a keyboard user's map of the app; a chord that never reaches them hides it.

check.text: on Windows or Linux, in each keymap, reach the first menu with the keyboard alone and walk the bar with the arrows.

rules.reference: no app yet. Editora's CUA, VS Code and Sublime keymaps bind `F10` to `debug.stepOver` ([`keymaps/cua.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/keymaps/cua.json)), and no command focuses the bar. Termina leaves a plain `F10` to the program in the terminal ([`ui/ViewKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/ViewKeys.java)) and has no such command either.

rules.appliesTo: an app with a right-click menu: a menu the app builds and opens on a right-click, the Menu key or `Shift+F10`, over something in one of its windows. The stock Cut, Copy and Paste menu that JavaFX gives a text field does not make an app one, and neither does a tray icon's menu, which the platform draws: nux has both and no right-click menu.
rules.text: In an app with a right-click menu, every list row, tree row, tab, editor and read-only console has one, with the actions for *that* thing, and every action in a right-click menu is a command ([KBD-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/keyboard/#kbd-01)). The rule covers the lists, trees, tabs, editors and read-only consoles in the app's windows. A log shown as text, the Debug Log among them, is a read-only console and has its right-click menu. A list that only navigates, switching what its window shows (a Settings sidebar, a list of pages), has no actions of its own and is outside the rule, as are the overlay list of a picker or a palette and a plain text area in a dialog.

check.text: list the lists, trees, tab strips, editors and read-only consoles in the app's windows, the text of the Debug Log window and of any other log shown as text among the consoles, and find the right-click menu each one installs; then read every row of every right-click menu the app builds: its action is one a registered command runs too, by the command's id through the registry or by calling what the command calls, so the palette reaches it. A row whose action no command runs fails, as does a list, tree, tab strip, editor or console with no menu; the stock Cut, Copy and Paste menu that JavaFX gives a text area is not one. A list that only switches what its window shows (a Settings sidebar, a list of pages), the overlay list of a picker or a palette and a plain text area in a dialog are not judged.

rules.reference: the app template's [`ui/CommandMenu.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/CommandMenu.java), which builds each menu from registered command ids and runs a row through the registry (`onRow` for a list row, `onConsole` for a text area): the tabs and the editor ([`ui/DocumentTabs.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/DocumentTabs.java)), the Output console ([`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MainWindow.java)), the Debug Log ([`ui/DebugLogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/DebugLogWindow.java)), the Documents list, the Message Log's rows and Settings' pages and key bindings ([`RightClickMenusFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/RightClickMenusFxTest.java)). Editora's [`ui/TabContextMenu.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TabContextMenu.java) and [`ui/ConsoleContextMenu.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ConsoleContextMenu.java) are menus this rule describes ([`ui/RowContextMenu.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/RowContextMenu.java) builds none: it sends the keyboard's request to the selected row's own menu), but their rows are built by hand and call the window's methods, not a command id, so nothing holds that each row has a command. Editora, Termina, Mirada, Torrenta and Modula don't meet the rule yet, in these places among others. In Editora the trees and the list of the Hierarchy, References and Undo History panels have no right-click menu ([`ui/HierarchyPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/HierarchyPanel.java), [`ui/ReferencesPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ReferencesPanel.java), [`ui/UndoHistoryPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/UndoHistoryPanel.java)), and the Customize Toolbar… row of the toolbar's menu turns on a mode that no command does (`showContextMenu` in [`ui/ToolbarCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolbarCoordinator.java)). In Termina the list of the Message Log has no menu ([`ui/MessageLogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/MessageLogWindow.java)), and neither has Mirada's ([`ui/MessageLogView.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/MessageLogView.java)). The Debug Log windows of Editora, Torrenta, Termina and Mirada show the log in a read-only `TextArea` and give it no menu (Editora's [`ui/DebugLogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/DebugLogWindow.java), Torrenta's [`ui/DebugLogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/DebugLogWindow.java), Termina's [`ui/DebugLogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/DebugLogWindow.java) and Mirada's [`ui/DebugLogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/DebugLogWindow.java)). In Torrenta the rows of the files and peers menus, Ban Peer among them, run handlers that no command reaches ([`ui/DetailPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/DetailPane.java)). In Modula the Rename… and Remove rows of a preset chip's menu ([`ui/PresetBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/PresetBar.java)) run no command, and its command list has neither ([`ui/RadioPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/RadioPane.java), `commands`).

rules.appliesTo: an app with a right-click menu: a menu the app builds and opens on a right-click, the Menu key or `Shift+F10`, over something in one of its windows. The stock Cut, Copy and Paste menu that JavaFX gives a text field does not make an app one, and neither does a tray icon's menu, which the platform draws: nux has both and no right-click menu.
rules.text: One right-click menu at a time: a right-click while a menu is open replaces it, and the first one closes before the second shows.
rules.why: JavaFX stacks a second menu beside the first when each row owns its own `ContextMenu`, and the stale one is then no longer dismissible.

check.text: the code that opens a right-click menu closes the one already showing before the next appears, in every window: the app keeps one menu and shows it again at the new place, or hides the showing menu in the handler of the press or the request that opens the next. Menus that each row or cell owns, with nothing to close the one shown last, fail. A test that right-clicks another row with a menu open and finds one menu showing is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/ContextMenuDismissal.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ContextMenuDismissal.java) closes every open right-click menu on the press that opens the next ([`ContextMenuDismissalFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/ContextMenuDismissalFxTest.java)), and its toolbar keeps one menu and shows it again, so a second right-click on the bar moves it ([`ToolbarCoordinator`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ToolbarCoordinator.java), [`ToolbarContextMenuDismissFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/ToolbarContextMenuDismissFxTest.java)); Termina's [`ui/OneMenu.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/OneMenu.java) closes every other menu as one starts to show ([`OneMenuTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/ui/OneMenuTest.java)), and the app template's [`RightClickMenusFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/RightClickMenusFxTest.java) (`aRightClickOnAnotherRowLeavesOneMenu`) holds it for a list's rows. Modula's [`RadioPane`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/RadioPane.java) hides its own previous menu before it shows a new one, but Modula doesn't meet the rule yet: each preset chip owns a menu ([`ui/PresetBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/PresetBar.java)), and no code closes the pane's menu when a chip's opens: the pane's press filter skips the right button, and the chip answers the menu request before the pane's handler can.

rules.appliesTo: an app with a right-click menu: a menu the app builds and opens on a right-click, the Menu key or `Shift+F10`, over something in one of its windows. The stock Cut, Copy and Paste menu that JavaFX gives a text field does not make an app one, and neither does a tray icon's menu, which the platform draws: nux has both and no right-click menu.
rules.text: A press anywhere outside a right-click menu closes it, including inside the control the menu was opened on. The press is not consumed: a click in a list still selects the row, and a right-click on another row opens that row's menu straight away. Drop-downs opened by a plain click (menu buttons, choice boxes, the menu bar) keep the stock behavior, and a menu that turned auto-hide off is left alone.
rules.why: JavaFX's auto-hide deliberately ignores a press on the menu's *owner node*, so a stock menu on a tree or a text area stays open when the user clicks another row or the text.

check.text: the app installs a mouse-press filter, on every window or on the scene of each window that has a right-click menu, that hides a showing right-click menu on a press outside the menu, a press inside its owner control included, and does not consume the press; a press in another window of the app closes the menu too, by the same filter or by the stock auto-hide. A right-click menu left with the stock auto-hide alone fails, since JavaFX ignores a press on the owner node. A test that presses inside the owner control and in another window and finds the menu closed is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`ContextMenuDismissal.install()`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ContextMenuDismissal.java), called once in [`App`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java) at startup for every current and future window; [`ContextMenuDismissalFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/ContextMenuDismissalFxTest.java), and for the toolbar's menu, whose owner is the whole bar, [`ToolbarContextMenuDismissFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/ToolbarContextMenuDismissFxTest.java). The app template installs the same class at start-up. Mirada turns auto-hide off on its three menus and closes them from a press filter on the scene of each window that has one ([`ui/Popups.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Popups.java), `closeOnPressOutside`). Termina's terminal view hides its menu from its own press filter, but its tab menus have the stock auto-hide alone ([`ui/TerminalWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalWindow.java)); so have Modula's preset chips ([`ui/PresetBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/PresetBar.java)), beside a pane menu that its own filter closes, and every right-click menu in Torrenta. nux has no right-click menu.

rules.appliesTo: an app with a right-click menu: a menu the app builds and opens on a right-click, the Menu key or `Shift+F10`, over something in one of its windows. The stock Cut, Copy and Paste menu that JavaFX gives a text field does not make an app one, and neither does a tray icon's menu, which the platform draws: nux has both and no right-click menu.
rules.text: Escape closes a right-click menu and focus goes back where it was. In a terminal app the Escape that closes the menu does not reach the shell.

check.text: open a menu, press Escape, and type: the keys reach the control that had focus.

rules.reference: the stock `ContextMenu` hide-on-Escape (the right-click menus' [Spec](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/menus/#spec)); Termina's `onKeyPressed` filter hides the menu and consumes the key ([`TerminalView`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalView.java)).

rules.appliesTo: an app with a right-click menu: a menu the app builds and opens on a right-click, the Menu key or `Shift+F10`, over something in one of its windows. The stock Cut, Copy and Paste menu that JavaFX gives a text field does not make an app one, and neither does a tray icon's menu, which the platform draws: nux has both and no right-click menu.
rules.text: The Menu key and `Shift+F10` open the right-click menu of the selected row, scrolled into view first, so every row action a mouse can reach the keyboard can too. In a view with no rows (an editor, a terminal, an image) they open the focused view's menu. The chord is the same on macOS, where keyboards have no Menu key: `Shift+F10`, with no `Cmd` form.
rules.why: those keys arrive at the focused control, not at a row's cell, so a menu installed on cells never saw them.

check.text: each list, tree or table whose rows have a right-click menu answers the keyboard's request (JavaFX's `ContextMenuEvent` with `isKeyboardTrigger()`, which it raises for both keys, or a key handler of the app's own for the Menu key and `Shift+F10`) by scrolling the selected row into view and showing that row's menu anchored to the row; a view with no rows shows its own menu for the same keys; and no branch gives macOS another chord. A test that sends the request to a tree and a list and finds the selected row's menu, anchored to that row, is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`RowContextMenu.install(tree)`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/RowContextMenu.java), [`RowContextMenuFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/RowContextMenuFxTest.java): it answers the request JavaFX raises for those keys (`ContextMenuEvent.isKeyboardTrigger`). Termina's [`ui/ViewKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/ViewKeys.java) and Mirada's [`Popups.isMenuKey`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/Popups.java) read the key press themselves, the same on every OS. One of Editora's keymaps gives the chord to a command as well: IntelliJ's binds `S-f10` to `run.rerun` ([`keymaps/intellij.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/keymaps/intellij.json)), a clash [`RowContextMenuFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/RowContextMenuFxTest.java) does not cover: it raises the request itself and presses no key. The app template's [`ui/RowContextMenu.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/RowContextMenu.java) answers the same request for a list's rows ([`RightClickMenusFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/RightClickMenusFxTest.java), `theMenuKeyOpensTheSelectedRowsMenuAtThatRow`).

rules.appliesTo: an app with a right-click menu: a menu the app builds and opens on a right-click, the Menu key or `Shift+F10`, over something in one of its windows. The stock Cut, Copy and Paste menu that JavaFX gives a text field does not make an app one, and neither does a tray icon's menu, which the platform draws: nux has both and no right-click menu.
rules.text: A right-click selects first. In an editor, a right-click outside every selection moves the caret to the click (so Paste lands there); inside a selection it keeps carets and selections (so Cut and Copy act on what was clicked). From the keyboard the target is the caret. In a list, the menu is the clicked row's.

check.text: in an editor, select a word, right-click elsewhere and paste: the text lands at the click; then right-click inside a selection and copy: the selection is what was copied. In a list, select one row and right-click another: the menu that opens is the clicked row's, and its actions act on that row. An app with no editor is judged on its lists alone.

rules.reference: Editora [`editor/ContextMenuTarget.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/editor/ContextMenuTarget.java).

rules.appliesTo: an app with a right-click menu: a menu the app builds and opens on a right-click, the Menu key or `Shift+F10`, over something in one of its windows. The stock Cut, Copy and Paste menu that JavaFX gives a text field does not make an app one, and neither does a tray icon's menu, which the platform draws: nux has both and no right-click menu.
rules.text: A menu attached to something that exists once per open file is built when first shown, and set up for each showing: an `onShowing` handler sets the labels, enablement and visibility for *this* showing, then collapses the separators.
rules.why: such a menu is built for every file and opened for almost none.

check.text: a menu that exists once per open file is not built with the file: its items are created in the handler of its first request, and an on-showing handler sets their labels, enablement and visibility and then collapses the separators (Editora's `LazyContextMenu.of(build)`).

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/LazyContextMenu.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/LazyContextMenu.java), [`LazyContextMenuFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/LazyContextMenuFxTest.java). A read-only console's menu is just Select All and Copy, both disabled while it is empty ([`ConsoleContextMenu`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ConsoleContextMenu.java)).

rules.appliesTo: an app with a right-click menu: a menu the app builds and opens on a right-click, the Menu key or `Shift+F10`, over something in one of its windows. The stock Cut, Copy and Paste menu that JavaFX gives a text field does not make an app one, and neither does a tray icon's menu, which the platform draws: nux has both and no right-click menu.
rules.text: A destructive row is styled as dangerous, its text in `-color-danger-fg` (Editora's style class for it is `danger`). What the action does before it destroys anything is not this rule's: the [Confirm dialog](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/confirm-dialog/) rules hold it ([CONF-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-01), [CONF-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-03): it asks first with a button that names it, or is undoable).

check.text: rows that delete, discard or reset carry the style class that colors their text `-color-danger-fg` (Editora's `danger`). Whether the action asks first is judged under CONF-01 and CONF-03, not here.

rules.reference: Editora `.menu-item.danger` in [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css), [`ui/BranchPopup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/BranchPopup.java); the app template's [`ui/AppMenus.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AppMenus.java) (`DESTRUCTIVE`: the rows that clear a log, reset a binding or import a configuration take `danger`), held by [`RightClickMenusFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/RightClickMenusFxTest.java) (`destructiveRowsAreStyledAsDangerous`).

rules.appliesTo: an app with a right-click menu: a menu the app builds and opens on a right-click, the Menu key or `Shift+F10`, over something in one of its windows. The stock Cut, Copy and Paste menu that JavaFX gives a text field does not make an app one, and neither does a tray icon's menu, which the platform draws: nux has both and no right-click menu.
rules.text: In a terminal view, a program that grabbed the mouse owns the right-click; `Shift`+right-click always opens the menu, and the keyboard request is never contested.

check.text: the terminal view decides whether to show its menu from the mouse mode, Shift and the trigger: a right-click while a program has the mouse goes to the program unless Shift is held, and a request from the keyboard always shows the menu. A test of that decision is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Termina's [`TerminalView.shouldShowMenu`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalView.java), [`ContextMenuContentionTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/ui/ContextMenuContentionTest.java).

rules.appliesTo: an app whose work goes on without its window, as Torrenta's, Modula's and nux's does.
rules.text: The tray is a StatusNotifierItem on Linux, with no AWT fallback, and AWT's `SystemTray` on Windows and macOS. The app creates it on a background thread, never on the FX thread, and no sooner than the code that shows the main window, so the first frame never waits for the tray.
rules.why: D-Bus and AWT can block, and neither is worth a stalled first frame. On Linux AWT's tray is the XEmbed one, which GNOME dropped in 3.26 and Wayland never had, so there is nothing worth falling back to.

check.text: on Linux the code that creates the tray makes the StatusNotifierItem or reports that there is no tray, and no branch of it falls back to AWT's tray (Torrenta's `Trays.create`, which makes an `AwtTray` off Linux only); on Windows and macOS it makes the AWT `SystemTray` icon; and the main window runs it on a background thread that it starts as it shows itself, or later.

rules.reference: Torrenta [`tray/Trays.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/tray/Trays.java) (`create`) and [`MainWindow.installTray`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java), which `show` calls and which starts a `tray-init` thread; the [Spec](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/tray-and-background/#spec) table. Modula and nux don't pass yet: on Linux their `Trays.create` falls back to `AwtTray` when `SniTray` fails (Modula [`tray/Trays.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/tray/Trays.java), nux [`tray/Trays.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/tray/Trays.java)).

rules.appliesTo: an app whose work goes on without its window, as Torrenta's, Modula's and nux's does.
rules.text: An app that lives behind a tray icon is fully usable when no icon comes up. No icon is a normal outcome (stock GNOME has no StatusNotifier host), not an error, and the main window then says in its status line why there is none and that closing the window quits the app.
rules.why: the bug they actually hit is silence: the box says close to tray, and closing quits.

check.text: when the attempt to create the tray returns none, the code sets the main window's status message (the echo area of its status bar, where it has one) to the reason and to the fact that closing the window quits; and the tray's menu holds no action the window lacks.

rules.reference: Torrenta [`MainWindow.installTray`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java) ("No tray icon (…); closing the window quits Torrenta", `status.noTray`); Modula's status says closing the window will quit it ([`RadioPane.reportNoTray`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/RadioPane.java)). nux doesn't pass yet: when no tray comes it shows the window, if it was hidden, and says nothing ([`TrayController.onCreated`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/app/TrayController.java)).

rules.appliesTo: an app whose work goes on without its window, as Torrenta's, Modula's and nux's does.
rules.text: Closing the window hides it only while an icon is actually up and the setting says so, both read at close time; otherwise a close quits. `Platform.setImplicitExit(false)` is set only once a tray exists, and turning the tray off brings a hidden window back.
rules.why: the checkbox can change while the window is open, and hiding a window that leaves no icon behind is how a program becomes unreachable.

check.text: the close handler tests that a tray exists and reads the live setting; `setImplicitExit(false)` sits after the tray is created.

rules.reference: Torrenta [`MainWindow.setOnCloseRequest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java), Modula's `installCloseBehaviour`, nux's [`TrayController.closeHidesWindow`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/app/TrayController.java) and `updateImplicitExit`.

rules.appliesTo: an app whose work goes on without its window, as Torrenta's, Modula's and nux's does.
rules.text: The tray's Quit runs the app's one quit method ([WIN-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-13)), and a quit ends the program with the window showing or hidden to the tray: the close handler never takes a quit for a close and hides the window, and the method exits outright, since closing the last window no longer does ([TRAY-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/tray-and-background/#tray-03)).
rules.why: a close hides a tray app's window, so a quit that goes through a close leaves the program running behind its icon. The tray's Quit also arrives while a dialog may be open, and quitting from inside a nested event loop aborted the JVM, which is why the quit method closes dialogs first.

check.text: the tray's Quit callback runs the quit method on the FX thread; the method marks the quit, so the close handler doesn't hide the window, tears down when the window is already hidden, and calls `Platform.exit`. On macOS the app menu's and the Dock's Quit reach the method too ([WIN-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-13)): JavaFX turns them into a close request on every window (`GlassStage.requestClosingAllWindows`), and a tray app that doesn't catch Glass's quit action hides to the tray instead of quitting.

rules.reference: Torrenta [`MainWindow.quit`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java) for the tray and File → Quit: it sets `quitting`, which the close handler reads, closes open dialogs and waits for their loops, then closes the window or, when it is hidden, shuts down directly. It doesn't catch macOS's Quit yet, so there Quit hides the window. Modula's tray Quit runs [`ModulaApp.quit`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ModulaApp.java) and nux's calls `Platform.exit` ([`App`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java)), as its `app.quit` command does; neither closes open dialogs first or catches macOS's Quit.

rules.appliesTo: an app whose work goes on without its window, as Torrenta's, Modula's and nux's does.
rules.text: `--minimized` starts the app with no window in front, in one of two ways. With the tray setting on it comes up behind the icon: the window is not shown until the tray attempt has answered, and if the icon that was asked for does not come, the window is shown after all. With the tray setting off there is no icon to wait for, and the window starts minimized.
rules.why: a start at login can then never leave a program with no way back: a hidden window has its icon, and a minimized one is on the taskbar or in the Dock. A person who turned the tray off asked for the minimized window. A person who asked for an icon looks for the icon, so when none comes the window is what tells them, with the reason on its status bar ([TRAY-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/tray-and-background/#tray-02)).

check.text: with the tray setting on, a `--minimized` start leaves the window hidden until the tray attempt answers, and shows it when the attempt returns no tray; with the setting off it shows the window minimized and waits for nothing.

rules.reference: Torrenta [`MainWindow.show`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java) and `installTray`, which calls `showFromTray` when no icon comes. nux's [`App`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java) and [`TrayController.onCreated`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/app/TrayController.java) do the same with the tray setting on; with it off nux doesn't pass yet: it ignores the flag and shows the window. Modula has no `--minimized`.

rules.appliesTo: an app whose work goes on without its window, as Torrenta's, Modula's and nux's does.
rules.text: Start at login writes the OS's own entry, and nothing else: an XDG autostart entry in `~/.config/autostart` (quoted `Exec`, `StartupWMClass` matching the installed launcher, `X-KDE-autostart-after=panel` so a tray host is up first), a LaunchAgent in `~/Library/LaunchAgents`, the `HKCU\…\Run` value on Windows (read together with `StartupApproved`, where Task Manager keeps the person's "off"). The entry is the one truth: turned off in GNOME Tweaks, KDE's Autostart page or Task Manager, the box shows unticked. The one setting beside it is *start behind the tray icon*, written into the entry as `--minimized`.

check.text: the code that turns start at login on or off writes or removes one entry for the OS it runs on, and keeps no setting of its own for it: the XDG entry with a quoted `Exec`, the installed launcher's `StartupWMClass` and `X-KDE-autostart-after=panel`; the LaunchAgent; the `Run` value. The box's state is read back from the entry, with `StartupApproved` on Windows, and start behind the tray icon adds `--minimized` to the entry's command. A test of each platform's entry, byte for byte, is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Torrenta [`os/Autostart.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/os/Autostart.java), [`os/AutostartSpec.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/os/AutostartSpec.java), [`AutostartSpecTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/test/java/com/torrenta/os/AutostartSpecTest.java). nux's [`autostart/AutostartSpec.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/autostart/AutostartSpec.java) is the earlier version: the same three entries, without `X-KDE-autostart-after` and without reading `StartupApproved`.

rules.appliesTo: an app whose work goes on without its window, as Torrenta's, Modula's and nux's does.
rules.text: Only the app writes the login entry, and only from an installed package: the installers never do it, and a run from source says it has nothing to start.
rules.why: an installer runs for every account.

check.text: the entry's target comes from `jpackage.app-path`, and is absent when it is unset.

rules.reference: Torrenta [`os/Autostart.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/os/Autostart.java).

rules.appliesTo: an app whose work goes on without its window, as Torrenta's, Modula's and nux's does.
rules.text: A dock badge: an app may put a figure of its own on the macOS dock icon through AWT's `Taskbar` and on a Linux launcher that honors Unity's `LauncherEntry` signal (KDE, Dash to Dock); nothing on Windows, whose taskbar badges only AWT's own windows. The badge is cleared when there is nothing to show and has its own switch. Torrenta's is the download rate on the dock and a count on the launcher, cleared when nothing downloads.

check.text: the badge is set through AWT's `Taskbar` on macOS and through the `LauncherEntry` signal on Linux, and not at all on Windows; the code clears it when there is nothing to show (in Torrenta, when nothing downloads); and a setting of its own turns it off. A test of the badge's state is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Torrenta [`os/Badges.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/os/Badges.java), [`BadgeState`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/os/BadgeState.java), [`BadgeStateTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/test/java/com/torrenta/os/BadgeStateTest.java).

rules.appliesTo: an app whose work goes on without its window, as Torrenta's, Modula's and nux's does.
rules.text: A second launch brings the hidden window forward: the [single-instance hand-off](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/command-line/) shows a window hidden to the tray before it opens what it was given.

check.text: close to the tray, then launch the app again with a file.

rules.reference: Torrenta [`MainWindow.showFromTray`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java).

rules.appliesTo: an app whose work goes on without its window, as Torrenta's, Modula's and nux's does.
rules.text: A tray makes AWT headful on Windows and macOS only, where the tray is AWT's ([TRAY-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/tray-and-background/#tray-01)); on Linux the app stays headless with its tray on. [CLI-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/command-line/#cli-09) holds the rule this is part of, for an app with a tray or without one: the whole list of uses that may make AWT headful, and that `main` decides it once, at start-up. Because it is decided once, a tray turned on later tells the user to restart ("restart to show the tray icon"), never that the tray is unsupported.

check.text: the code that decides `java.awt.headless` at start-up counts the tray setting as a reason on Windows and macOS and never on Linux, and the code that creates the tray, finding AWT headless on Windows or macOS, reports that a restart will show the icon. A test of the decision per OS is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Torrenta [`os/AwtUse.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/os/AwtUse.java) (`headful`, which `App.main` asks once with the tray, badge and handler settings), [`AwtUseTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/test/java/com/torrenta/os/AwtUseTest.java) (`awtIsHeadfulOnlyWhereSomethingAwtIsWanted`); [`Trays.usesAwt`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/tray/Trays.java) and [`TraysTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/test/java/com/torrenta/tray/TraysTest.java) for the tray alone, and `Trays.create`, which gives the restart reason (`tray.reason.restart`) when AWT was left headless. Modula and nux never set `java.awt.headless`, so AWT is headful on every OS.

rules.appliesTo: every app that sends desktop notifications, with a tray or without one: Torrenta and nux for their own events, Editora and Termina for a program's OSC 9 and OSC 777.
rules.text: Desktop notifications go through one notifier: `notify-send` on Linux, `osascript` with `display notification` on macOS, a PowerShell toast on Windows. On Linux an app may also fall back to `gdbus` against the freedesktop service where `notify-send` is missing; the rule does not ask for it. Each is a short program, and the text reaches the program as data (an argument, or an environment variable a fixed script reads), never as part of a script. It runs off the FX thread, and the call times out after ten seconds or less; a failure is logged and never breaks the app.
rules.why: text from a torrent name or a remote shell then cannot run anything.

check.text: one class builds every notification's command line: `notify-send` on Linux, `osascript` on macOS, PowerShell on Windows. Each carries the title and the message as arguments or environment variables of their own, and the script it runs is fixed and never has the text concatenated into it. The program runs on a background thread with a timeout of ten seconds or less that kills it, and a failure is written to the app's log, never thrown further and never dropped: an exception from starting the program or waiting for it, a program that is not there to run, the timeout, and an exit code that is not zero. A test of each platform's command line is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Torrenta [`automation/Notifiers.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/automation/Notifiers.java), [`ProcessNotifier`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/automation/ProcessNotifier.java), [`NotifierTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/test/java/com/torrenta/automation/NotifierTest.java) (it ships [`toast.ps1`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/resources/com/torrenta/automation/toast.ps1), which takes the title and message as parameters); on Linux it runs `notify-send` and has no fallback. It runs each on a virtual thread with a ten-second ceiling and reports a failure to its event log, the first of a session only: the ones after it are dropped ([`automation/Automation.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/automation/Automation.java), `notify`), so Torrenta doesn't meet the last clause yet. Termina's [`ui/DesktopNotifier.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/DesktopNotifier.java) builds its command lines as the rule asks on every OS: the text is an argument of `notify-send` and of `osascript` (a fixed `on run argv` script), a GVariant string for `gdbus`, and on Windows two environment variables that a fixed PowerShell script (`-EncodedCommand`) reads; the program is killed after five seconds and an exception from running it is logged ([`DesktopNotifierTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/ui/DesktopNotifierTest.java)). Termina doesn't meet the last clause in full yet: `post` logs nothing when it finds no tool to run (on Linux, neither `notify-send` nor `gdbus`), when it kills the tool at the timeout, or when the tool exits with an error. Editora's [`terminal/DesktopNotifier.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/terminal/DesktopNotifier.java) builds the same command lines with the same five seconds, but doesn't meet the rule yet: its `post` catches a failure and drops it, with nothing logged. Both fall back to `gdbus`, and so does nux. nux doesn't meet the rule on Windows yet: its [`service/Notifier`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/service/Notifier.java) has no PowerShell toast, and hands the notification to the tray, which shows AWT's balloon ([`tray/AwtTray.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/tray/AwtTray.java), `displayMessage`). Nor does it on macOS: it escapes the title and the message into an AppleScript string (`appleScriptEscape`) and passes the whole script to `osascript -e`. It logs no failure either: a tool that is missing or fails hands the notification to the tray, or to nothing. Its timeout is in the measure: it kills the tool after five seconds.

rules.appliesTo: every app that sends desktop notifications, with a tray or without one: Torrenta and nux for their own events, Editora and Termina for a program's OSC 9 and OSC 777.
rules.text: Desktop notifications are for what happened while the window was away: the app posts none for an event whose window, or whose tab, is the one in front. Each kind of event has a switch of its own, and where the app notifies of several kinds, most of the switches start off.

check.text: the code that posts a notification first tests that the window, or the tab the event belongs to, is not the one in front; each notified kind of event has its own setting; and where the app notifies of several kinds, more of those settings default to off than to on.

rules.reference: Editora ([`ui/TerminalPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TerminalPanel.java)) and Termina ([`ui/TabMarks.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TabMarks.java)) relay a program's own OSC 9 and OSC 777 notifications, one event with one switch, and post nothing while that terminal is focused and in view. Torrenta notifies on added, finished, seeding done, error and updated, each with its switch and only *finished* on at first, and a Test button in Settings shows one now ([`automation/AutomationSettings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/automation/AutomationSettings.java)); it posts them while its window has focus too ([`automation/Automation.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/automation/Automation.java)). nux has one switch for all its power events and a rule per UPS (all, critical or none), not a switch per event, and also posts while its window is in front ([`App`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java)).
