rules.text: A notification is never the only place a state is said: the in-app status already shows it.

check.text: trigger each notified event with notifications off; the window still shows it.

rules.reference: Torrenta's status bar and transfer list.

rules.text: The Settings window opens from a palette command, bound to `Ctrl+,` (`Cmd+,` on macOS) in the CUA keymap. An app with one key table and no CUA keymap, which is a terminal app's own keymap ([KBD-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/keyboard/#kbd-09)) or the built-in table of an app that ships no keymap files, binds the chord in that table.

check.text: a registered command opens Settings, and the CUA keymap binds it to `Ctrl+,` (`C-,` in Editora's `cua.json`) and, on macOS, to `Cmd+,` (`Cmd-,` in `cua.mac.json`). In an app with one key table (a terminal app's `keymap.json` and `keymap.mac.json`, or a table in code), that table binds the two.

rules.reference: Editora `view.settings`, bound in [`keymaps/cua.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/keymaps/cua.json) and [`cua.mac.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/keymaps/cua.mac.json) (and in the VS Code and Sublime keymaps; IntelliJ's uses `C-M-s`). Termina, a terminal app, binds `settings` to `Shortcut+Comma` in its one keymap ([`keymaps/keymap.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/resources/com/termina/keymaps/keymap.json) and [`keymap.mac.json`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/resources/com/termina/keymaps/keymap.mac.json)). Torrenta and nux, which ship no keymap files, bind the same chord in code ([`ui/Chords.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/Chords.java); nux's [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java), `Shortcut+Comma`). Modula doesn't yet: its Settings command has no chord ([`ui/RadioPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/RadioPane.java), `commands`).

rules.text: The Settings window has a sidebar of pages with icons on the left, the open page on the right, and a search field on top.

check.text: open Settings: the pages are listed in a sidebar on the left, each with an icon, the open page fills the right, and the search field sits above both.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/SettingsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsWindow.java), [`ui/SettingsSidebarNav.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsSidebarNav.java), [`ui/SettingsIcons.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsIcons.java).

rules.text: The Settings window's search finds a row by its title, description, visible text, its card or section heading, its page name and English keywords. Title hits rank above description hits; whole words above word starts. The page with the best match opens, and every non-matching row, heading and card is hidden.

check.text: the Settings search matches a query against each row's title, description, visible text, card or section heading, page name and keywords; its score puts a title hit above a description hit and a whole word above a word start; and it opens the page of the best match and hides every row, heading and card that does not match. A unit test that ranks a title hit above a keyword hit and a whole word above part of one is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/SettingsSearch.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsSearch.java), [`SettingsSearchTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsSearchTest.java) (`aTitleHitOutranksAKeywordHitAndAWholeWordOutranksPartOfOne`). Torrenta's search doesn't rank a whole word above part of one yet: its score looks only at where the text was found, title, description or keywords ([`ui/SettingsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/SettingsWindow.java), `rank`).

rules.text: Settings apply live, with no Save button. Text fields commit on Enter or focus loss; invalid values are marked and never committed. A setting that cannot apply until a restart says so on its own row.

check.text: the Settings window has no Save or Apply button, and each control writes its setting and applies it when it changes; a text field commits its value on Enter and when it loses focus (Editora's `commitOnEnterOrBlur`), and a value that fails validation is marked and not written; and every setting the app reads only at startup (the language, the window's style) names the restart in its own row's text.

rules.reference: Editora [`SettingsWindow.commitOnEnterOrBlur`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsWindow.java); [`SettingsSyncPage`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsSyncPage.java)'s branch field marks an invalid branch. Rows that wait for a restart say so: Editora's interface language ("Applies after restarting Editora.", `settings.uiLanguage.note`), and Torrenta's tray icon, which on Windows and macOS "applies after restarting Torrenta" (`settings.general.trayIcon.desc`, in [`ui/SettingsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/SettingsWindow.java)). nux doesn't yet: its Settings window writes nothing until its Save button is pressed, and has a Cancel beside it ([`ui/SettingsWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/SettingsWindow.java)).

rules.text: A setting changed in one window reaches every other open window of the app.

check.text: every window reads its settings from one model the windows share, and a change to that model is announced to each open window, which applies it. An FX test that changes a setting in one window and finds it applied in the other is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora: every window holds the same [`config/SharedConfig.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/SharedConfig.java), which announces each change (`onSettingsChanged`); [`CrossWindowSettingsFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/CrossWindowSettingsFxTest.java).

rules.section: Adding a setting touches five places
rules.text: Every setting the Settings window shows has a palette command that flips the field or prompts for its value. A key that [SET-16](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/settings/#set-16) keeps out of the UI has no row, and takes no command.

check.text: list the settings the Settings window's rows change and the commands the palette lists; each setting has a command that flips it or prompts for its value. A row that only shows something, or runs an action, has no setting to give a command to. A test that fails on a row with no command is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Termina [`ui/SettingCommands.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/SettingCommands.java), a command for each setting or the reason a row needs none ([`SettingCommandsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/ui/SettingCommandsTest.java), `everySettingsRowHasACommandOrSaysWhyNot`), and Mirada [`ui/SettingsPages.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/SettingsPages.java), where every row names its command ([`SettingsPagesTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/ui/SettingsPagesTest.java), `everyPageHasRowsAndEveryRowAPaletteCommand`). Editora has its `view.toggle…` and picker commands ([`ui/WindowCommandRegistrar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/WindowCommandRegistrar.java)) but not one for every setting yet: `terminalNotifications`, for one, is only a Settings row. Modula's palette changes one of its settings, the daylight theme ([`ui/RadioPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/RadioPane.java), `commands`), and nux's three: the tray metric, the notification rule and start at login ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java), `registerCommands`).

rules.text: Config lives in `~/.<app>`, a folder in the user's home on Windows, macOS and Linux alike, unless `<APP>_CONFIG_DIR` or a command-line flag ([CLI-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/command-line/#cli-02)) names another folder. A flag wins over the variable, since what is typed on the command line is the more specific instruction: `--config-dir` first, then `--dev`, then the variable.

check.text: one resolver picks the folder from `--config-dir`, `--dev`, the environment variable and the default, with `--config-dir` first, `--dev` next, the variable after it and the default last, whichever of the two flags is typed first; and the default is `<user.home>/.<app>` on Windows, macOS and Linux alike: the resolver doesn't branch on the OS, or a test resolves the default as each OS and finds the same folder.

rules.reference: the app template's [`config/ConfigDir.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/ConfigDir.java) (`resolve`: `--config-dir`, `--dev`, the variable, then `~/.exampleapp`, with no branch on the OS; [`ConfigDirTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/config/ConfigDirTest.java), `configDirThenDevThenEnvironmentThenPropertyThenTheDefault`). No app has all of it yet. Editora ([`App`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java) and [`ConfigManager.configDirFor`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/ConfigManager.java), [`ConfigDirTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/config/ConfigDirTest.java)), and Termina ([`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/config/Settings.java), `defaultFile`) put `--config-dir` first and have one default for every OS, but the variable wins over `--dev`, which only changes the default. In Mirada either flag wins over the variable, but the two flags set one value and the one typed last wins, so `--config-dir X --dev` gives `~/.mirada-dev` ([`Launch.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/Launch.java), `parse`); and its default depends on the OS ([`settings/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/settings/Settings.java), `defaultFile` and `folder`): `~/Library/Application Support/Mirada` on macOS, `%APPDATA%\Mirada` on Windows, `~/.mirada` elsewhere. Torrenta has `--config-dir`, the variable and the default in that order and no `--dev` ([`store/ConfigDir.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/store/ConfigDir.java)). Modula and nux read a fixed `~/.modula` and `~/.nux`, with no flag and no variable.

rules.text: Preferences live in one file and session state (where the window was, what was open) in another, and every other store has a file of its own. Editora's are `settings.json` and `workspace-state.json`.

check.text: preferences and session state are separate files: the file that holds what the user chose in Settings holds no window geometry and no list of open items.

rules.reference: Editora [`config/ConfigManager.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/ConfigManager.java) (`SETTINGS_FILE_NAME`, `WORKSPACE_FILE_NAME`), [`config/WorkspaceState.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/WorkspaceState.java); Termina [`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/config/Settings.java), which writes the same two names and sorts each key into one of them (`isStateKey`). Torrenta and Mirada keep the window's bounds in their preferences file (`ui.window.bounds` and `window.bounds` in `settings.properties`). The app template meets it: the window and the open documents go to `session.json`, beside `settings.json` and never in it (`SESSION_FILE` in [`config/ConfigStore.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/ConfigStore.java); its [`config/Migrations.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/Migrations.java) moves them out of an older `settings.json`).

rules.text: Every config file the app writes and reads back carries a schema version, and each version has a `v → v+1` migration step. A purely additive field uses an identity step. Which files are config files is in [SET-22](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/settings/#set-22); a plain list with one item to a line, such as a word list, has no shape to version and is exempt.

check.text: the store of every config file ([SET-22](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/settings/#set-22) says which files those are) declares a schema version (`SCHEMA_VERSION` in Editora), writes it into the file and reads it back, and the migrations hold one step for every version below the current one, an identity step where the version only added a field.

rules.reference: Editora [`config/migration/ConfigMigrations.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/migration/ConfigMigrations.java), [`ConfigSchema.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/migration/ConfigSchema.java) (one entry for each store), [`ConfigMigrationsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/config/migration/ConfigMigrationsTest.java); its `dictionary.txt`, one word to a line, is the kind of list the rule exempts. Termina ([`config/ConfigJson.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/config/ConfigJson.java), for `settings.json` and `workspace-state.json`) and Mirada ([`settings/Migrations.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/settings/Migrations.java), for `settings.properties` and `bookmarks.properties`) do it too, and so does the app template for `settings.json` ([`config/Migrations.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/Migrations.java)) and for `session.json` (`SESSION_SCHEMA` in [`config/ConfigStore.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/ConfigStore.java)), Settings Sync's `base.json` and `keybindings.json` ([`sync/SyncData.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/sync/SyncData.java), `SCHEMA_VERSION` and `migrate`) and the account it pins (`account.json`, [`sync/AccountPin.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/sync/AccountPin.java)). Nor does Termina for the color schemes it imports: each is a file Termina writes whole, in a format of its own, and reads back at start (`themes/<name>.properties`, [`theme/ThemeFile.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/theme/ThemeFile.java)), so a config file by [SET-22](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/settings/#set-22), and it carries no version. Torrenta's files ([`store/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/store/Settings.java) and the other stores beside it) and Modula's ([`config/ConfigStore.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/config/ConfigStore.java): `settings.properties`, `presets.txt`, `schedules.txt`, each line a record with fields) carry no version, and nux writes `schema=1` into its file and never reads it ([`config/ConfigStore.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/config/ConfigStore.java), `format` and `parse`).

rules.text: A config file whose schema version ([SET-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/settings/#set-09)) is higher than the running build's is kept as a backup beside it (Editora names it `<name>.v<n>.bak`) and defaults load.
rules.why: an older build never clobbers a newer config.

check.text: the load of each config file compares the file's schema version with the build's, and for a higher one keeps the file as a backup beside it and loads the defaults. A test that loads such a file and finds the backup beside it and the defaults loaded is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`ConfigVersioningTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/config/ConfigVersioningTest.java) (`tooNewSettingsAreBackedUpAndDefaultsLoaded`). Termina ([`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/config/Settings.java)), Mirada ([`settings/ConfigFile.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/settings/ConfigFile.java), `newerBackupOf`) and the app template ([`config/ConfigStore.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/ConfigStore.java)) do the same, under the same name. Torrenta, Modula and nux read no version ([SET-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/settings/#set-09)), so they cannot tell a newer file, and nor can Termina for an imported color scheme, which carries none.

rules.text: Never trust a config file. Clamp every value to its valid range when it is **read**, not only when it is written; an unknown value falls back to its default; a file that cannot be decoded is kept as a backup (Editora names it `<name>.corrupt.bak`) and defaults load. A bad file never stops the app from starting.
rules.why: config is plain JSON (or properties) and people edit it by hand. A hand-edited two-million-line scrollback must not exhaust memory at the next launch (Termina).

check.text: the load clamps each value to its range as it reads it and puts the default in place of an unknown one; a file the parser cannot decode is kept as a backup and the defaults load; and the load catches what the parser throws besides an `IOException` (a malformed `\uXXXX` escape in a `.properties` file throws an `IllegalArgumentException`), so no file stops the start. A test that loads out-of-range numbers and an unparseable file of that kind is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`config/migration/ConfigMigrations.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/migration/ConfigMigrations.java) (`keepCorrupt`), [`ConfigLoadProblemsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/config/ConfigLoadProblemsTest.java) (`outOfRangeNumbersAreClampedOnLoad`, `anUnparseableFileIsReportedWithItsBackup`); Termina [`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/config/Settings.java), [`SettingsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/config/SettingsTest.java) (`aMalformedEscapeNoLongerStopsTheAppStarting`); Mirada [`settings/ConfigFile.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/settings/ConfigFile.java), which moves a file that will not decode to `<name>.corrupt.bak` ([`ConfigFileTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/test/java/com/mirada/settings/ConfigFileTest.java), `aFileThatWillNotDecodeIsKeptAsABackup`). Torrenta, Modula and nux keep no backup, and in Torrenta and nux a malformed escape stops the app from starting.

rules.text: A config file is written whole or not at all: the app writes a temporary file beside it and moves that into place, so a crash mid-write never leaves a half-written file. A config file is any file the app writes as a whole and reads back as its state: the settings, the session state, a store of bookmarks or presets, what a sync engine keeps beside its clone. A file the app only appends to (a log, a ledger, a word list) is not one, and neither is a file in the working tree of a sync repository's clone, which Git holds a committed copy of and the next sync writes again. Nor is a file the app writes for one run and deletes at exit, such as one that tells another process where this run listens.
rules.why: without it, a crash or a full disk in the middle of a save leaves a file that will not decode, and the corrupt-file path of [SET-11](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/settings/#set-11), a backup and then defaults, is what the person gets for it.

check.text: every write of a config file as a whole (a store's save, an import, a sync engine's own state outside its clone) goes to a temporary file in the same folder and ends in a move onto the target (`Files.move`). `ATOMIC_MOVE` is the surest form; a move that only replaces the target passes too, since the statement asks for the temporary file and the move. An append to a log, a ledger or a list is not such a write, and neither is a write into a sync clone's working tree, nor the write of a file the app deletes when it exits.

rules.reference: Editora [`config/ConfigWriter.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/ConfigWriter.java) (`writeAtomicOrThrow`: a temporary file of its own beside the target, forced to disk, then moved; [`ConfigWriterTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/config/ConfigWriterTest.java), `atomicReplacementFailuresKeepThePreviousConfiguration`), which its settings and stores go through. Editora's `mcp-endpoint.json` is not a config file: its MCP server writes it for the run when it starts and deletes it when it stops, as the last window closes ([`mcp/McpServer.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/mcp/McpServer.java), `writeEndpointFile` and `stop`), and one that a crash left behind is deleted at the next launch (`reapStaleEndpoint`). Every other app's settings store does it too: Torrenta [`store/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/store/Settings.java) (`save`), Termina [`config/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/config/Settings.java) (`writeOne`, `moveIntoPlace`), Mirada [`settings/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/settings/Settings.java) (`write`), Modula [`config/ConfigStore.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/config/ConfigStore.java) (`writeAtomically`), nux [`config/ConfigStore.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/config/ConfigStore.java) (`save`) and the app template's [`config/ConfigStore.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/ConfigStore.java) (`writePending`, for `settings.json` and `session.json`). The template's other whole-file writes go the same way, through [`config/ConfigFiles.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/ConfigFiles.java) (`write`): an import ([`config/ConfigImport.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/config/ConfigImport.java), `apply`), Settings Sync's `base.json`, the merge base it keeps beside the clone ([`sync/SyncData.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/sync/SyncData.java), `write`), and the account it pins there ([`sync/AccountPin.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/sync/AccountPin.java)). Termina's [`sync/SyncEngine.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/sync/SyncEngine.java) and Torrenta's [`sync/SyncEngine.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/sync/SyncEngine.java) write in place only inside the clone, and keep their merge base as a Git ref (`refs/termina/base`, `refs/torrenta/base`).

rules.text: Export configuration writes a timestamped `.zip` of the config folder; Import restores from one.

check.text: the export command writes a `.zip` that carries the time of the export in its name and the config folder's files among its entries, and the import command reads such a zip and restores its files. A test of each is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`config/ConfigExporter.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/ConfigExporter.java), [`config/ConfigImport.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/ConfigImport.java), [`ConfigExporterTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/config/ConfigExporterTest.java) (`zipNameDropsLeadingDotAndEmbedsVersionUserTime`, `exportZipsAllFilesWithRelativeEntries`), [`ConfigImportTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/config/ConfigImportTest.java) (`theTickedPartsReplaceTheirsHereAndNothingElseChanges`: Editora's import restores the parts the user ticks).

rules.text: An app that stores a secret the user gave it (a password, a token, a key) puts none in a config file. Each goes to the operating system's keychain: macOS Keychain, Windows Credential Manager, the Secret Service on Linux. Calls may block on a prompt, so they run off the FX thread. Where no keychain answers, as in a Linux session with no Secret Service, the secret is kept in memory for the session only and its row in Settings says so: it is never written to a file instead. A run with no window says so on standard error. A key or token the app generates itself is not such a secret: it may live in a file only the owner can read, outside the settings files (Torrenta's `keys/<name>.key`). Whether a credential is kept from one session to the next is the app's to decide: one it keeps is this rule's, and one it only holds for the session, and asks for again in the next, is [SET-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/settings/#set-14)'s.

check.text: the rule covers an app that keeps a password, an API key or a token the user gave it from one session to the next; an app that keeps none is outside it. In an app it covers, no such secret is a field of the settings model or is written to any other file; reads and writes go through the secret store, and every caller reaches it from a background thread, never from a handler on the FX thread; the store's fallback, for when no keychain answers, holds the secret in memory and writes no file, and the secret's row in Settings says when it is kept for the session only, as a line on standard error does in a run with no window. A key or token the app generates is not judged as such a secret where it is in a file of its own, outside the settings files, that the app makes readable by its owner alone (owner-only permissions, where the file system has them).

rules.reference: Editora [`secrets/SecretStore.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/secrets/SecretStore.java), [`config/ApiKeyVault.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/ApiKeyVault.java). Editora doesn't yet: [`Settings`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/Settings.java) keeps the AI keys as a fallback for when no keychain answers, and saving a key from Settings writes the keychain on the FX thread. Its Settings row does say which of the two holds the key. The bearer token Editora's MCP server generates is in a file of its own for the run, `mcp-endpoint.json`, made owner-only where the file system has POSIX permissions and deleted when the server stops ([`mcp/McpServer.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/mcp/McpServer.java), `writeEndpointFile`), which the rule allows. Torrenta uses no keychain: its proxy password and the password of its Remote access certificate file (`proxy.password` and `webapi.httpsPassword` in `settings.properties`, [`store/Settings.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/store/Settings.java)), its Torznab keys (`search-providers.json`) and its remote-profile passwords (`profiles.json`) are in plain text in its config folder; of its Remote access password it keeps only a hash. The keys Torrenta generates for the updatable torrents it publishes are where the rule allows: a file each, outside the settings files and owner-only where the file system has permissions (`keys/<name>.key`, [`store/KeyStore.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/store/KeyStore.java)). Termina, Mirada and Modula store no secret, so the rule does not cover them: Termina's sync signs in through the user's own Git and `gh` ([`sync/SyncAccount.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/sync/SyncAccount.java)), and the other two ask for none. nux's one credential is for the session only, and so are the SSH passwords and passphrases Editora asks for ([SET-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/settings/#set-14)).

rules.text: An app that asks for a credential it does not keep from one session to the next holds it in memory for the session only and never writes it. Whether to keep a credential is the app's to decide: one it keeps is [SET-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/settings/#set-13)'s, in the keychain and never in a config file, and this rule covers only one it does not keep. Work that needs such a credential waits until the user has signed in this session; do not "fix" that by writing the password to a file.

check.text: for each credential the app asks the user for (a login, a password, a passphrase), find whether the app keeps it for the next session. One it keeps is [SET-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/settings/#set-13)'s and is not judged here. One it does not keep is a field of a runtime object, absent from every config class, and no code writes it to a file. An app that asks for no credential, or keeps every one it asks for, is outside the rule.

rules.reference: nux's UPS login: the user name and password it asks for are two fields of a runtime object ([`app/CommandRunner.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/app/CommandRunner.java)), in no config class. Editora asks for an SSH password or a key's passphrase while a login runs ([`vfs/LoginPrompt.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/vfs/LoginPrompt.java)) and stores neither: a saved connection holds the host, the user and the key's path ([`config/ConnectionStore.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/ConnectionStore.java)). What an app keeps is [SET-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/settings/#set-13)'s alone: Editora's AI keys, and Torrenta's proxy, Torznab and remote-profile secrets. Termina, Mirada and Modula ask for no credential.

rules.text: An app with Settings Sync refuses a repository URL with a password or token in it, and says what to use instead: a Git credential helper or an SSH URL ([Settings Sync](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/settings-sync/)). A problem report's redaction is [DIAG-11](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/diagnostics/#diag-11).

check.text: paste `https://user:token@host/repo.git` as the sync repository: the page refuses it, with a message that says what to use instead.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/SettingsSyncPage.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsSyncPage.java) (`settings.sync.repo.credentials`), which asks [`sync/SyncEngine.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/sync/SyncEngine.java) (`hasCredentials`) as the URL is typed, when the field commits and again at Connect.

rules.text: An option that weakens security has no UI: it exists only as a key in the config file, so nobody turns it on by clicking. An option weakens security when it switches off a check or a question the app otherwise makes to protect the user; a feature, such as remote access or a proxy, is not such an option.

check.text: no Settings row or command writes the key of an option that switches off a check or a question the app otherwise makes to protect the user, whichever of its values is the weaker one: on for nux's `tlsTrustAll`, off for a check the app makes by default.

rules.reference: nux's trust-all TLS (`tlsTrustAll` in [`config/Config.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/config/Config.java)), and Termina's paste confirmation, which only its config file turns off ([`SecurityOptionsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/config/SecurityOptionsTest.java), `noControlOrCommandWritesAWeakeningOption`). Editora doesn't yet: *Require registry signature* for plugins is a Settings checkbox and the `plugins.toggleRequireSignature` command.

rules.appliesTo: an app with Settings Sync.
rules.text: Settings Sync is set up by pasting a repository URL, or with **Create on GitHub** through the `gh` CLI. The account that can read the repository is pinned per clone, so machines with two GitHub accounts work.

check.text: the Sync page takes a repository URL in a field and offers a Create on GitHub action that runs `gh`; and the sync code finds which of the signed-in GitHub accounts can read the repository, records it with the clone, and uses that account for the clone from then on. A test that remembers the first account that can read the repository and uses it without asking again is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`sync/SyncAccount.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/sync/SyncAccount.java), [`SyncAccountTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/sync/SyncAccountTest.java), [`ui/SettingsSyncPage.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsSyncPage.java). The app template's [`sync/AccountPin.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/sync/AccountPin.java) finds the first signed-in `gh` account whose token can read the repository, records it beside the clone and passes it to every fetch and push from then on ([`AccountPinTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/sync/AccountPinTest.java), `theFirstAccountThatCanReadIsPinnedAndKept`).

rules.appliesTo: an app with Settings Sync.
rules.text: Settings Sync runs automatically (on change and at start) and on demand. Machine-local keys (window size, paths) never sync.

check.text: a sync starts by itself after startup and after a local change, and a command starts one on demand (`sync.now` in Editora); and no machine-local key or file (window size, a path) is among those the sync sends to the repository.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/SettingsSync.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsSync.java) (after startup, after a local change, on an interval, and `sync.now`), [`sync/SyncCategory.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/sync/SyncCategory.java); Torrenta [`sync/SyncKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/sync/SyncKeys.java).

rules.appliesTo: an app with Settings Sync.
rules.text: When Settings Sync finds one entry changed on both sides, *this machine wins*, and a backup is taken before any sync that replaces local files.

check.text: the merge keeps this machine's value for an entry both sides changed, and the sync copies the local files to a backup before it replaces them. A merge test where both sides changed one entry is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`sync/SyncMerge.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/sync/SyncMerge.java), [`SyncMergeTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/sync/SyncMergeTest.java); the app template's [`sync/SyncMerge.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/sync/SyncMerge.java) and [`ui/SyncController.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/SyncController.java) (`backUp`, which copies `settings.json` to `backups/` before a merge replaces the local bindings; [`SyncControllerFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/SyncControllerFxTest.java), `aSyncThatReplacesLocalSettingsBacksThemUpFirst`).

rules.appliesTo: an app with Settings Sync.
rules.text: Settings Sync shows its status as a pill in Settings and as echo messages; its failures go to the Message Log.

check.text: point Sync at a repository that does not exist: the pill in Settings shows the failure, the echo area says it, and the Message Log keeps it.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/SettingsSyncPage.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsSyncPage.java), [`SyncStatus`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SyncStatus.java).

rules.text: The **Message Log** is a session-only, bounded history of every echo-area message with `HH:mm:ss` times, newest first. Esc closes it; Clear empties it. What opens it, a click on the echo area, is [WIN-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-01)'s to require; the [Message Log template](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/message-log/) has the rest.

check.text: every message the echo area shows is added, with its time, to one log held in memory and never written to disk; the log drops its oldest entry past a fixed count and lists the rest newest first with `HH:mm:ss` times; and its window closes on Esc and has a Clear action that empties it. A test that records messages newest first, evicts the oldest past the cap, and clears is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/MessageLog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLog.java) ([`MessageLogTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLogTest.java)), [`ui/MessageLogPopup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLogPopup.java).

rules.text: The **Debug Log** captures all `java.util.logging` records and uncaught exceptions in memory (bounded) **and** mirrors them to a session file in the config folder, keeping the previous session's file so a crash is still visible next launch. Editora names the two `<app>-session.log` and `<app>-session.prev.log`.

check.text: a handler on the root `java.util.logging` logger and the uncaught exception handler feed one bounded buffer in memory and a session file in the config folder, and at start the last session's file is kept under a second name before the new one is begun. Tests that bound the buffer and find the session file written and the previous one kept are the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/DebugLog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/DebugLog.java) ([`DebugLogTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/DebugLogTest.java), [`DebugLogSessionFileTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/DebugLogSessionFileTest.java)).

rules.text: The Debug Log opens in a modeless window with Refresh, Copy, Clear, Export and Report a Problem. The window's find bar is [FIND-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/find-bar/#find-01).
rules.why: it is the only way to see logs in a packaged build.

check.text: the Debug Log's window is a stage with no modality, so the main window keeps working while it is open, and it carries the five actions: Refresh, Copy, Clear, Export and Report a Problem.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/DebugLogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/DebugLogWindow.java). Termina's, Mirada's and the app template's windows have the five actions too; Torrenta's has no Export ([`ui/DebugLogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/DebugLogWindow.java)). Modula and nux have no Debug Log ([DIAG-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/diagnostics/#diag-02)).

rules.text: An **uncaught exception handler** is installed at the start of `main`, before the toolkit starts, and routes to the Debug Log and an echo message. Never a stack trace dialog.

check.text: `main` calls the install method before any argument handling or `launch`, and the handler posts an error to the echo area, and opens no dialog.

rules.reference: Editora [`DebugLog.install()`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/DebugLog.java) for the install and the log. The echo message is posted by Termina ([`ui/WindowManager.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/WindowManager.java), through `DebugLog.onUncaught`), the app template ([`ui/Startup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Startup.java)) and Mirada ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/App.java), `uncaught`). Editora's handler and Torrenta's ([`ui/DebugLog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/DebugLog.java)) log the exception but do not yet post one.

rules.text: The **update check** reads GitHub `/releases/latest`. The automatic check runs once per app session (not per window), at most once a day, and starts at least three seconds after the first frame ([PERF-15](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/performance/#perf-15)); a check the user asks for ([DIAG-10](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/diagnostics/#diag-10)) runs when asked. It never downloads or installs anything by itself.

check.text: the code that starts the automatic check waits for the first frame and then a delay of three seconds or more before it asks GitHub's `/releases/latest` for the app's repository (Editora's `AfterFirstPaint`, then a pause of five seconds); it asks once for the whole process, however many windows open, and not at all when the last check, whose time the app keeps from one session to the next, was less than a day ago, or when the setting is off ([DIAG-10](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/diagnostics/#diag-10)); and what it does with the answer is show it: no code downloads or installs a release. A test that asserts the wait, the one check a session and the two skips is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`update/UpdateCheck.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/update/UpdateCheck.java), [`ui/UpdateCheckScheduler.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/UpdateCheckScheduler.java) ([`UpdateCheckSchedulerTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/UpdateCheckSchedulerTest.java), `waitsForTheFirstPaintThenTheDelayThenStampsAndChecks` and `onlyOnceASessionAndNotWhenOffOrNotDue`), [`ui/UpdateCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/UpdateCoordinator.java); Editora waits five seconds (`UpdateCheckScheduler.DELAY`). Termina ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/App.java), three seconds after its first frame), Mirada ([`update/UpdateCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/update/UpdateCoordinator.java), `scheduleStartupCheck`, five seconds) and the app template ([`ui/UpdateCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/UpdateCoordinator.java), started from [`ui/Startup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Startup.java) after the first paint, five seconds) wait the same way. Three apps don't wait yet: Torrenta starts its check as soon as its engine is ready ([`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java), `maybeCheckForUpdates`), and Modula ([`ModulaApp.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ModulaApp.java), `checkForUpdates`) and nux ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java), `maybeCheckForUpdates`) start theirs inside `start()`.

rules.text: When the update check ([DIAG-05](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/diagnostics/#diag-05)) finds a newer version, the status bar says so, naming the version and linking its release. About's line for the last check is [ABOUT-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/about/#about-02).

check.text: when a check finds a newer version, the app shows a notice in the status bar that names that version, and the notice, or a link beside it in the bar, opens that release's page (Editora's `UpdateCoordinator` shows a status-bar segment whose click opens the release).

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/UpdateCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/UpdateCoordinator.java). Mirada ([`ui/StatusBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/StatusBar.java)) and the app template ([`ui/StatusBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/StatusBar.java)) show a link in the bar, and Torrenta a badge there that opens the release ([`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java), `updateBadge`). check.text: the window's report field is editable; its submit action puts the field's text on the clipboard and opens a new-issue link that names `bug_report.yml` as its template and carries the report in the form's fields; and the report's code opens that link in the browser and makes no network request of its own.

Termina's [`ui/ReportProblemWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/ReportProblemWindow.java), Torrenta's [`ui/ReportProblemWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/ReportProblemWindow.java), Mirada's [`ui/ReportProblemWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/ReportProblemWindow.java) and the app template's [`ui/ReportProblemWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/ReportProblemWindow.java) do the same.
