rules.text: An option the app does not know stops the launch: it names the option on standard error, says how to get help, and exits with status 2 before the GUI starts. That holds for an option with one dash as for one with two: it is never ignored and never taken for a file. Two kinds of argument are not unknown options. In an app that opens files named on its command line, a lone `-`, and every argument after `--`, is one of those files, whatever it starts with; that sentence does not cover an app that opens none. And the JVM options a launcher can leave among the program's arguments, `--add-exports`, `--add-opens` and `-p`, are skipped by name, each with its value, whether the value is the next argument or follows `=` in the same one (`--add-exports=…`): never refused, and the value never opened as a file. On Windows the message prints in the console, which is [CLI-11](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/command-line/#cli-11).
rules.why: a mistyped `--config-dir` that is ignored starts the app on the real settings, which is the one thing the flag was typed to avoid. Status 2 is what a script tests for a usage error. `--` is how a file whose name starts with a dash is opened at all. A launcher's own option is not the user's mistake, so it must not stop the app; it is skipped by name because a parser that skips whatever it does not know is the one that ignores a typo.

check.text: the parser `main` runs before the GUI refuses an option the app does not define, with two dashes or with one, and `main` then prints the option and how to get help on standard error and exits with status 2 before `launch`. In an app that opens files named on its command line, the parser takes a lone `-`, and a name that starts with a dash after `--`, for files; in an app that opens none, this part has nothing to find. And the parser skips `--add-exports`, `--add-opens` and `-p` with their values, in both forms a launcher writes (`--add-exports <value>` and `--add-exports=<value>`), with no error and no file. A test that hands the parser each of these arguments is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: the app template's [`cli/CommandLine.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/cli/CommandLine.java) does all of it: it refuses an unknown option with one dash or two ([`Main.run`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/Main.java) prints the message and returns 2) and takes `-` and whatever follows `--` for files, and skips `--add-exports`, `--add-opens` and `-p` with their values in both forms ([`CommandLineTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/cli/CommandLineTest.java), `reportsMistakes`, `acceptsTheEqualsFormAndDoubleDash` and `skipsTheLaunchersJvmOptionsAndTakesCapitalVForVersion`). No other app does all of it yet. Termina's [`cli/CommandLine.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/cli/CommandLine.java) and Torrenta's [`cli/CommandLine.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/cli/CommandLine.java) refuse both kinds of unknown option with status 2, and the launcher's options with them. Torrenta, which opens the `.torrent` files and magnet links named on its command line, also refuses `-` and `--`: anything that starts with a dash and is not a magnet link. Termina opens no files from its command line, so that part of the rule does not cover it (it refuses `-` as an unexpected argument and `--` as an unknown option); the launcher's options are all it misses. Mirada's [`Launch.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/Launch.java) exits 2 on an unknown option with two dashes, `--add-exports` and `--add-opens` among them, and takes `-` and whatever follows `--` for files, but it takes a single-dash option, `-p` included, for a file too. Editora skips every option it does not know without a word, a lone `-` included, and has no `--` ([`App.fileTargets`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java)); that is how it gets past a leaked `--add-exports`, `--add-opens` or `-p`, whose value it opens only when a file of that name exists ([`AppArgsTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/AppArgsTest.java)). nux reads `--minimized` and `--screenshot=` and ignores every other argument ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java)), and Modula reads none ([`ModulaApp.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ModulaApp.java)); neither opens files, so what they miss is the refusal.

rules.text: The short flags are the same in every app: `-h` for `--help`, and both `-v` and `-V` for `--version`.

check.text: the command-line parser takes `-h` for `--help`, and `-v` and `-V` for `--version`.

rules.reference: Termina's [`cli/CommandLine.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/cli/CommandLine.java) and Torrenta's [`cli/CommandLine.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/cli/CommandLine.java); the `--help` text of both lists `-h` and `-v` and leaves `-V` out. The app template's [`cli/CommandLine.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/cli/CommandLine.java) takes all three, and its `--help` text lists them. Editora takes `-h` and `-V` but not `-v`, Mirada has no short flags, and Modula and nux take neither flag in any form.

rules.text: On Windows, `--help`, `--version` and `--report` print in the console they were typed in, and so does the message that refuses an unknown option ([CLI-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/command-line/#cli-12)). A GUI launcher has no console, so the installer also carries a console launcher (jpackage's `win-console`) that runs the same entry point, or `main` attaches to the parent's console before it prints.
rules.why: without it, the three flags and a mistyped option print nothing from cmd or PowerShell, and the command line differs on one OS.

check.text: the Windows jpackage configuration adds a launcher with `win-console=true` that runs the app's own main class and lets the three flags and an unknown option reach it, or `main` calls `AttachConsole` before printing.

rules.reference: Torrenta meets it with its second launcher, `torrenta-nox`: [`src/jpackage/torrenta-nox-windows.properties`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/jpackage/torrenta-nox-windows.properties) sets `win-console=true`, and its [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/pom.xml) adds that launcher to the image on Windows (the `os-windows` profile picks the file), beside the main launcher and on the same module and main class. The launcher's own `arguments=--headless` applies only when the person gives none (its [`CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/CLAUDE.md) says so), so `torrenta-nox --help`, `--version`, `--report` and an option it does not know reach `main` as typed, and `main` refuses the unknown option and answers the three flags before it looks for `--headless` ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/App.java)). The app template does it the same way: its `os-windows` profile in [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/pom.xml) adds a second launcher, `exampleapp-cli`, whose [`packaging/windows/exampleapp-cli.properties`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/packaging/windows/exampleapp-cli.properties) sets `win-console=true` and nothing else, so it runs the same main class with the arguments as typed. No other app has a `win-console` launcher or calls `AttachConsole`. Mirada's one Windows executable is its native image, copied over jpackage's launcher ([`native-app-image.sh`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/scripts/native-app-image.sh)); whether it prints in the console depends on how that image is linked, which Mirada's files do not say, and no Windows run has confirmed it.

rules.text: An app that opens files or folders (documents, images, a `.torrent`) opens the ones named as arguments on its command line, which its `--help` lists as `[files…]`.

check.text: launch with two files and find both open, and run `--help` and find `[files…]` in its usage line.

rules.reference: Editora [`App.fileTargets`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java). Termina, Modula and nux open no files, so the rule does not cover them.

rules.text: One instance runs per config folder, unless a launch asks for another with `--new-instance` ([CLI-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/command-line/#cli-03)). Any other second launch hands its arguments, when it has any, to the running app over a local endpoint and exits. In an app that opens files, the `openFiles` Apple Events of macOS reach the running app too.

check.text: the first launch on a config folder becomes the primary and listens on a local endpoint; a second launch without `--new-instance` sends it its arguments and exits; and, in an app that opens files, a handler for the macOS open-files event passes them to the running app (Editora's `MacOpenFiles`). A test that makes the first launch primary and delivers a second launch's arguments to it is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`ipc/SingleInstance.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ipc/SingleInstance.java) ([`SingleInstanceTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ipc/SingleInstanceTest.java)), [`MacOpenFiles.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/MacOpenFiles.java). nux doesn't yet: its second launch asks the running app to show its window and exits, handing over none of its arguments ([`instance/SingleInstance.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/instance/SingleInstance.java), `NUX-SHOW`), and what lets a second instance run on the folder is a setting (`singleInstance`, read in `main` of [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/App.java)), not `--new-instance`.

rules.text: An advisory lock tells two processes on one config folder about each other.

check.text: each process takes an advisory file lock in its config folder, and can tell that another process already holds one there. A test that takes the lock from two processes is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`config/InstanceLock.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/config/InstanceLock.java) ([`InstanceLockTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/config/InstanceLockTest.java)).

rules.text: `main` sets `java.awt.headless=true` before any AWT class loads. Only these uses make AWT headful, in an app that has them: the tray on Windows and macOS, and on macOS the dock badge, the open-file handlers and Move to Trash. Linux never needs it. `main` decides once, before that point, which of them the settings ask for on this OS. What a tray app says when its tray is turned on after that is [TRAY-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/tray-and-background/#tray-14).
rules.why: on macOS, AWT's native toolkit and JavaFX contend for the one AppKit run loop and can hang; headless Java2D still draws to images.

check.text: `main` calls `System.setProperty("java.awt.headless", …)` before `launch` and before anything that loads an AWT class, and the value is `"true"` unless one of the listed uses is wanted on this OS: always on Linux, on Windows unless the tray is on, and on macOS unless the tray, the dock badge, an open-file handler or, in an app that trashes through AWT, Move to Trash is.

rules.reference: Editora [`App.main`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java), always headless, as Termina ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/App.java)) and the app template ([`Main.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/Main.java)) are. Torrenta [`os/AwtUse.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/os/AwtUse.java) (`headful`, which its `App.main` asks once: never on Linux, for the tray on Windows, and for the tray, the dock badge or the open-file handlers on macOS). Mirada [`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/App.java) (headless except on macOS, for Move to Trash: [`os/Trash.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/os/Trash.java), `headless`). Modula and nux never set the property, so AWT is headful on every OS, Linux included.

rules.text: An app that starts external tools (`git`, a compiler, `ffmpeg`) resolves them through the login shell's `PATH` on macOS and Linux. Windows has no login shell's `PATH` to ask for, and the one the app inherits is used there.
rules.why: a `.app` launched from Finder inherits a stripped `PATH`.

check.text: on macOS and Linux, every process the app starts gets a `PATH` that includes the login shell's. An app that starts no external tool is outside the rule.

rules.reference: Editora [`process/ProcessRunner.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/process/ProcessRunner.java) (`augmentedPath`; on Windows its login-shell probe returns nothing and the inherited `PATH` is used). The app template's [`sync/ShellPath.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/sync/ShellPath.java) does the same for the `git` and `gh` it starts: the login shell's `PATH` before the inherited one on macOS and Linux, the inherited one on Windows ([`ShellPathTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/sync/ShellPathTest.java)).

rules.text: The app ships a message catalog for each of at least six languages: English (the base), Spanish, Portuguese, French, Italian and German.

check.text: the six `messages*.properties` files are in the app's `i18n` resources.

rules.reference: Editora [`src/main/resources/com/editora/i18n/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/tree/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/i18n).

rules.text: A new language is a `messages_<code>.properties` with every key, listed in the Settings language picker and in the parity test.

check.text: the language's code is in `Messages`' language list (which the picker shows) and in the catalog list the parity test walks.

rules.reference: Editora [`i18n/Messages.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/i18n/Messages.java) (`LANGUAGES`, `available()`); [`MessagesTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/i18n/MessagesTest.java)'s `LOCALES` and `ALL_CATALOGS`, after which `translationCatalogsHaveExactlyTheBaseKeySet` holds it to the same keys as the others.

rules.text: Every value is translated for real: no English value is shipped in another language's catalog.

check.text: compare each catalog's values with the base; a value identical to the English one is a name, a term or a bare pattern that stays the same in that language ("Git: Pull (Rebase)", "{0} · {1}"), never an untranslated sentence. No test catches it, so it is also checked in review.

rules.reference: Editora `messages_*.properties`.

rules.text: The layout holds in every language at 1024 px wide: rows wrap, never cut. German is today's longest.

check.text: run the app in each language with the window 1024 px wide, open each window and Settings page, and find no row cut off.

rules.reference: Editora [`messages_de.properties`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/i18n/messages_de.properties).

rules.text: A Chinese, Japanese or Korean catalog comes with a font fallback for its script.
rules.why: Inter has no CJK glyphs. JavaFX falls back to whatever font the OS has, so without a bundled one the text looks different on each OS, and a minimal Linux install may have none.

check.text: run the app in that language and look for missing-glyph boxes.

rules.reference: no app yet.

rules.text: An Arabic or Hebrew catalog sets `NodeOrientation.RIGHT_TO_LEFT` on every scene.

check.text: the scene setup sets the node orientation from the current language.

rules.reference: no app yet.

rules.text: No raw English literal is passed to a control: every string comes from the catalog, by its key, through one lookup in one class (`tr("some.key")` in Editora's `Messages`).

check.text: no source file passes a string literal in a text position: a control's constructor, `setText`, `setPromptText`, `setTitle`, a tooltip, a menu item or a command's label. Each takes its text from the catalog's lookup, which is one method of one class (Editora's `Messages.tr`). A test that scans the sources and fails on such a literal is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`i18n/Messages.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/i18n/Messages.java). The tests that hold the rule are Torrenta's [`UiStringSweepTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/test/java/com/torrenta/i18n/UiStringSweepTest.java) (`noStringLiteralInATextPosition`) and nux's [`NoLiteralUiTextTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/test/java/com/nux/i18n/NoLiteralUiTextTest.java) (`userFacingTextGoesThroughTheCatalogue`). Editora's [`MessagesTest.everyLiteralKeyUsedInTheSourcesExists`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/i18n/MessagesTest.java) checks only that every key a `tr("…")` call names is in the base catalog, not that no literal reaches a control.

rules.text: Every catalog has every key of the base catalog, and no more, each with a non-empty value.

check.text: compare each translated catalog's keys with the base catalog's: none is missing, none is extra, and no value is empty. A parity test that fails the build on any of the three is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`MessagesTest.translationCatalogsHaveExactlyTheBaseKeySet`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/i18n/MessagesTest.java), `translationsAreNonEmptyAndDistinctFromKeys`.

rules.text: In a catalog value with a placeholder, a literal apostrophe is doubled; in a value without one, it is written once. Inside a `{0,choice,…}` limb ([INTL-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/i18n/#intl-12)) that itself holds a placeholder, it is written four times; in a limb without one it is doubled, like the rest of the value.
rules.why: a value with a placeholder is a `MessageFormat` pattern, where a lone apostrophe starts a quoted section and can swallow the placeholder after it; a value without one is shown exactly as written. A choice limb that holds a placeholder is parsed a second time as a pattern of its own, and each pass halves the apostrophes.

check.text: in every catalog, a value with a placeholder has no lone apostrophe and a value without one has no doubled apostrophe; a choice limb that holds a placeholder writes a literal apostrophe four times, and a limb that holds none writes it twice. Catalog tests that fail each of the four mistakes are the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`MessagesTest.aValueWithAPlaceholderNeverHasALoneApostrophe`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/i18n/MessagesTest.java), `aValueWithoutAPlaceholderNeverDoublesAnApostrophe`. The choice limbs are held by Torrenta's [`MessagesTest.apostrophesInsideChoiceLimbsAreQuotedForTheRightNumberOfPasses`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/test/java/com/torrenta/i18n/MessagesTest.java) (`diagnosis.unavailable` in its [`messages_fr.properties`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/resources/com/torrenta/i18n/messages_fr.properties) writes "n''''est" in a limb with `{1}`); Editora's test has no such case.

rules.text: Identifiers such as line numbers and ports use `{0,number,#}`, so they are not digit-grouped.

check.text: in every catalog, a placeholder the code fills with an identifier (a line number, a port) carries the `number,#` format, as in `{0,number,#}`, and is never a bare `{0}`. A test that formats each identifier argument in every locale and fails on a grouped number is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`MessagesTest.identifierArgumentsAreNeverDigitGrouped`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/i18n/MessagesTest.java).

rules.text: Technical identifiers stay untranslated: command ids, setting keys, file names and protocol names read the same in every language. The `--help` and `--version` text is [CLI-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/command-line/#cli-01).

check.text: compare each translated catalog with the base, key by key: a command id, a setting key, a file name or a protocol name in the base value appears, spelled the same, in the translated value. A made-up example name inside a value (`name.gpg`) is not an identifier, and may be translated.

rules.reference: Editora's catalogs ([`messages.properties`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/i18n/messages.properties) and its translations).

rules.text: A message with a count words it for the count, with a `{0,choice,…}` limb for each form the language needs: never "file(s)".
rules.why: "(s)" is English; other languages change more than one ending, and the translator can only get it right with the forms written out.

check.text: no catalog value has a placeholder and `(s)`; a message with a count has a `{0,choice,…}` pattern with a limb for each form its language needs, and every such pattern parses. A catalog test that fails a value with a placeholder and `(s)`, and parses every `choice` pattern in every catalog, is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Torrenta's `omni.targets.matching` in [`messages.properties`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/resources/com/torrenta/i18n/messages.properties), parsed in every language by [`MessagesTest.placeholdersMatchAcrossLanguagesAndEveryPatternParses`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/test/java/com/torrenta/i18n/MessagesTest.java). That test only parses the patterns: no app has the `(s)` test yet, and Editora's base catalog has 22 values with a placeholder and `(s)` (`find.replaced`, "Replaced {0} occurrence(s)").

rules.text: A chord's modifiers read the same in every language: `Ctrl`, `Alt`, `Shift` and the macOS glyphs are never translated ("Ctrl", not "Strg").
rules.why: the keymaps, the docs and the screenshots use one spelling, and a user who changes the language keeps the chords they learned.

check.text: the code that writes a chord out takes its modifier names from constants, not the catalog, and no catalog value writes a modifier in another language: a catalog test looks for Strg, Umschalt, Maj, Mayús and Maiusc.

rules.reference: Editora [`command/ChordFormat.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/command/ChordFormat.java) writes chords with untranslated modifiers. Its catalogs do not hold the rule yet: they translate modifiers in prose ("Strg+D", "Mayús+Tab", "Maj+Entrée") and in the Project Map help's key names ([`messages_de.properties`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/i18n/messages_de.properties), `project.map.help.key.control=Strg`, read by [`ui/ProjectMapHelp.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ProjectMapHelp.java)). No app has the catalog test yet.

rules.text: The app starts in the language the user chose in its settings, where it offers that choice; with none chosen, in the system's language when it ships a catalog for it; otherwise in English. The locale that formats dates and numbers keeps the system's region: with no language chosen it is the system's locale whole, whatever language the menus are in, and with one chosen it is still the system's locale when that is the system's own language, and the bare language only when it is another. That locale is the JVM's default once the app has started: the app sets it wherever it is not the locale the JVM started with. The message catalog formats its values with it too, never with a locale of its own made from the bare language.
rules.why: `de-AT` collapsed to `de` writes an Austrian's numbers and dates the German way, and an English UI on a French system has no reason to change how its dates are written. Apps that settle this differently format the same date two ways side by side, and so does one app whose catalog formats a message's number with another locale than the rest of the window.

check.text: the start-up code takes the stored choice, the system's locale and the catalogs the app ships and gives the language and the locale as the four cases ask: none chosen with a catalog for the system's language (the system's locale whole); none chosen without one (English, the system's locale kept whole); the system's own language chosen (its region kept); another language chosen (the bare language). It sets that locale as the JVM's default (`Locale.setDefault`) as it starts, wherever that is not the locale the JVM started with: an app that offers no language choice and ships no catalogs leaves the default alone, which is the system's locale whole, and meets this part. And the catalog's lookup formats a value with the default locale (`new MessageFormat(pattern)`, or `MessageFormat.format`), not with one it builds from the language code (`Locale.forLanguageTag`). A test that covers the four cases is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Termina [`i18n/Messages.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/i18n/Messages.java) (`resolve`, `defaultLocale`, and `tr`, which formats with the default locale) with [`MessagesTest.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/test/java/com/termina/i18n/MessagesTest.java) (`automaticKeepsTheOperatingSystemsLocaleWhole`, `anExplicitChoiceMovesTheLocaleButKeepsAMatchingCountry`). Torrenta carries the same two functions and tests and sets the default from them ([`Startup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/Startup.java), `language`), but doesn't meet the rule yet: its catalog formats every message with the bare language ([`i18n/Messages.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/i18n/Messages.java), `locale`), so a number inside a message loses the region the rest of the window keeps. nux's [`i18n/Messages.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/i18n/Messages.java) (`uiLocale`, [`UiLocaleTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/test/java/com/nux/i18n/UiLocaleTest.java)) keeps the region when the language is the system's, but with none chosen and no catalog for the system's language it sets bare English. Editora ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/App.java)) and Mirada ([`App.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/App.java)) set the default to the bare language every time, so the region is lost; Mirada's catalog formats with the bare language as well ([`i18n/Messages.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/i18n/Messages.java)). The app template meets it: its [`i18n/Messages.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/i18n/Messages.java) gives the four cases (`locale`), sets the result as the JVM's default where it differs (`start`) and formats with `new MessageFormat(value)` (`render`); its [`MessagesTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/i18n/MessagesTest.java) (`theFormattingLocaleKeepsTheSystemsRegion`) covers the four. Modula ships no catalogs and offers no language choice, and leaves the JVM's locale as the system set it, which is the locale the rule asks for: it meets this rule, and its missing catalogs are [INTL-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/i18n/#intl-01)'s.

rules.text: Every app has a Command Palette, one in each main window, opened by the `palette.show` command. A Settings, About or log window needs none of its own. Its chords, `M-x` in the Emacs keymap and `Ctrl+Shift+P` (`Cmd+Shift+P` on macOS) in the others (`Ctrl+Shift+A` allowed in the IntelliJ keymap), are [KBD-05](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/keyboard/#kbd-05).

check.text: each main window builds one palette, and the command registered as `palette.show` opens it (in Editora the window controller builds one `CommandPalette`). A window that is not a main window (Settings, About, a log, a history or events window) is not judged.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java), built once in [`MainController`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java).

rules.text: The palette lists every registered command, with its title and description ([KBD-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/keyboard/#kbd-03)).

check.text: the palette's rows come from the whole registry, filtered only by the query; a command that cannot run stays listed, grayed; each row shows its command's title; and the palette shows the description of the command under the cursor, in the row or in a line of the card. A palette that shows no description fails this rule; that every command has one is [KBD-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/keyboard/#kbd-03)'s.

rules.reference: Editora [`CommandPalette.filter`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java) (`registry.all()`), [`MessagesTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/i18n/MessagesTest.java); the page's [Spec](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/command-palette/#spec). Torrenta's, Modula's and nux's palettes don't yet. Torrenta's lists only the commands that can run now: `show` in [`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/CommandPalette.java) drops every disabled command, after `offeredCommands` in [`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java) has dropped what the engine cannot run and what Simple mode hides; and it shows no description, since its [`Command`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/Command.java) has none. Modula's leaves out one (`stereo`, while its control is disabled, in [`ui/RadioPane.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/RadioPane.java)), and its rows show a title and a shortcut, with no description ([`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/CommandPalette.java)). nux's lists its whole registry, and each row shows the title and the command's id, with no description: its commands have none ([`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/CommandPalette.java), `CommandCell`; [`command/CommandRegistry.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/command/CommandRegistry.java)).

rules.text: The palette is 620 px wide, its rows 36 px high with 8 visible before the list scrolls, at the default zoom ([WIN-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-12)), and its field's prompt reads "Run command…", in words from the catalog (Editora's key for them is `palette.prompt`).
rules.why: the palette is the one window every app shares; a different width or prompt is the first thing a person moving between apps notices.

check.text: the palette's width, row height and visible rows come from constants of these values, and its prompt is read from the catalog, where the English is "Run command…". The rule asks for the words, not for a catalog key.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java) (`ROW_HEIGHT`, `VISIBLE_ROWS`), Torrenta, Termina and the app template's [`ui/Picker.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Picker.java). Mirada's [`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/CommandPalette.java) matches the three sizes and reads the same words from the catalog under another key, `palette.runCommandPrompt`. Modula's is 420 px with a literal "Type a command…", and nux's 540 px with a `palette.prompt` that reads "Type a command…".

rules.text: Every open starts with an empty query: the palette does not keep the last one, so it opens on the whole list ([PAL-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/command-palette/#pal-02)).

check.text: `show` clears the field and filters on the empty query before the card appears.

rules.reference: Editora [`CommandPalette.show`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java).

rules.text: Typing in the palette filters its list, and the first *enabled* match is selected.

check.text: after each filter the palette selects the first row whose command can run, stepping over disabled rows at the top (Editora's `selectFirstEnabled`). A test that asserts it, with a disabled command at the top, is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`CommandPalette.selectFirstEnabled`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java), [`CommandPaletteDisabledFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPaletteDisabledFxTest.java).

rules.text: The active keymap's line and page chords move the selection, as do ↑ ↓ and Page Up/Down, which always work. In Editora they are the chords of its `nav.lineDown`, `nav.lineUp`, `nav.pageDown` and `nav.pageUp` commands, `C-n` and `C-p` among them in the Emacs keymap. Enter, or a click on an enabled row, runs the command. The palette closes first, then the command runs.

check.text: the palette's key handler looks a press up in the active keymap and moves on the commands it binds for a line and a page up and down, not on fixed letters, and on ↑ ↓ and Page Up/Down whatever the keymap; the run path hides the card before it calls the registry, and does nothing on a disabled row.

rules.reference: Editora [`CommandPalette.runSelected`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java), [`PickerKeys.resolve`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/PickerKeys.java), and the app template's [`ui/PickerKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/PickerKeys.java) (`resolve`, for its [`ui/Picker.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Picker.java)), which reads the keymap's `nav.lineDown`, `nav.lineUp`, `nav.pageDown` and `nav.pageUp` beside the fixed keys: the two palettes that ask the keymap. The others move on fixed keys: Termina's [`ui/PaletteKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/PaletteKeys.java) and Mirada's [`ui/PaletteKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/PaletteKeys.java) on a fixed table of Emacs chords beside them (`EMACS`: `C-n`, `C-p`, `C-v`, `M-v`); Torrenta's [`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/CommandPalette.java) (`onKey`) on the arrows and `Ctrl+N` and `Ctrl+P`, with no page keys; Modula's [`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/CommandPalette.java) and nux's [`ui/CommandPalette.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/CommandPalette.java) on the arrows alone.

rules.text: The active keymap's cancel chord, Esc or a click on the scrim cancels the palette, and focus returns to where it was. In Editora the chord is that of its `edit.cancel` command, `C-g` in the Emacs keymap.

check.text: Esc, the chord the active keymap binds to the cancel command, and a press on the backdrop all hide the overlay, and hiding focuses the node that had focus before it opened. In an app with one key table (a terminal app's keymap, or the built-in table of an app that ships no keymap files), the chord is the one that table binds to a cancel command; where it binds none, Esc and the backdrop are all there is to test.

rules.reference: Editora [`PickerKeys`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/PickerKeys.java) (`isCancel`), [`OverlayHost`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/OverlayHost.java) (`previousFocus`), and the app template's [`ui/OverlayHost.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/OverlayHost.java) (`cancelOn`, which [`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MainWindow.java) hands the keymap's `edit.cancel` chord, `C-g` in its Emacs keymap, and `hide`, which gives the focus back): the two that ask the keymap for the chord. `Ctrl+G` is fixed in the `EMACS` table of Termina's [`ui/PaletteKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/PaletteKeys.java) and Mirada's [`ui/PaletteKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/PaletteKeys.java). Torrenta's, Modula's and nux's palettes cancel on Esc and on a press on the backdrop: none of the three apps has a keymap or a cancel command, so the chord asks nothing more of them.

rules.text: In the palette, a help chord opens the selected command's page in the docs on the website, for the running version. The chord is the first of `Ctrl+H`, `F1` and `Shift+F1` that the active keymap leaves free. It is the same on macOS, where `Ctrl+H` is the Control key and has no `Cmd` form (`C-h` in Emacs notation).

check.text: the palette's help chord is the first of the three that the active keymap neither binds nor starts a longer chord with, and the URL it opens is built from the app's versioned docs address and the selected command's id.

rules.reference: Editora [`CommandPalette`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java) ([`PickerKeys.freeChord`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/PickerKeys.java) over `C-h`, `f1` and `S-f1`; `docsUrl`), [`AppInfo.docsUrl`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/AppInfo.java). The app template's [`ui/PickerKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/PickerKeys.java) (`HELP_CHORDS`, `helpChord`) picks the chord the same way, and the palette opens the command's page under its versioned docs ([`PickerFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/PickerFxTest.java), `helpTitleCurrentValueAndTheEnds`). No other app's palette has a help chord yet.

rules.text: A live keymap switch re-renders the palette's key chips, its opener chip and its key legend.

check.text: applying a new keymap calls the palette's rebind method, which rebuilds the opener, the legend and the rows.

rules.reference: Editora [`CommandPalette.refreshBindings`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CommandPalette.java), called from [`SettingsReapply`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsReapply.java); the app template's `Picker.rebind` ([`ui/Picker.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Picker.java)), which its palette runs on a keymap change with the new opener, rows and legend ([`ui/MainWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MainWindow.java)).

rules.text: One picker serves every list choice: recent files, themes, keymaps, a setting's values, a branch to compare with.

check.text: those choices are instances of one generic picker class; there is no second list-picker class or `ChoiceDialog` for them.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/QuickOpen.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpen.java) (one generic class, instantiated more than seventy times), driven by [`PickerKeys`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/PickerKeys.java). Editora still asks with a `ChoiceDialog` in three places: the Git reset mode and the merge parent to revert against ([`ui/GitWindowCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/GitWindowCoordinator.java)), and the settings backup to restore ([`ui/SettingsResetFlow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsResetFlow.java)).

rules.text: In an app with a picker (a card, opened by a command, for choosing one thing from a list by typing; a Command Palette that lists only commands is not one, and nor is a menu, a combo box or a field's completion list), the picker is the palette's card in the shared in-scene overlay host, with a title naming the command over the field and a prompt in the field. That it is never a `javafx.stage.Popup` is [KBD-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/keyboard/#kbd-07).

check.text: each picker shows its card through the overlay host the palette uses and sets a title and a prompt text.

rules.appliesTo: an app with a picker: a card, opened by a command, for choosing one thing from a list by typing (a Command Palette that lists only commands is not one, and nor is a menu, a combo box or a field's completion list).
rules.text: A picker reads its items fresh on every showing and snapshots them, so typing filters a stable list. A source that answers late (an outline the language server has not returned yet) has the picker read its items again and keep the query (`reload()` in Editora).

check.text: showing a picker calls its items supplier, and a late source makes the picker read the items again while it keeps the query (Editora's `show` and `reload`).

rules.reference: Editora [`QuickOpen.show`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpen.java), [`QuickOpen.reload`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpen.java).

rules.appliesTo: an app with a picker: a card, opened by a command, for choosing one thing from a list by typing (a Command Palette that lists only commands is not one, and nor is a menu, a combo box or a field's completion list).
rules.text: With nothing typed, a picker's list keeps the supplier's own order (recency for recent files, document order for symbols), with the current value pre-selected when there is one.

check.text: a picker's empty query passes the items through unsorted and selects the value in force when the picker was given one (Editora's `setCurrentItem`).

rules.reference: Editora [`QuickOpen.filter`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpen.java), `setCurrentItem`; the app template's [`ui/Picker.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Picker.java) (`current`), whose theme, keymap and language pickers open on the choice in force ([`PickerFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/PickerFxTest.java), `helpTitleCurrentValueAndTheEnds`).

rules.appliesTo: an app with a picker: a card, opened by a command, for choosing one thing from a list by typing (a Command Palette that lists only commands is not one, and nor is a menu, a combo box or a field's completion list).
rules.text: Typing in a picker ranks its rows by fuzzy score, and ties keep the supplier's order, so rows do not shuffle under the cursor between keystrokes.

check.text: the last tiebreak of the picker's sort is the supplier's index.

rules.reference: Editora [`QuickOpen.filter`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpen.java).

rules.appliesTo: an app with a picker: a card, opened by a command, for choosing one thing from a list by typing (a Command Palette that lists only commands is not one, and nor is a menu, a combo box or a field's completion list).
rules.text: In a picker, the active keymap's line and page chords move the selection (in Editora, the chords of its `nav.lineDown`, `nav.lineUp`, `nav.pageDown` and `nav.pageUp` commands), as do ↑ ↓, Page Up/Down and `Ctrl+Home`/`Ctrl+End` (`Cmd` on macOS), which always work; plain Home and End stay with the field's caret. Enter or a click on a row chooses; the card hides first, then the choice runs, so focus is already back where it belongs.

check.text: the picker's key handler moves on the commands the active keymap binds for a line and a page up and down, and on the fixed keys whatever the keymap; the accept path hides the card before it calls the choice handler.

rules.reference: Editora [`QuickOpen`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpen.java) (`hide()` then `onChoose`), [`PickerKeys.resolve`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/PickerKeys.java), the only picker that asks the keymap. The app template's [`ui/Picker.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Picker.java) asks the keymap the same way, through its [`ui/PickerKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/PickerKeys.java) (`resolve`), and takes `Ctrl+Home` and `Ctrl+End` (`Cmd` on macOS); Mirada's picker is its palette, whose [`ui/PaletteKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/PaletteKeys.java) carries a fixed table of Emacs chords (`EMACS`) beside the fixed keys. Termina, Torrenta, Modula and nux have no picker ([Uses](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/quick-open/#uses)).

rules.appliesTo: an app with a picker: a card, opened by a command, for choosing one thing from a list by typing (a Command Palette that lists only commands is not one, and nor is a menu, a combo box or a field's completion list).
rules.text: The active keymap's cancel chord, Esc or a click on the scrim cancels a picker, and the overlay host restores focus. In Editora the chord is that of its `edit.cancel` command, `C-g` in the Emacs keymap. A picker that previewed something undoes it.

check.text: Esc, the chord the active keymap binds to the cancel command, and a press on the backdrop each hide the picker; hiding gives the focus back to the node that had it before the picker opened; and a picker that previewed a row runs its undo when it is dismissed without a choice. A test that asserts the undo is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`OverlayHost`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/OverlayHost.java) (`previousFocus`; it cancels on [`PickerKeys.isCancel`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/PickerKeys.java)), [`QuickOpenPreviewFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpenPreviewFxTest.java) (`dismissingRestoresWhatWasPreviewed`). The app template's [`ui/OverlayHost.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/OverlayHost.java) cancels its pickers on Esc, on the scrim and on the keymap's `edit.cancel` chord (`cancelOn`), and gives the focus back; none of its pickers previews anything. `Ctrl+G` is fixed in the `EMACS` table of Mirada's [`ui/PaletteKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/PaletteKeys.java).

rules.appliesTo: an app with a picker: a card, opened by a command, for choosing one thing from a list by typing (a Command Palette that lists only commands is not one, and nor is a menu, a combo box or a field's completion list).
rules.text: A picker previews the highlighted row as the selection moves and undoes the preview on cancel (Editora's Recent Locations shows each place and returns to the origin on Esc). A preview without an undo is worse than none, and nothing is previewed for the row the picker opens on, only for one the user moved to. Editora's theme and keymap pickers do not preview; they apply on Enter.

check.text: a previewing picker previews from its selection listener once it is showing, never for the row it opens on, restores what it previewed when dismissed, and does not restore after a choice. A test that asserts it is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`QuickOpen.setPreview(onPreview, onCancelled)`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpen.java), [`QuickOpenPreviewFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpenPreviewFxTest.java).

rules.appliesTo: an app with a picker: a card, opened by a command, for choosing one thing from a list by typing (a Command Palette that lists only commands is not one, and nor is a menu, a combo box or a field's completion list).
rules.text: A row action acts on the highlighted row and keeps the picker open (Editora's breakpoints picker enables or removes one), re-reading the list afterwards and keeping the cursor in place.

check.text: a row action's key runs the action on the highlighted row without hiding the card, and the picker then reads its items again and keeps the cursor on that row. A test that asserts it is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`QuickOpen.addRowAction(key, legend, action)`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpen.java), [`QuickOpenPreviewFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/QuickOpenPreviewFxTest.java) (`aRowActionActsOnTheHighlightedRowAndKeepsThePickerOpen`).

rules.appliesTo: an app with a picker: a card, opened by a command, for choosing one thing from a list by typing (a Command Palette that lists only commands is not one, and nor is a menu, a combo box or a field's completion list).
rules.text: A picker that can open on an empty list shows a placeholder sentence in it, never a blank card. A picker with nothing to offer may instead say so in the status line and not open.

check.text: each picker whose source can be empty either calls `setPlaceholder` or returns before `show` with a status message.

check.text: showing a card in the overlay host removes the previous card before it adds the new one, and keeps the original focus owner (Editora's `OverlayHost.show`).

rules.text: A picker's relatives, the other list overlays an app has (in Editora the open-files switcher, the find-file field, the multi-select picker, and the branch and stash popups), move, accept and cancel with the same keys as the picker.

check.text: each of those overlays moves, accepts and cancels on the keys the picker does: the moves of [QOPEN-06](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/quick-open/#qopen-06), Enter, and the cancel chord and Esc of [QOPEN-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/quick-open/#qopen-07). In Editora each maps its keys through the helper the picker uses (`PickerKeys`), which is one way to hold it.

rules.text: The Welcome page is shown at startup when there is no session to restore (so always with `--no-session`), by the `view.welcome` command (Help → Welcome Page where the app has a Help menu, in the place [DOCS-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/documentation/#docs-07) gives it), and when a switch to another project leaves the tab strip empty (Editora's project swap). check.text: those three paths open the one Welcome tab, and where the app has a Help menu, a row inside it runs `view.welcome`; a startup that goes straight to a view holds a flag that skips the page.
