rules.reference: Editora [`MainController.addWelcomeTab`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java); the app template's [`ui/DocumentTabs.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/DocumentTabs.java), whose Welcome tab's menu holds `buffer.close` alone, is not pinned, and leaves the title to the project and the app.

rules.text: Every app has an About window, reached by the `help.about` command, by Help → About where the app has a Help menu (the Help menu of a menu bar, or a Help submenu of the app's main menu, which [WIN-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-14) defines), and on macOS by the About item of the application menu, the one macOS names after the app. The app adds that item itself: JavaFX builds the menu with Hide and Quit and no About.
rules.why: on macOS that menu is where every app keeps About, so it is one of the places [the OS's way wins](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/same-on-every-os/#where-the-oss-way-wins).

check.text: `help.about` is registered and opens the About window; where the app has a Help menu, a row inside that menu runs the command (a row beside a Help submenu is not in it); and on macOS the app inserts an About item into the application menu that opens the same window.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/AboutDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/AboutDialog.java) and [`ui/MenuBarModel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MenuBarModel.java) (`help.about` ends the Help menu), and the app template's [`ui/Commands.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Commands.java) and [`ui/AppMenus.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AppMenus.java), do the Help row and the command, and the template's [`ui/MacAppMenu.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MacAppMenu.java) inserts the macOS item, which runs `help.about`, so the template meets the whole rule. Editora doesn't add the macOS item yet, and nor do Torrenta, Modula and nux. Termina ([`ui/MacAppMenu.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/MacAppMenu.java)) and Mirada ([`os/MacAppMenu.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/os/MacAppMenu.java)) add it too: JavaFX has no public API for that menu, so the three insert the item into the one Glass keeps (`MacApplication.getAppleMenu`). Neither of those two is the whole rule: Termina's command is `about`, not `help.about`, and Mirada's About row sits beside the Help submenu of its main menu, not in it ([`ui/TitleBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/TitleBar.java), `finish`).

rules.text: About shows the version and build, the runtime, the license, links to the app's home page, its source code and its releases, and the result of the last update check. The Pauta edition is [ABOUT-05](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/about/#about-05).

check.text: the About window shows the version and the build as the build recorded them (in Editora both come from `AppInfo`, which `--version` prints from too); the Java and JavaFX versions; the license; a link that opens the app's home page (its website, or its repository's page on the host where About links no website), one that opens its source code (the repository) and one that opens its releases (the repository's releases page or its latest release), each there whatever the update check answered; and the update checker's last answer whatever it was (an update, up to date, a failed check or not checked yet), not only an update that is available. One link meets two of the three when the page it opens is both: the repository's page is the home page and the source code where About links no website, and a releases page of the repository holds its source too (Editora's "Source code and releases"). A link to the running build's release notes, and a link shown only when an update is available, are not the link to the releases.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/AboutDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/AboutDialog.java), [`AppInfo`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/AppInfo.java) (`HOMEPAGE`, its website, and `RELEASES_PAGE`, the repository's latest release, behind "Source code and releases"); the page's [Spec](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/about/#spec). Four apps lack a link. Termina's About ([`ui/AboutWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/AboutWindow.java)) links its website and not its source code, and its releases only when an update is available. Mirada's ([`ui/AboutWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/AboutWindow.java)) links its repository and the running build's release notes, and its releases only when an update is available. Modula's About ([`ui/AboutWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/src/main/java/com/modula/ui/AboutWindow.java)) links its repository and never its releases; it also shows no Java version, and it shows the update check only when an update is available. nux's ([`ui/AboutWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/AboutWindow.java)) has the runtime lines and links its repository; it shows the update check, and with it the link to its releases, only when there is a newer version.

rules.text: About's *Copy details* button copies the environment block and leaves the window open; its label becomes "Copied".

check.text: the button's handler puts the environment block's text on the clipboard and sets the button's label to the copied text (Editora's `about.copied`); the button sits in the content, not the dialog's button bar, so pressing it can't close the window.

rules.reference: Editora [`AboutDialog`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/AboutDialog.java) (`about.copyDetails`, `about.copied`).

rules.text: About's update status claims nothing before a check has answered: with no answer, or with the check switched off, it says it has not checked, never "up to date".

check.text: About's update status falls back to the not-checked text when the checker has no result.

rules.reference: Editora [`AboutDialog`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/AboutDialog.java) (`about.notChecked`); the [Update status states](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/about/#update-status-states).

rules.text: In About, an available update stands out: "Update available" is bold in amber, a color no link or label in About uses, while the links stay in the accent, "up to date" is green, a failed check red and the last-checked line muted (Editora's tokens for the four are `-state-amber`, `-state-accent`, `-state-green` and `-state-red`).
rules.why: in the accent every link wears, the one line that asks for action reads as one more link.

check.text: the style of About's update-available line (the app template's `.about-update-available`) is bold in the amber token, and no other About style uses that token; the up-to-date line is in the green token, a failed check in the red and the last-checked line in the muted color, and the links keep the accent.

rules.reference: the [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s `.about-update-available` in [`styles/app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/resources/com/example/app/styles/app.css), set by [`ui/AboutDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AboutDialog.java). No released app does yet: Editora's `.about-update` in [`app.css`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/resources/com/editora/styles/app.css) is `-state-accent`, the links' color.

rules.text: About names the Pauta edition in two places: a link, *Built to Pauta x.y.z*, among its other links (at Partial it reads *Working toward Pauta x.y.z*, [ABOUT-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/about/#about-09)), and a line `Pauta: x.y.z` in the environment block, right after the commit, so *Copy details* carries it.

check.text: one of About's links reads *Built to Pauta* and the edition, or *Working toward Pauta* and the edition at Partial, in words from the catalog, and About's environment block writes a `Pauta:` line right after the commit line. The rule asks for the words, not for a catalog key: the app template's and Termina's key is `about.pauta`, Mirada's `about.pautaLink`.

rules.reference: The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`ui/AboutDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AboutDialog.java) and [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/AppInfo.java); Termina's [`ui/AboutWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/AboutWindow.java) and [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/AppInfo.java); Mirada's [`ui/AboutWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/AboutWindow.java) (`about.pautaLink`) and [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/AppInfo.java).

rules.text: About's edition link ([ABOUT-05](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/about/#about-05)) opens the edition's own address, `https://pauta-project.dev/<edition>/`, which never changes, not `latest/`, which moves on to newer editions.

check.text: the URL About's edition link opens is built from the edition number (`pauta.version`) and never contains `latest`. An About with no edition link has nothing to open: the rule fails with [ABOUT-05](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/about/#about-05), which requires the link, and the evidence names that rule.

rules.reference: The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/AppInfo.java) (`pautaUrl`); Termina's [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/AppInfo.java) (`pautaUrl`); Mirada's [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/AppInfo.java) (`pautaUrl`).

rules.text: The Pauta edition About names is the edition the app meets, not the newest. Moving to a newer edition means reading its changelog for new or stronger MUSTs, meeting them, then changing the number. An app at Partial names the edition it is working toward instead, and says so ([ABOUT-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/about/#about-09)).

check.text: read which words About uses for the edition ([ABOUT-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/about/#about-09)). *Working toward* meets the rule. An About that names no edition claims none: this rule has nothing to judge and passes, and the missing edition is [ABOUT-05](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/about/#about-05)'s finding. *Built to* is judged last, from the audit's other results: audited against the edition the app names (`pauta.version`), with that edition's own rules (`https://pauta-project.dev/<edition>/rules.json`), not the newest edition's, the app has no MUST that is `fail` or `pending`. The evidence names the MUSTs that are. An audit of part of the edition judges the rule from the MUSTs in its scope and says so. Only the rules of the edition the app names settle a *Built to*: an audit run against another edition reports the rule as `not-checked` and names the edition whose rules would settle it.

rules.reference: The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template), at Complete: its About says *Built to Pauta 6.0.0* ([`ui/AboutDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AboutDialog.java), `editionKey`) and so does its README, and its audit against 6.0.0's own rules finds no MUST that is `fail` or `pending` ([`docs/pauta-audit.md`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/docs/pauta-audit.md)). Termina and Mirada don't meet it yet. Termina's About says "Built to Pauta 2.0.2" ([`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/pom.xml), `pauta.version`), an edition that already required a find bar in its Debug Log, the UI font on every scene and the command ids `help.about` and `palette.show`, none of which it has. Mirada's says "Built to Pauta 4.0.1", an edition that already required its settings in `~/.mirada` on every OS.

rules.text: The Pauta edition an app names has one source: a `pauta.version` property in `pom.xml`, which the build filters into the app's resources and the app reads from there, like its own version (`build-info.properties` and `AppInfo` in the app template). The README's badge and "Built to" line, which name that edition too, are [PAUTA-15](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#pauta-15).

check.text: `pom.xml` defines `pauta.version`; a resource the build filters carries it (the app template's `build-info.properties`); and the edition the app shows is read from that resource (the template's `AppInfo`), never from a literal in its code.

rules.reference: The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/pom.xml), `build-info.properties` and [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/AppInfo.java); Termina's the same, with [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/AppInfo.java), and Mirada's, with its [`pom.xml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/pom.xml) and [`AppInfo.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/AppInfo.java).

rules.text: About shows the app's conformance, Complete, Core or Partial, as the conformance helper computes it from `pauta.json` ([PAUTA-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#pauta-02)) and never higher: a link, *Pauta conformance: Core*, right after the edition's link, that runs the `help.pauta` command and so opens the Pauta window ([PWIN-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/pauta-window/#pwin-01)), and a line `Pauta conformance: Core (2 exceptions)` in the environment block, right after the `Pauta:` line; with one it says `(1 exception)`, with none `(no exceptions)`. At Partial the edition's link reads *Working toward Pauta x.y.z*: the app does not meet that edition yet, so it does not say it is built to it.
rules.why: [*Never claim what is not true*](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/principles/#for-the-people-using-the-apps).

check.text: About calls the conformance helper and holds no conformance name of its own; its conformance link runs `help.pauta`; the environment block has the conformance line after the `Pauta:` line; and at Partial the edition's link reads *Working toward Pauta* and the edition (the app template's key for it is `about.pautaWorkingToward`).

rules.reference: The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`ui/AboutDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AboutDialog.java) and [`PautaConformance.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/PautaConformance.java) (`environmentLine`). Termina's and Mirada's About show the edition but not the conformance.

rules.text: Every app has a Pauta window, opened by the `help.pauta` command: from the Command Palette like every command, and from a *Pauta Conformance* row in the Help menu where the app has a Help menu (the Help menu of a menu bar, or a Help submenu of the app's main menu, which [WIN-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-14) defines). The row's place in that menu is [DOCS-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/documentation/#docs-07), and About's *Pauta conformance* link, which runs the same command, is [ABOUT-09](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/about/#about-09).

check.text: a command with the id `help.pauta` is registered and opens the Pauta window, and where the app has a Help menu, a row inside that menu runs the command (the app template's Help menu is a list of command ids that holds `help.pauta`). A row beside a Help submenu is not in it.

rules.reference: The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`ui/Commands.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Commands.java) (`help.pauta`, which runs `openPauta`) and [`ui/AppMenus.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AppMenus.java) (`help.pauta` in `menu.help`, just above `help.about`). No released app has a Pauta window yet.

rules.text: The Pauta window shows the edition, the conformance with one sentence that says what it means, a count of exceptions by kind, and every exception: the rule's ID, its level (MUST or SHOULD), the kind, the reason, and for a deviation or a pending exception its link.

check.text: open the Pauta window and compare it with the app's `pauta.json`, entry by entry.

rules.reference: The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`ui/PautaWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/PautaWindow.java).

rules.text: The Pauta window reads the exceptions from `pauta.json` and the edition from the build, as About does ([ABOUT-08](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/about/#about-08); `AppInfo` in the template), and takes the conformance from the same helper as About ([PAUTA-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/conformance/#pauta-02)). No edition, conformance or exception is written in the window's own code.

check.text: the Pauta window loads the exceptions through the one loader of `pauta.json`, reads the edition where About reads it, and calls the conformance helper; its code holds no rule ID, edition number or conformance name of its own.

rules.reference: The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`ui/PautaWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/PautaWindow.java) (`PautaConformance.of`).

rules.text: Every link in the Pauta window opens a fixed address, never one under `latest/`: the edition's link opens the edition's own address, the one [ABOUT-06](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/about/#about-06) gives About's link, and each rule ID opens the rule's address in that edition (the entry's `url` in `pauta.json`). The edition's link, in the Pauta window and in About, runs the `help.pautaRules` command, so the palette reaches it too.
rules.why: an app built to an edition answers to that edition's rules; `latest/` moves on.

check.text: `help.pautaRules` is registered and opens the edition's address, built from `pauta.version`; the edition's link in the Pauta window and the one in About both run that command; and each rule ID in the Pauta window opens its entry's `url`.

rules.reference: The [app template](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template)'s [`ui/Commands.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Commands.java) (`help.pautaRules`, which opens `AppInfo.pautaUrl()`), run by the edition's link in [`ui/PautaWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/PautaWindow.java) and [`ui/AboutDialog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/AboutDialog.java); `PautaWindow` opens each rule ID at its entry's `url`.

rules.text: The Pauta window lists pending exceptions first, then deviations, then app-only (in a template), then not-applicable; within a kind, MUSTs before SHOULDs, then by ID.
rules.why: what the app still owes is what a reader came to find.

check.text: the list the Pauta window draws is sorted by kind in that order, then MUSTs before SHOULDs, then by rule ID (the app template's `PautaConformance.sorted`). A test that asserts it is the surest evidence.

rules.text: In an app that asks before a destructive action (before it removes, deletes, discards or overwrites something, ends a running program, or runs a command that cannot be taken back), the question names the thing and what happens to it. A question that warns before something is run or pasted and destroys nothing (Termina's before a multi-line paste), and a question before a harmless command (nux's before a UPS command it does not count as risky), are not questions before a destructive action. This list says which questions the rules on a question's form cover; it is wider than what [CONF-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-01) requires a question or an undo for, which is only what the user made.

check.text: the string of every question before a destructive action names the thing, by an argument for its name or count or in its own words ("Quit Editora?"), and says what happens to it.

rules.text: Every dialog with two or more buttons words each button from the message catalog, never with JavaFX's stock OK, Yes, No, Cancel, Apply or Close, which are worded in the JVM's locale. That is every JavaFX `Dialog` the app shows, whatever it is for: a question, before a destructive action ([CONF-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-02)) or not, a text prompt, a pick from a list, a form. Only a message with one button is outside the rule. Like [CONF-08](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-08) and [CONF-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-12), it reaches past the question before a destructive action.
rules.why: a stock button is labeled from JavaFX's own resources, in the JVM's locale, so under menus in the language chosen in Settings a dialog can still say "Cancel" in another.

check.text: in every `Dialog` the app shows with two or more buttons (an `Alert` of any type, a `TextInputDialog`, a `ChoiceDialog`, a `Dialog` the app fills itself), each button shows a string from the message catalog: its `ButtonType` is built with one, or its button's text is set from the catalog before the dialog is shown. None is left as `ButtonType.OK`, `ButtonType.YES`, `ButtonType.NO`, `ButtonType.CANCEL`, `ButtonType.APPLY` or `ButtonType.CLOSE`, and none is the stock OK or Cancel that an `Alert` of type `CONFIRMATION`, a `TextInputDialog` and a `ChoiceDialog` come with. A dialog whose stock buttons are swapped for catalog-worded ones before it is shown passes (Torrenta's `StockButtons.translate`). A dialog with one button is not judged. An app that shows no dialog with two or more buttons has nothing to judge, and passes.

rules.text: In an app that asks before a destructive action, Cancel is the way out of the question: Escape and the window's close button both answer Cancel, and nothing is lost on a dismissal.

check.text: in every question before a destructive action ([CONF-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-02) says which those are), Cancel has the `CANCEL_CLOSE` role, and the result defaults to Cancel when the dialog closes any other way (`showAndWait().orElse(cancel)`).

rules.reference: Editora [`GitCoordinator.confirmDestructive`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/GitCoordinator.java), [`CloseCoordinator.unsavedAlert`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/CloseCoordinator.java); Torrenta [`RemoveConfirm.ask`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/RemoveConfirm.java).

rules.text: In an app that asks before a destructive action, every such question has one default button, and it is never the red one (Editora's `danger` style class): Cancel where the only action is destructive, Save where saving is an option ([CONF-05](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-05)). The dialog opens with keyboard focus on the default button, so Enter in a question that has just opened keeps what the user has, on every OS, and the red action runs only from its own button: a click, or the focus moved to it with Tab and then Space, which presses the focused button on every OS.
rules.why: Enter is the key a hurried hand presses, and Escape already cancels ([CONF-04](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-04)): with Cancel as the default, no single key destroys anything. JavaFX makes a button with the `OK_DONE` role the default by itself, so a named action is the default unless the dialog says otherwise. It also presses a focused button on Enter on Windows and Linux but not on macOS, so a question with no default button answers Enter differently on each OS. With Cancel as the default one difference is left, and it is JavaFX's: once Tab has put the focus on the red button, Enter runs it on Windows and Linux and answers Cancel on macOS. Space is the key that does the same everywhere.

check.text: in every question before a destructive action ([CONF-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/confirm-dialog/#conf-02) says which those are), the code calls `setDefaultButton(true)` on Cancel, or on Save in the unsaved-changes question, and `setDefaultButton(false)` on the destructive action, so that one is not left a default button too, and it does both before the dialog is shown. JavaFX gives the opening focus to the first button that is a default button, so with one default button the dialog opens with the focus on it. No such question leaves the red action, or no button at all, as the default.

rules.reference: Termina [`ui/Confirm.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/Confirm.java) (`Options.cancelIsDefault`, which its close-running-program question sets), the app template's [`ui/Confirm.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Confirm.java) (`dialog`, which every destructive question of the template asks through) and nux [`ui/CommandConfirmation.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/src/main/java/com/nux/ui/CommandConfirmation.java) (a risky UPS command): each unsets the action's default and sets Cancel's as it builds the dialog, before it is shown. Editora does it in about twenty of its questions, each by hand: deleting for good what the trash cannot take ([`ProjectPanel.cancelByDefault`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ProjectPanel.java)), closing a terminal with a program running ([`ui/TerminalCoordinator.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TerminalCoordinator.java)), resetting settings ([`ui/SettingsResetFlow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/SettingsResetFlow.java)), trusting a folder ([`ui/TrustPrompts.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TrustPrompts.java)) among them. A Save that fails leaves the tab open.

rules.why: every app has a Debug Log ([DIAG-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/diagnostics/#diag-03)), and a log is read by searching it.

rules.text: A list is narrowed by a filter box where text is searched by a find bar. In an app whose main content is a list, a filter box over that list takes the place of a find bar there, with the same field and the same Escape. The main content is a list when it is a list or a table of items that grows without bound and that the user finds things in; Torrenta, with its torrents, is the one such app today. In every app, a log shown as a list of entries (a Message Log, an event log, a Debug Log drawn as a list or a table) is covered the same way: a filter field over the list narrows it, and it needs no find bar. An event log and a log tab that lists one item's events count as logs shown as a list (nux's event log, the Log tab of Torrenta's detail pane); a table of readings or of history does not.

check.text: in an app whose main content is a list (a list or a table of items that grows without bound and that the user finds things in), a filter field sits over that list and filters it as it is typed, and Escape pressed in it leads back to the list, as it leads back to the text from a find bar ([FIND-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/find-bar/#find-07)). Whether the first Escape empties the box before the next one leaves it is [FIND-14](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/find-bar/#find-14)'s. In every app, each log shown as a list or a table of entries has a filter field over it that narrows the entries as it is typed; check boxes that narrow a log by level are not one. An event log and a tab that lists one item's events are such logs; a table of readings or of history is not judged.

rules.text: A command opens each find bar, and run while its bar is already open it finds the next match. For the main window's own text (the editor; the terminal in a terminal app) the command is `find.show`, bound to `C-s` in the Emacs keymap and `Ctrl/Cmd+F` in CUA, Sublime, VS Code and IntelliJ, with `F3` as well in CUA and Sublime (`Cmd+G` in place of `F3` in CUA on macOS); a terminal binds it to `Ctrl+Shift+F`, `Cmd+F` on macOS, since a plain `Ctrl+letter` belongs to the shell. Any other bar (over a log window, or over a console or a terminal panel beside the editor) has a command with an id of its own, as the app template's `debugLog.find` is for its Debug Log.

check.text: each bundled keymap binds that chord to `find.show`; every other find bar is opened by a registered command of its own; and each of these commands, run while its bar is shown, steps to the next match.

rules.reference: Editora `keymaps/*.json` and [`MainController.findShowOrNext`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MainController.java), which finds the next match while the editor's bar is open. The app template's bars all do: `find.show`, bound in each of its keymaps, over the documents, `output.find` over the Output console and `debugLog.find` over the Debug Log each open their bar and, run while it is open, step to the next match (`openOrNext` in its [`ui/FindBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/FindBar.java); [`ui/Commands.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/Commands.java); [`FindBarFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/FindBarFxTest.java)). No other app's bar does both yet. Termina's find command ([`TerminalWindow`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalWindow.java), `menu.find`, [`MenuAction.appChord`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/MenuAction.java)) runs [`TerminalView.showSearch`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalView.java), which puts the caret back in the field of a bar that is already open. So does Editora's `terminal.find` over its terminal panel ([`TerminalCoordinator.find`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TerminalCoordinator.java)). The template's Debug Log window also runs `debugLog.find` ([`MainWindow.findInDebugLog`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MainWindow.java)) on a fixed `Ctrl/Cmd+F`. Editora's console bar has no command: the find command's chord pressed in the console opens it (`ConsoleNav.onCommand` in [`ui/BuildToolPanel.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/BuildToolPanel.java)), as does a button in the panel's header.

rules.text: Typing in a find bar highlights every match, the active one distinctly, and selects and scrolls to the match the search starts on. In a document (an editor, a console, a log) that is the first match at or after the caret as it was when the bar opened, so refining the query does not run away down the document. In a terminal it is the newest match at or above the bottom of the view, since a terminal is searched upward ([FIND-06](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/find-bar/#find-06)). A view that can draw one selection and nothing else, such as a log in a plain text area, shows the active match alone, and the count ([FIND-02](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/find-bar/#find-02)) says how many there are.

check.text: every match in view is painted while the bar is open, not only the active one, unless the view can draw a single selection only. In a document the search starts from an anchor saved when the bar opens, not from the current selection; in a terminal, from the bottom row of the view.

rules.reference: Editora [`FindReplaceBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/FindReplaceBar.java) (`searchAnchor`, `recompute`) over the editor. Over a terminal, Editora's [`terminal/TerminalView.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/terminal/TerminalView.java) (`startIndex`, `drawSearch`) and Termina's [`TerminalView`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalView.java) (`drawSearchMatches`) with [`ScrollbackSearch.initial`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/ScrollbackSearch.java). The app template's [`ui/FindBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/FindBar.java) saves the caret as its `anchor` when the bar opens and `refine` searches from it ([`FindBarFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/FindBarFxTest.java), `theSearchStartsAtTheCaretAndTheFieldKeepsItsEditingKeys`). Editora's [`ConsoleFindBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ConsoleFindBar.java) doesn't yet: it searches from the current selection (`refine`), not from an anchor saved when the bar opened. Editora's console is a `CodeArea`, which could paint every match, and its bar paints the active one only. The template's documents, Output and Debug Log are each a `TextArea`, which draws one selection and nothing else, so its bar rightly shows the active match alone.

rules.text: In a find bar, Enter steps to the next match and Shift+Enter to the previous one, wrapping around at the ends. In a find bar over a terminal the directions are up and down the scrollback: Enter steps up to older output, Shift+Enter down.

check.text: in each find bar the app has, the query field's key handler steps to the next match on Enter and to the previous one on Shift+Enter (over a terminal, up to older output on Enter and down on Shift+Enter), and a step past the last match goes on to the first, and back. A view where [FIND-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/find-bar/#find-01) asks for a find bar and the app has none fails this rule with FIND-01, and so does an app with no find bar and no Debug Log window at all; the evidence names that rule.

rules.reference: Editora [`ConsoleFindBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ConsoleFindBar.java), [`TerminalFindBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TerminalFindBar.java); Termina [`SearchBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/SearchBar.java). Editora's editor bar ([`FindReplaceBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/FindReplaceBar.java)) does not yet: its field steps forward on Enter, and back only with the previous button, `find.showBackward` (`C-r`, `Shift+F3`) or `find.previous`. Alt+Enter there turns every match into a caret. The app template's [`ui/FindBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/FindBar.java) steps and wraps the same way (`step`), in each of its three bars.

rules.text: Escape or the close button closes a find bar: its highlights go, a search still pending is canceled so nothing moves after the bar is gone, and focus returns to the text the bar searched (the editor, the console, the shell or the log). In a find bar over a terminal, the Escape that closes the bar does not reach the shell.

check.text: in each find bar the app has, the close path, run by Escape in the field and by the close button, stops the debounces, cancels the running search, clears the highlights and focuses the text the bar searched. In a find bar over a terminal, the field's key handler consumes the Escape it closes the bar on, so the terminal never sends that key to the shell. A view where [FIND-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/find-bar/#find-01) asks for a find bar and the app has none fails this rule with FIND-01, and so does an app with no find bar and no Debug Log window at all; the evidence names that rule.

rules.reference: Editora [`FindReplaceBar.hideBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/FindReplaceBar.java); the app template's [`ui/FindBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/FindBar.java) (`close`), in each of its three bars. Over a terminal, Termina's [`SearchBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/SearchBar.java) (`onKey`) and Editora's [`TerminalFindBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TerminalFindBar.java) each close the bar on Escape and consume the key.

rules.text: A terminal with a find bar keeps its own key and mouse filters off the bar: they leave every event aimed at the bar alone, so what is typed or clicked there never reaches the shell. The Escape that closes the bar is [FIND-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/find-bar/#find-07)'s.

check.text: no key or mouse filter of the terminal acts on an event aimed at the find bar: the filters return early for an event whose target is inside the bar (Termina's `fromSearchBar`), or the bar is outside the node the filters are on, so its events never pass them.

rules.reference: Termina [`TerminalView.fromSearchBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TerminalView.java), which its key, mouse and scroll handlers ask first.

rules.text: In a find bar's fields, the keymap's caret and editing chords (`C-a`, `C-e`, `C-k`, `C-y` in the Emacs keymap; `Ctrl+V/X/C/Z` in CUA, `Cmd+V/X/C/Z` on macOS) act on the field, not on the document. Find's own chords stay global, so next, previous, replace and close work while the field has focus.

check.text: in each find bar's fields, the active keymap's caret and editing chords are handled by the field and never run the document's commands (Editora installs its shared text-input keymap on the fields), and the commands for next, previous, replace and close still run while a find field has the focus.

rules.reference: Editora [`TextInputKeymap.installShared`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/command/TextInputKeymap.java), installed on [`FindReplaceBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/FindReplaceBar.java)'s find and replace fields. Editora's [`ConsoleFindBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ConsoleFindBar.java) and [`TerminalFindBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TerminalFindBar.java) don't yet: neither installs it on its field. Nor does Termina's find field: its [`TextInputKeys`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/TextInputKeys.java) is installed on the palette only. The app template's [`ui/TextInputKeys.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/TextInputKeys.java) (`install`) is on the field of each of its find bars, and its key dispatcher leaves a text field's editing chords to the field ([`TextInputKeysTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/TextInputKeysTest.java); [`FindBarFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/test/java/com/example/app/ui/FindBarFxTest.java), `theSearchStartsAtTheCaretAndTheFieldKeepsItsEditingKeys`).

rules.text: Nothing found is one status-line message ("Not found: x") or the count "No matches". No beep, no dialog.

check.text: the no-match path sets `find.notFound` or `search.none` and opens nothing.

rules.reference: Editora [`FindReplaceBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/FindReplaceBar.java) (`find.notFound`); Termina [`SearchBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/SearchBar.java) (`search.none`).

rules.text: In a find bar that replaces (an editor's), Replace keeps each match's case when *AB* (preserve case) is on.

check.text: with preserve case on, the replace path gives each replacement the casing of the match it replaces (Editora's `PreserveCase.apply`). A test that asserts it is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora [`FindReplaceBarFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/FindReplaceBarFxTest.java) (`preserveCaseFollowsEachMatchesCasing`).

rules.text: In a find bar that replaces, Replace and Replace All run under a time budget, as the search does: a replacement that outruns it stops and says so in the status line (in Editora's words, "Replace stopped: the pattern is too slow") instead of hanging the window. How long the budget is is the app's own.

check.text: Replace and Replace All match under a time budget, as the search does, and when it runs out they stop and say so in the status line (Editora's `find.replaceTimeout`) instead of hanging the window. A test that asserts it, with a catastrophic regular expression in Replace All, is the surest evidence.

rules.reference: Editora `find.replaceTimeout`, [`FindReplaceBarFxTest`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/test/java/com/editora/ui/FindReplaceBarFxTest.java) (`catastrophicRegexInReplaceAllAbortsInsteadOfHanging`).

rules.text: In an app whose main content is a list ([FIND-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/find-bar/#find-03) says which apps those are), the filter box filters the names as plain words are typed, turns `key:value` terms into chips and runs a command after `>`. A command puts the focus in the box (`filter` in Torrenta), bound to `Ctrl+K`, `Cmd+K` on macOS, and the box draws that command's chord as a key badge.

check.text: the box's text listener filters the names by the plain words, turns a `key:value` term into a chip and runs the command typed after `>`; a registered command focuses the box, on `Ctrl+K` (`Cmd+K` on macOS); and the badge in the box is read from that command's chord, not written out.

rules.reference: Torrenta [`Omnibox`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/Omnibox.java), [`MainWindow.buildFilterBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java).

rules.text: In an app whose main content is a list ([FIND-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/find-bar/#find-03) says which apps those are), Escape in the filter box peels one layer: a box with something in it empties, an empty one gives the list back.

check.text: the box's Escape handler clears a non-empty box and otherwise focuses the list.

rules.reference: Torrenta [`MainWindow.onOmniboxKey`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java).

rules.text: In an app whose main content is a list ([FIND-03](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/find-bar/#find-03) says which apps those are), the filter box is out of the Tab order, so a fresh launch does not land every keystroke in it, and the window's own chords (in Torrenta, undo and the saved views' `Ctrl+Alt+1…9`, `Cmd+Alt+1…9` on macOS) do not fire while a text field has focus: `Ctrl+Z` (`Cmd+Z` on macOS) there is the field's own undo.

check.text: the box is not focus-traversable, and the window's chord handlers return early when the focus owner is a `TextInputControl`.

rules.reference: Torrenta [`MainWindow.buildFilterBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java), [`MainWindow`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java) window chords.

rules.text: A control of a find bar or of a filter box leaves the Tab order only when the keyboard does what it does another way: a registered command does the same, or the bar's own field handles a key that does. So the Next, Previous and Close buttons may leave it, since Enter, Shift+Enter and Escape in the field do the same ([FIND-06](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/find-bar/#find-06), [FIND-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/find-bar/#find-07)), and so may a field's clear button, since the field's editing keys empty it. An option's toggle (match case, whole word, regular expression) stays in it unless a command toggles that option. A list app's filter box leaves it ([FIND-15](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/find-bar/#find-15)) because its command puts the focus there ([FIND-13](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/find-bar/#find-13)). A terminal's bar is no exception: Tab belongs to the shell only while the terminal has the focus, so a toggle taken out of the Tab order there needs a command like any other.
rules.why: [KBD-15](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/keyboard/#kbd-15) lets a control out of the Tab order only when the keyboard does its work another way. A toggle that is out of it with no command can be changed with the mouse alone.

check.text: for every control of a find bar or filter box that is set not focus-traversable, a registered command does what the control does, or the bar's field handles a key that does: Enter, Shift+Enter or Escape for Next, Previous and Close, the editing keys for a clear button. A toggle that is not focus-traversable has a command that toggles its option. An app with no find bar and no filter box has no such control: nothing breaks this rule and it passes, the missing bar being [FIND-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/find-bar/#find-01)'s finding.

rules.reference: Editora's [`FindReplaceBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/FindReplaceBar.java) keeps every button and option box in the Tab order, all but the clear button inside each field. Its [`ConsoleFindBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/ConsoleFindBar.java) and [`TerminalFindBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/TerminalFindBar.java) take Previous, Next and Close out of it, which Shift+Enter, Enter and Escape in the field do, and leave the field and the match-case toggle in. The app template's [`FindBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/FindBar.java) takes the same three out: Previous and Next run its bar's step commands (`find.previous` and `find.next` over a document, `output.findPrevious` and `output.findNext`, `debugLog.findPrevious` and `debugLog.findNext`), Close is the field's Escape, and the Match Case box stays in. Torrenta's filter box is out of it and reached by its `filter` command ([`MainWindow.buildFilterBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MainWindow.java)). In Mirada's [`BookmarksWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/BookmarksWindow.java) the three kind toggles are out of it and have a command each (`bookmarks.listAll`, `bookmarks.listBookmarked`, `bookmarks.listNotes`). Termina's [`SearchBar.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/SearchBar.java) leaves only its field in the Tab order: the two arrows and Close are the field's Enter, Shift+Enter and Escape, and the arrows its `findNext` and `findPrevious` commands too, but its regex toggle doesn't meet the rule yet: it is out of the Tab order and no command toggles it.

rules.text: The Message Log is a card in the window's in-scene overlay host, anchored just above the status bar's echo area, never a separate window: 773 px wide, its list 336 px high, at the default zoom, holding the newest 200 messages of the session (the cap [DIAG-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/diagnostics/#diag-01) asks for).
rules.why: the log answers "what just happened?" next to the line that said it; a separate window, or another size and cap, makes the same log look and behave differently from app to app.

check.text: the log adds its node to the overlay host (no `Stage`), with width 773, list height 336 and a cap of 200.

rules.reference: Editora [`ui/MessageLogPopup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLogPopup.java) (`WIDTH`, `LIST_HEIGHT`) and [`ui/MessageLog.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLog.java) (`MAX_ENTRIES`); the app template's [`ui/MessageLogView.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MessageLogView.java). Torrenta's card is 640 × 300, and Termina's log is a separate window that keeps 500 messages.

rules.text: A click on the status bar's unread-error count opens the Message Log, as a click on the echo area does ([WIN-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/window-shell/#win-01)), and so does the `view.messageLog` command.

check.text: the unread-error count runs `view.messageLog` on a click, and the command is registered.

rules.reference: Editora [`StatusBar`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/StatusBar.java) (`echo`, `unreadErrors`), [`StatusBar.showMessageLog`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/StatusBar.java).

rules.text: The active keymap's cancel chord or a click outside closes the Message Log, as Esc does.

check.text: the Message Log closes on the chord the active keymap binds to its cancel command, not on a fixed `Ctrl+G`, and a press outside the log closes it: on the backdrop, where the log is the in-scene card [MLOG-08](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/templates/message-log/#mlog-08) asks for. In an app with one key table (a terminal app's keymap, or the built-in table of an app that ships no keymap files), the chord is the one that table binds to a cancel command; where it binds none, Esc and the press outside are all there is to test.

rules.reference: Editora [`OverlayHost`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/OverlayHost.java), which hides the card on a press on its backdrop and on [`PickerKeys.isCancel`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/PickerKeys.java): Esc, or the chord the keymap binds to `edit.cancel` (Editora's id; `C-g` in its Emacs keymap). Its [`MessageLogPopup`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLogPopup.java) also closes on `Ctrl+G` whatever the keymap, though the CUA keymap binds `C-g` to `nav.goToLine`; its handler reads `Alt+G` too, which the Emacs keymap's `M-g` prefix takes first. The app template's Message Log ([`ui/MessageLogView.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MessageLogView.java)) is shown through its [`ui/OverlayHost.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/OverlayHost.java), which closes it the same way, on the keymap's `edit.cancel` chord (`cancelOn`). Elsewhere the chord is fixed: `Ctrl+G` in Termina ([`ui/MessageLogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/MessageLogWindow.java)) and Mirada ([`ui/MessageLogView.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/MessageLogView.java)). Torrenta's ([`ui/MessageLogPopup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MessageLogPopup.java)) closes on Esc and on a press on its backdrop: Torrenta has no keymap and no cancel command, so the chord asks nothing more of it.

rules.text: The Message Log copies the selected entries on the platform's copy chord, `Ctrl+C` (`Cmd+C` on macOS), in every keymap, and on the active keymap's copy chord too.

check.text: the Message Log's key handling copies the selected entries on C with the platform's shortcut modifier down (`isShortcutDown`), whatever the active keymap binds to copy, and also on the chord the active keymap binds to its copy command (`M-w` in an Emacs keymap), read from the keymap and not written into the handler.

rules.reference: for the platform's chord, Editora [`MessageLogPopup.copySelection`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/ui/MessageLogPopup.java), on a fixed shortcut-down C, and the Message Logs of Torrenta ([`ui/MessageLogPopup.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/src/main/java/com/torrenta/ui/MessageLogPopup.java)), Termina ([`ui/MessageLogWindow.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/src/main/java/com/termina/ui/MessageLogWindow.java)), Mirada ([`ui/MessageLogView.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/src/main/java/com/mirada/ui/MessageLogView.java)) and the app template ([`ui/MessageLogView.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/src/main/java/com/example/app/ui/MessageLogView.java)), each the same way. For the keymap's chord, no app yet: none of the five reads the keymap's copy binding in its log, and Editora's Emacs keymap binds copy to `M-w`, which its log does not read. The app template meets the rule all the same: none of its keymaps binds a copy command, so there is no second chord to read, and its key dispatcher steps aside while the log, an overlay, is open (`KeyDispatcher`), so `Ctrl+C` reaches it under the Emacs keymap's `C-c` prefix too. Editora doesn't hold the first half under that keymap on Windows and Linux either: the keymap starts longer chords with `C-c`, a prefix the window's key dispatcher ([`command/KeyDispatcher.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/src/main/java/com/editora/command/KeyDispatcher.java)) consumes in a scene filter, ahead of the log's own.

rules.text: A message's severity comes from its key: a `status.*` key whose last segment contains `fail` or `error` is an error, one containing `cannot` or `invalid` a warning. Name new keys accordingly, or post the message as an error directly (Editora's status bar has an error channel for that).

check.text: one function gives a message's severity from its key by those rules (Editora's `StatusSeverity.ofKey`). A test that asserts it is the surest evidence.

rules.text: Opening the Message Log, or clearing it, resets the unread-error count.

check.text: opening the Message Log marks it read, and clearing it zeroes the count (Editora's `markRead` and `clear`).

rules.text: The CI workflow (`ci.yml` in Editora) runs on every push to the default branch and every pull request, with two checks: the format check of [PLAT-10](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/platform/#plat-10) (`spotless:check`; the job Editora names **Format**) and the build with its tests (`./mvnw verify`, coverage gate included; Editora's **Build & Test**), on the JDK [PLAT-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/platform/#plat-01) names.
