One of its jobs is the Format job of [PLAT-10](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/platform/#plat-10), which runs `spotless:check` and neither builds nor tests, and its jobs between them run the whole suite and `verify` with the coverage gate: one job that runs `./mvnw verify`, or, as in Editora, jobs that run `test` in shards and one that runs `verify` over their results. What the jobs are called is the app's own. A workflow that lacks a trigger or one of the two checks fails the rule. That the default branch requires both is a repository setting, which no file shows. An audit run from the app's checkout alone reports the rule as `not-checked` and says what would settle it.

rules.reference: Editora [`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/ci.yml), on `master` (its `format` job, its four `tests` shards and its `build` job, which runs `verify` over the shards' results); the app template's [`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/.github/workflows/ci.yml) and Termina's [`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/.github/workflows/ci.yml), on `master`, and Mirada's [`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/.github/workflows/ci.yml), on `main`, each with a job for `spotless:check` and one for `verify`. Torrenta ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/.github/workflows/ci.yml)), Modula ([`build.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/.github/workflows/build.yml)) and nux ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/.github/workflows/ci.yml)) don't yet: none has a format check of its own. Torrenta's and Modula's one test job runs `./mvnw verify`, which their poms bind `spotless:check` to, so a single status stands for both checks; nux's pom has no Spotless, and its job runs `./mvnw test`, not `verify`. Modula's and nux's builds have no coverage gate either ([PLAT-12](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/platform/#plat-12)). No file of any of them shows the required checks.

rules.text: The tests run on all three OSes: the pure suite (no JavaFX toolkit) on Linux, macOS and Windows, and the FX suite on Linux and at least one more. They run there every day or on every pull request. How the runs are split is the app's own: one workflow that runs everything on every pull request meets this, and so does a quick workflow for pull requests with a fuller one on a schedule. A release waits for these runs on its own commit, on all three OSes: that it waits at all is [REL-30](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/release/#rel-30).
rules.why: path separators, line endings, case-insensitive file systems and process spawning fail on one OS only, and the pure suite is where they show; the FX suite catches layout and focus differences. The FX suite is the slow one (three shards on macOS in Editora), so it is asked on two OSes and not three: the third is covered by the pure suite alone.

check.text: taken together, the workflows' test jobs run the pure suite on `ubuntu-*`, `macos-*` and `windows-*` runners and the FX suite on `ubuntu-*` and one more, under a `schedule` or a `pull_request` trigger that needs no label; and the tests a release waits for ([REL-30](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/release/#rel-30)) ran on those runners, in the release workflow itself or in the run it reads.

rules.reference: Editora splits them: [`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/ci.yml) runs the whole suite on Linux on every pull request, and [`full-tests.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/full-tests.yml) the pure suite on Windows and macOS and the FX suite on macOS, in three shards, daily, on a pull request labeled `full-ci` and before every release: the "Check that the Full tests passed on this commit" step in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/release.yml). It lists flaky tests in the job summary ([`scripts/ci/ReportFlakes.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/scripts/ci/ReportFlakes.java)). The app template splits them the same way, and its release calls [`full-tests.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/.github/workflows/full-tests.yml) itself. Termina ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/.github/workflows/ci.yml)), Torrenta ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/.github/workflows/ci.yml)), Mirada ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/.github/workflows/ci.yml)), Modula ([`build.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/.github/workflows/build.yml)) and nux ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/.github/workflows/ci.yml)) run the whole suite on the three OSes on every pull request.

rules.text: The release workflow (`release.yml` in Editora) runs on a version tag (`v*` meets it; the version-shaped `v[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+*` is the better pattern, since a tag like `vendor-import` doesn't match it), with `workflow_dispatch` as a dry run that builds and signs and publishes nothing. The tag matching the pom is [REL-05](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/release/#rel-05), the tests it waits for [REL-30](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/release/#rel-30), the release-asset check [REL-07](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/release/#rel-07), and the bump to the next snapshot [REL-06](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/release/#rel-06).

check.text: the release workflow triggers on a tag pattern that starts with `v` and on `workflow_dispatch`. A dispatched run goes through the build and signing jobs and publishes nothing: the step that publishes runs in a mode that publishes nothing (JReleaser's `--dry-run`), or the job that publishes runs only for a tag (an `if:` on the ref).

rules.reference: Editora [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/release.yml), whose "JReleaser" step takes `release --dry-run` on a dispatch; the template, Termina, Torrenta and Mirada pass JReleaser `--dry-run` the same way. Modula's [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/.github/workflows/release.yml) and nux's [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/.github/workflows/release.yml), which have no JReleaser, run their publishing job only for a tag (`if: startsWith(github.ref, 'refs/tags/…')`).

rules.text: A release is cut only from a commit whose tests passed: the release workflow runs the suite before it builds the installers, or a preflight job reads CI's result for the tagged commit and stops when it is not green.
rules.why: the build legs often skip the tests (`-DskipTests`), and a tag can be pushed on any commit, so without this a release can be cut from code whose checks failed or never ran.

check.text: in the release workflow, every job that publishes needs, directly or through the jobs between, a job that settles the tests on the tagged commit: it runs them (a Maven run that reaches the `test` phase, `./mvnw test`, `package`, `verify` or `install`, with no `-DskipTests` and no `-Dmaven.test.skip`, or a call to the full-tests workflow), or it reads the conclusion of the CI run on `GITHUB_SHA` and fails on anything but success.

rules.reference: both ways are in use, and all seven release workflows meet it. A preflight that reads CI: Editora's "Check that CI passed on this commit" step in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/release.yml) ([`scripts/release/CheckRelease.java`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/scripts/release/CheckRelease.java) `ci`, which waits up to 30 minutes for the required checks; its build legs run `-DskipTests`), and Torrenta's "Require CI on this commit" step in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/.github/workflows/release.yml), which reads the newest `ci.yml` run on the commit and starts one when there is none. The suite in the release: the template's `full-tests` job in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/.github/workflows/release.yml) calls `full-tests.yml` before `build`; the "Build, test and package" step of Termina's [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/.github/workflows/release.yml) and Mirada's [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/.github/workflows/release.yml) runs `./mvnw … verify` on every build leg; Modula's "Build the installer" step in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/.github/workflows/release.yml) runs `package` with the tests; nux's build legs run a "Test" step (`./mvnw test`) before they package, in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/.github/workflows/release.yml). In each of the five the job that publishes needs the build legs, directly or through the signing and asset-check jobs. Mirada's [`codecs.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/.github/workflows/codecs.yml) also creates a GitHub release, of the codec libraries its build downloads by checksum: that is a dependency, not a release of the app, and the app's own release runs the suite with them.

rules.text: Every workflow pins each third-party action to a commit SHA, with its version in a comment (`actions/setup-java@b843ebf… # v6.1.0`).

check.text: every `uses:` in `.github/workflows/`, and in a composite action under `.github/actions/` where the repository has one, ends in a 40-character SHA and a comment naming its version (`# v6.1.0`, `# 2.5.0`, `# v2`), never a branch such as `# main`. The `v2` in Editora's and Torrenta's `jreleaser/release-action … # v2` names that action's `v2` line, whose head the SHA is; the template, Termina and Mirada pin its 2.5.0 release.
check.command: [ -f pom.xml ] || { echo 'not an app root: no pom.xml here'; exit 1; }; [ -d .github/workflows ] || { echo 'no .github/workflows'; exit 1; }; ! grep -rhE '^[[:space:]]*-?[[:space:]]*uses:' .github/workflows .github/actions 2>/dev/null | grep -vE 'uses:[[:space:]]*\./' | grep -vE '@[0-9a-f]{40}[[:space:]]+#[[:space:]]*v?[0-9]'

rules.reference: Editora [`.github/workflows/`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/tree/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows).

rules.text: Dependabot updates `github-actions` and `maven` weekly.

check.text: `.github/dependabot.yml` lists both ecosystems with `interval: weekly`.

rules.reference: Editora [`.github/dependabot.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/dependabot.yml).

rules.text: Every workflow starts from `permissions: contents: read`, or from less; only a job that needs write access asks for it, in its own block.

check.text: each workflow has a top-level `permissions` that grants no write: `contents: read`, or less (`permissions: {}`); and every `write` sits in a job's own `permissions`.

rules.reference: Editora [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/release.yml): `release` (publish), `bump` (the pull request) and `preflight` (start a Full tests run). Modula's [`notify-catalog.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/.github/workflows/notify-catalog.yml) starts from `permissions: {}`.

rules.text: Every `actions/setup-java` step caches Maven's repository (`cache: maven`). The JDK it sets up is [PLAT-01](https://pauta-project.dev/6.0.1/platform/#plat-01)'s.

check.text: each `setup-java` step has `cache: maven`.

rules.reference: Mirada ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/.github/workflows/ci.yml)), Modula, nux and the app template ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/.github/workflows/ci.yml), [`full-tests.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/.github/workflows/full-tests.yml), [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/.github/workflows/release.yml)), on every step. Editora ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/ci.yml), [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/release.yml)), Termina and Torrenta each have a `setup-java` step without it. Editora sets up Temurin for its tests and Liberica for the release build, for linux-aarch64 coverage.

rules.text: Every job that runs steps has `timeout-minutes`. A job that calls a reusable workflow (`uses:` in place of `steps:`) takes no `timeout-minutes`: GitHub does not accept the key there, and the called workflow's own jobs carry theirs.

check.text: in every workflow, every job with `steps:` sets `timeout-minutes` on the job itself; a timeout on one of its steps does not stand for it. A job with `uses:` and no `steps:` is not judged.

rules.reference: every job of Editora's five workflows ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/ci.yml), [`full-tests.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/full-tests.yml), [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/release.yml) and the rest), of the template's three, Termina's two and Mirada's five sets one; the template's `full-tests` job in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/.github/workflows/release.yml), which calls `full-tests.yml`, carries none, as the rule says, and nor does the `winget` job of Mirada's [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/.github/workflows/release.yml), which calls `winget.yml`. Torrenta, Modula and nux don't yet: the two jobs of Torrenta's [`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/.github/workflows/ci.yml) and the one of its [`engine-soak.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/.github/workflows/engine-soak.yml) set none (its `release.yml` does); no job in Modula's three workflows ([`build.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/.github/workflows/build.yml), [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/.github/workflows/release.yml), [`notify-catalog.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/.github/workflows/notify-catalog.yml)) or in nux's two ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/.github/workflows/ci.yml), [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/.github/workflows/release.yml)) sets one: each app has it on one step only, the one that notarizes.

rules.text: Every workflow that runs on pull requests has a `concurrency` group that cancels a superseded pull-request run, and never a run on the default branch.

check.text: every workflow with a `pull_request` trigger has a `concurrency` block whose `group` is shared by the runs of one pull request and by no run on the default branch (keyed by `github.ref`, or by the pull request's number), and whose `cancel-in-progress` is true for a pull-request run: true, or an expression that is true there. And in that workflow `cancel-in-progress` is never true for a run on the default branch, whatever starts it (a push, a schedule, or a run started by hand, which `workflow_dispatch` allows on any branch): it is an expression that is false there, and it may be plain true only in a workflow that nothing can start on the default branch. A workflow with no `pull_request` trigger is not judged.

rules.reference: Editora [`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/ci.yml) and [`full-tests.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/full-tests.yml) (`cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}`, in a group keyed by the pull request's number). The template's ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/.github/workflows/ci.yml), [`full-tests.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/adl-desktop-app-template/blob/b5cbc21ce60b1e7aee0b8af224b0fa6d8c49e73f/.github/workflows/full-tests.yml)), Termina's ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Termina/blob/6de43a19b7185a25c01cdf506a6286719b1991ff/.github/workflows/ci.yml)) and Mirada's ([`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Mirada/blob/a3a84ec5e8227b1886e3dd920ab2b030aa3a2ba1/.github/workflows/ci.yml)) pull-request workflows use the same expression, Termina's and Mirada's in a group keyed by `github.ref`. Editora's third pull-request workflow, [`terminal-image.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/terminal-image.yml), doesn't yet: its `cancel-in-progress` is plain true, and beside pull requests and pushes to `probe/**` it can be started by hand, so a second run started on `master` cancels the first. Torrenta, Modula and nux don't either: Modula's [`build.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Modula/blob/518300a4c2114909315fbd3a73acc999fb4c16b5/.github/workflows/build.yml) and nux's [`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/nux/blob/d374ec4ee3f2eff0f7d378797884e6b81520ce20/.github/workflows/ci.yml) run on pull requests with no `concurrency` block, so they cancel nothing, and Torrenta's [`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/.github/workflows/ci.yml) sets `cancel-in-progress: true` for its pushes to `master` as well.

rules.text: A CI run leaves its results where they can be read without running it again: it uploads the surefire reports even when tests fail, uploads the JaCoCo report, and writes the coverage totals to the job summary.

check.text: the step that uploads the surefire reports runs under `if: always()`, a step uploads the JaCoCo report, and a step appends the coverage totals to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`.

rules.reference: Editora's "Upload test reports and coverage data" and "Summarise coverage" steps in [`ci.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/ci.yml).

rules.text: Signing skips cleanly when the secrets are absent (forks, dry runs), so they still build; a tag without them fails.

check.text: each signing step checks its secrets first, skips without them, and fails on a tag push.

rules.reference: Editora's "Import signing certificate (macOS)" step in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/Editora/blob/f314ca3b117829d25dbaa63be6ba2353fd898fd8/.github/workflows/release.yml) checks `MACOS_CERT_P12` first.

rules.text: The packaged app is launched once on each OS before a release (a smoke test).

check.text: the release workflow runs the packaged launcher on each OS (a Linux, a macOS and a Windows leg) before the step that publishes.

rules.reference: Torrenta's "Smoke-test the packaged app" step in [`release.yml`](https://github.com/adriandeleon/torrenta/blob/52d47c02ac57d8671d1e58d268b96a5532dbb00a/.github/workflows/release.yml) runs the launcher in the image of each of its three targets, one per OS. Editora runs only the notarized macOS app (`--version`, `--check-terminal`).
